Ek saaf baatOne thing, stated plainly

Yeh chheh kirdaar kaalpanik hain. Inki kahaniyan, inke numbers, inke trades — sab padhane ke liye banaye gaye hain, kisi asli vyakti ya asli track record se nahi liye gaye. Market ke numbers alag cheez hain — woh source aur date ke saath diye gaye hain, aur unhe aap khud verify kar sakte ho.

These six characters are fictional. Their stories, numbers and trades were written to teach, and are not drawn from any real person or track record. Market statistics are a different matter — each is given with its source and date, so you can verify it yourself.

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 1 Foundation · Chapter 1Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 1 Foundation · Chapter 1

Pehla ShareThe First Share

Aapka ₹100 jaata kahan hai? Order button dabane se lekar share aapke naam hone tak.

Where does your ₹100 actually go? From tapping the order button to the share landing in your name.

M1–2M1–2~35 min~35 min
1

Pehli salary, aur pehla jhatkaFirst salary, first reality check

Pune. Shanivaar shaam. Ek chhoti si chai ki tapri, teen log.

Pune. Saturday evening. A small tea stall, three people.

Arth

Rahul sir, pehli salary aa gayi. ₹38,000. Papa keh rahe hain FD kar do. Dost keh raha hai stock market mein daal. Aur mujhe dono mein se kuch samajh nahi aa raha.

Rahul sir, my first salary came in. ₹38,000. Dad says put it in an FD. A friend says put it in the stock market. And I don't really understand either one.

Tejas

Arre Arth, tension hi mat le yaar. Mere Telegram group mein ek script aayi hai — do din mein 20% pakka. Bas ₹20,000 daal de.

Come on Arth, don't overthink it. My Telegram group has a script — 20% in two days, guaranteed. Just put in ₹20,000.

Rahul Sir

Tejas. Ek sawaal. Arth jo ₹20,000 bhejega — woh paise jaayenge kahan?

Tejas. One question. The ₹20,000 Arth sends — where does that money go?

Tejas

Broker ke paas.

To the broker.

Rahul Sir

Aur broker ke paas se aage?

And from the broker, where next?

Tejas chai ka glass ghoomata rehta hai. Jawab nahi aata.

Tejas turns the tea glass in his hand. No answer comes.

Rahul Sir

Saat saal se trade kar rahe ho, Tejas. Aur aaj tak pata nahi ki paisa jaata kidhar hai. Isiliye har baar phas jaate ho.

Aur doosri baat — jo bhi tumse “pakka” bole, wahi sabse pehla red flag hai. Market mein “pakka” naam ka koi shabd hota hi nahi. Jo guarantee de raha hai, ya toh usne khud socha nahi, ya jaan-boojh kar jhooth bol raha hai. Teesra option hai hi nahi.

Seven years of trading, Tejas. And you still don't know where the money goes. That is exactly why you keep getting caught out.

And one more thing — anyone who says “guaranteed” is the first red flag you will ever meet. There is no such word in this market. A person promising a certain return either hasn't thought it through, or is lying deliberately. There is no third option.

Red flag — yeh line yaad rakhiyeRed flag — remember this line

“Pakka profit”, “guaranteed return”, “sure-shot”, “100% accuracy”, “loss nahi hoga” — in mein se ek bhi line koi sunaye, baat wahin khatam. Koi bhi SEBI-registered Research Analyst ya broker kaanooni taur pe return ki guarantee de hi nahi sakta. Jo de raha hai, woh registered nahi hai — ya rule tod raha hai.

SEBI registration ka matlab hai ki regulator ne us vyakti ko register kiya hai. Iska matlab yeh bilkul nahi hai ki return ki koi guarantee hai.

“Guaranteed profit”, “assured return”, “sure-shot”, “100% accuracy”, “no loss” — if anyone says any of these, the conversation is over. No SEBI-registered Research Analyst or broker is legally permitted to guarantee a return. Anyone who does is either not registered, or is breaking the rules.

SEBI registration means the regulator has registered that person. It does not mean any return is guaranteed.

2

Ramu ki tapri — share hota kya haiRamu's tea stall — what a share really is

Rahul Sir

Arth, yeh tapri Ramu ki hai. Achha chalta hai. Ab Ramu ko doosri dukaan kholni hai — ₹10 lakh chahiye. Do raaste hain.

Pehla — udhaar. Bank loan. Har mahine interest dena padega, dukaan chale ya na chale. Dukaan Ramu ki hi rahegi.

Doosra — hissedaar. Chaar dost, har ek ₹2.5 lakh. Ab har ek ka 25% hissa. Profit chaaron ka, loss bhi chaaron ka. Interest ki tension nahi.

Bas. Woh 25% wala kaagaz hi share hai. Company ka ek tukda. Aur kuch nahi.

Arth, this stall is Ramu's. It does well. Now he wants a second outlet — he needs ₹10 lakh. There are two routes.

One — borrow. A bank loan. Interest is due every month whether the shop does well or not. The shop stays entirely his.

Two — take partners. Four friends, ₹2.5 lakh each. Now each owns 25%. Profit splits four ways, so does loss, and there is no interest to service.

That's it. That 25% slip of paper is a share. A piece of the business. Nothing more mysterious.

Arth

Par sir, agar un chaar mein se ek ko achanak paisa chahiye ho? Dukaan toh todke nahi de sakte.

But sir, what if one of those four suddenly needs money? You can't break off a quarter of the shop and hand it over.

Rahul Sir

Bilkul sahi sawaal. Woh apna 25% kisi aur ko bech dega. Par ab do nayi dikkatein: ek — kharidaar milega kahan se? Do — ajnabi pe bharosa kaun karega?

Yeh dono hal karne ke liye hi stock exchange bana. Hazaaron kharidaar-bechne wale ek jagah, koi kisi ko jaanta nahi — phir bhi paisa aur share surakshit tarike se haath badal lete hain.

Exactly the right question. He sells his 25% to someone else. But that creates two problems: one — where does he find a buyer? Two — why would either side trust a stranger?

A stock exchange exists to solve exactly those two. Thousands of buyers and sellers in one place, none of them knowing each other — and money and shares still change hands safely.

Arth

Ruko. Matlab jab main share kharidta hoon… paisa company ko nahi jaata?

Wait. So when I buy a share… the money doesn't go to the company?

Rahul Sir

Nahi jaata. Ek rupaya bhi nahi. Company ko paisa sirf ek baar milta hai — jab woh pehli baar apne hisse bechti hai. Usko IPO kehte hain.

Uske baad share aapas mein ghoomte rehte hain. Company us lenden mein hoti hi nahi. Isiliye jo bazaar aap roz dekhte ho, woh secondary market hai.

It does not. Not one rupee. The company is paid only once — when it sells its shares for the first time. That's the IPO.

After that the shares just circulate. The company isn't part of those transactions at all. Which is why the market you watch every day is called the secondary market.

3

Rupaye ka peechha karoFollow the rupee

Rahul Sir

Ab asli cheez. Maan lo tumne ek share ka order laga diya — ₹100 ka. Do second mein “executed”. Un do second mein tumhara rupaya paanch jagah se guzarta hai. Har stop pe click karo.

Now the real thing. Say you place an order for one share — ₹100. Two seconds later, “executed”. In those two seconds your rupee passes through five places. Click each stop.

InteractiveInteractive

₹100 ka safar — kisi bhi stop pe click karoThe journey of ₹100 — click any stop

Stop 01 — AapStop 01 — You

Aap app kholke order lagate ho: kaunsa share, kitne, kis bhaav pe. Yahan ek cheez dhyaan mein — aapke paas do alag account hain. Trading account se order jaata hai, demat account mein share aake rukta hai.

You open the app and place an order: which share, how many, at what price. One thing to hold on to — you have two separate accounts. Orders go out from the trading account; shares come to rest in the demat account.

Sawaal khud se: aapke demat aur trading account ek hi jagah se khule hain, ya alag?

Ask yourself: were your demat and trading accounts opened at the same place, or separately?

Stop 02 — BrokerStop 02 — Broker

Broker teen kaam karta hai, do second se kam mein. Paisa hai ya nahi — check. Risk rules (limit, margin, ban) — apply. Order exchange tak — route. Broker aapka raasta hai. Na aapka paisa rakhta hai, na share.

The broker does three things in under two seconds. Checks you have the money. Applies risk rules (limits, margin, bans). Routes the order to the exchange. The broker is your route. It holds neither your money nor your shares.

Isiliye broker doobne se aapke share nahi doobte — woh wahan hain hi nahi.

Which is why a broker failing does not take your shares with it — they were never there.

Stop 03 — Exchange (NSE / BSE)Stop 03 — Exchange (NSE / BSE)

Matching engine har second laakhon order jodta hai — price-time priority pe. Pehle behtar bhaav, phir jo pehle aaya wo. Koi nahi jaanta doosri taraf kaun hai, aur jaanne ki zaroorat bhi nahi.

The matching engine pairs off hundreds of thousands of orders a second on price-time priority: better price first, then whoever arrived first. Nobody knows who is on the other side, and nobody needs to.

Yahi wajah hai ki bade aur chhote trader ko ek hi queue milti hai.

This is why a large trader and a small one stand in the same queue.

Stop 04 — Clearing Corporation (NCL / ICCL)Stop 04 — Clearing Corporation (NCL / ICCL)

Poore system ki sabse badi cheez, aur sabse kam samjhi jaane wali. Trade match hote hi clearing corporation beech mein aa jaata hai — kharidaar ke liye bechne wala wahi, bechne wale ke liye kharidaar bhi wahi. Naam: novation.

The biggest thing in the system and the least understood. The moment a trade matches, the clearing corporation steps into the middle — becoming the seller to the buyer and the buyer to the seller. It has a name: novation.

Nateeja: saamne wala mukar jaaye toh bhi aapka sauda poora hoga. Nuksaan clearing corporation ka, aapka nahi.

The result: if the other side defaults, your trade still completes. The loss is the clearing corporation's, not yours.

Stop 05 — Depository (NSDL / CDSL)Stop 05 — Depository (NSDL / CDSL)

Aakhri stop. Share aapke demat account mein aapke naam pe chadh jaate hain. India mein default settlement T+1 hai. Top 500 stocks mein T+0 (usi din) ka optional cycle bhi chalta hai, jise SEBI ne 31 January 2025 se phase-wise shuru kiya.

The last stop. Shares are credited to your demat account, in your own name. India's default settlement is T+1. An optional T+0 (same-day) cycle also runs on the top 500 stocks, which SEBI rolled out in phases from 31 January 2025.

Har mahine CAS aata hai — seedha depository se, broker se nahi. Wahi aapka asli record hai.

Your CAS arrives monthly — straight from the depository, not the broker. That is your real record.

4

Jab kuch tootta hai, bachata kaun haiWhen something breaks, who catches you

Arth

Aur agar broker hi doob gaya toh? Mere share toh uske paas hain na?

And if the broker itself goes under? My shares are sitting with them, aren't they?

Rahul Sir

Nahi hain. Aur yeh sabse zaroori line hai jo aaj tum sunoge.

Tumhare share depository mein — NSDL ya CDSL mein — tumhare apne naam pe hain. Broker sirf raasta hai, tijori nahi. Broker band ho jaaye toh share doosre broker mein transfer ho jaate hain.

Isiliye har mahine CAS seedha NSDL/CDSL se aata hai. Taaki tum broker ki app pe bharosa kiye bina khud check kar sako.

They are not. And this is the single most important sentence you will hear today.

Your shares sit in a depository — NSDL or CDSL — in your own name. The broker is a route, not a vault. If it shuts down, you move your holdings to another broker.

Which is why your CAS arrives monthly directly from NSDL/CDSL — so you can verify what you own without taking the broker's app on trust.

Vridhi

Yeh sirf theory nahi hai. 2019–20 mein ek bada broker clients ke share girvi rakh ke apne liye paisa utha raha tha. SEBI ne pakda, aur uske baad rules tight kar diye — power of attorney ki jagah margin pledge aaya, aur client ke share alag rakhna zaroori ho gaya.

Poora system isi tarah banta hai. Kuch tootta hai, phir band hota hai. Jo rule aaj bewajah lagta hai, woh kisi purane nuksaan ka nateeja hai.

This isn't theory. In 2019–20 a large broker was pledging client shares to raise money for itself. SEBI caught it, and tightened the rules afterwards — the margin pledge system replaced blanket power of attorney, and client securities must now be segregated.

The whole system gets built this way. Something breaks, then it gets closed. A rule that looks pointless today is almost always the scar tissue of an old loss.

Aaj hi kar loDo this todayEmail mein “CAS” search karo. NSDL ya CDSL ka statement milega. Usme jo holding likhi hai aur broker app mein jo dikh raha hai — dono match hone chahiye.Search your email for “CAS”. You'll find a statement from NSDL or CDSL. What it lists and what your broker app shows should match exactly.
Duniya bhar mein — naam alag, kaam wahiAround the world — different names, same job

Yeh dhaancha sirf India ka nahi. Har bade market mein yahi teen parat hain:

This structure isn't unique to India. Every major market has the same three layers:

  • India — SEBI · NSE Clearing / ICCL · NSDL & CDSL · Investor Protection Fund
  • USA — SEC · NSCC/DTCC · DTC · SIPC
  • UK — FCA · LCH · CREST/Euroclear UK · FSCS
  • India — SEBI · NSE Clearing / ICCL · NSDL & CDSL · Investor Protection Fund
  • USA — SEC · NSCC/DTCC · DTC · SIPC
  • UK — FCA · LCH · CREST/Euroclear UK · FSCS

Naam badalte hain, kaam wahi rehta hai. Ek baar yeh dhaancha samajh aa gaya, toh duniya ke kisi bhi market ka structure 10 minute mein padh loge.

The names change; the jobs don't. Once you have this, you can read the plumbing of any market in the world in about ten minutes.

5

Woh number jo sab kuch badal deta haiThe number that reframes everything

Arth

Sir yeh toh solid system hai. Toh phir log paisa haarte kyun hain?

Sir, this sounds like a solid system. So why do people lose money?

Vridhi

Kyunki system aapka paisa chori hone se bachata hai. Aapke apne faislon se nahi bacha sakta. Yeh SEBI ka apna data hai. Dhyaan se padho.

Because the system protects your money from being stolen. It cannot protect you from your own decisions. This is SEBI's own data. Read it carefully.

91%individual F&O traders ne FY25 mein net loss kiyaof individual F&O traders made a net loss in FY25
₹1.06 L crFY25 ka net loss (₹1,05,603 crore), costs ke baadnet loss in FY25 (₹1,05,603 crore), after costs
93%FY22–FY24 — kul ₹1.8 lakh crore se zyadaover FY22–FY24 — more than ₹1.8 lakh crore in total

Source: SEBI study on individual traders in the equity derivatives segment — FY25 figures published July 2025; FY22–FY24 from the SEBI press release, September 2024. Yeh aankde equity F&O segment ke hain — poore share bazaar ke nahi.Source: SEBI's study of individual traders in the equity derivatives segment — FY25 figures published July 2025; FY22–FY24 from the SEBI press release, September 2024. These figures cover the equity F&O segment — not the whole stock market.

Vridhi

Do baatein. Pehli — yeh number derivatives ka hai, poore market ka nahi, long-term investing ka nahi.

Doosri, aur yeh zyada important — naye log sabse pehle wahin jaate hain. Kyunki wahan chhote paise mein position ban jaati hai aur ek din mein double ya khatam ho sakti hai. Tejas bhi wahin gaya tha.

Two things. First — this number is about derivatives, not the whole market, and nothing to do with long-term investing.

Second, and this matters more — it is exactly where beginners go first. Because a small sum buys a position there, and it can double or vanish in a day. That is where Tejas went too.

Tejas

…haan. Main gaya tha.

…yes. I did.

Rahul Sir

Is course ki shuruaat yeh number se jaan-boojh kar ki gayi hai. Isliye nahi ki darana hai. Isliye ki jo shuru mein hi jaan leta hai ki haarna kitna aasaan hai, wahi hoshiyaari se khelta hai.

Aaj tumne ek bhi trade nahi kiya. Ek rupaya risk pe nahi lagaya. Aur phir bhi Tejas se aage nikal gaye — kyunki ab tumhe pata hai paisa jaata kahan hai.

This course opens on that number deliberately. Not to frighten you. Because the person who learns early how easy it is to lose is the one who plays carefully.

Today you placed no trades. You risked not one rupee. And you are still ahead of Tejas — because you now know where the money goes.

Chapter 1 · band karne se pehleChapter 1 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Share = company ka ek tukda. Ramu ki tapri ka 25% hissa. Bas usi ka kaagaz.

A share is a piece of a business. A 25% stake in Ramu's tea stall. That's all it is.

2

Roz ke bazaar mein company ko paisa nahi milta. Sirf IPO mein milta hai. Baaki har din ek investor doosre ko deta hai.

The company gets nothing from the daily market. It is paid only at the IPO. Every day after, one investor pays another.

3

Paisa paanch stop se guzarta hai — Aap, Broker, Exchange, Clearing Corporation, Depository.

The money passes five stops — You, Broker, Exchange, Clearing Corporation, Depository.

4

Clearing corporation beech mein aa jaata hai (novation). Saamne wala mukar bhi jaaye, aapko share milega hi.

The clearing corporation steps into the middle (novation). Even if the other side defaults, you still get your share.

5

Share broker ke paas nahi, depository mein aapke naam pe hain. Broker raasta hai, tijori nahi.

Your shares are not with the broker — they sit in a depository, in your name.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Broker chunte waqt. Ab aap poochoge: mere share kis depository mein jaayenge, CAS kis email pe aayega.
  • Jab koi “pakki khabar” de. Ek line se pata chal jaayega ki saamne wala serious hai ya nahi.
  • Jab app pe holding galat dikhe. Sach depository ke CAS mein likha hai, broker ki screen pe nahi.
  • Jab bhaav gire. Company ke paise nahi gaye — uski keemat ka andaza badla hai.
  • Kisi bhi desh ka market samajhne mein. Regulator, clearing house, depository — teen parat har jagah.
  • Choosing a broker. You'll now ask which depository your shares go to and which email the CAS lands on.
  • When someone offers a “sure thing”. One sentence tells you whether they're serious.
  • When your app shows the wrong holding. The truth is in the depository's CAS, not the broker's screen.
  • When the price falls. The company's cash didn't move — the estimate of its worth did.
  • Reading any country's market. Regulator, clearing house, depository — three layers everywhere.

Ghanti Se Ghanti TakBell to Bell

9:15 se 3:30. Order ke kitne type, kaunsa kab, aur circuit lagta kyun hai.

9:15 to 3:30. How many order types there are, when to use which, and why a circuit gets hit.

M3–4M3–4~35 min~35 min
1

Tejas ka ₹7 ka nuksaanTejas's ₹7 lesson

Agli subah. 9:14. Tejas phone pe, Arth dekh raha hai.

Next morning. 9:14. Tejas on his phone, Arth watching.

Tejas

Dekh, main abhi market order lagata hoon. Fatafat lag jaayega.

Watch, I'll place a market order now. Instant fill.

9:15:02. Order lag gaya. Tejas screen dekhta hai aur muh banata hai.

9:15:02. Filled. Tejas looks at the screen and winces.

Tejas

Arre? Maine ₹412 dekha tha, mila ₹419 pe. Saat rupaye upar!

What? I saw ₹412, it filled at ₹419. Seven rupees higher!

Rahul Sir

Market order ka matlab hai: “bhaav jo bhi ho, mujhe abhi chahiye.” Tumne bhaav ki nahi, speed ki demand ki thi. Speed mili. Bhaav gaya.

Aur 9:15 pe toh sabse bura waqt hai. Raat bhar ki saari khabar ek saath khul rahi hai. Bhaav abhi tay ho hi raha hai.

A market order says: “whatever the price, I want it now.” You demanded speed, not price. You got speed. You lost price.

And 9:15 is the worst moment for it. Every piece of overnight news is opening at once. The price is still being discovered.

Arth

Toh limit order behtar hai?

So a limit order is better?

Rahul Sir

Behtar nahi — alag. Limit order kehta hai: “mujhe ₹412 se upar nahi chahiye.” Bhaav pakka. Par fill pakka nahi. Bhaav wahan tak aaya hi nahi toh order pada rahega.

Har order type ek hi sawaal ka jawab hai: kya tumhe bhaav chahiye ya fill chahiye? Dono ek saath kabhi nahi milte.

Not better — different. A limit order says: “I won't pay above ₹412.” Price certain. Fill not certain. If the price never comes back, the order just sits there.

Every order type answers one question: do you want price, or do you want the fill? You never get both.

Order typeYeh guarantee karta haiYeh nahi kartaKab
MarketFillBhaavNikalna zaroori ho
LimitBhaav (ya behtar)FillEntry, patience ho
SL (stop-loss limit)Trigger pe limit orderGap mein fillNormal exit
SL-M (stop-loss market)Trigger pe nikalnaKis bhaav pe nikleNikalna sabse zaroori ho
AMOAgle din queue meinKuch bhi aurMarket band ho
Order typeThis it guaranteesThis it does notWhen
MarketThe fillThe priceYou must get out now
LimitThe price, or betterThe fillEntry, when you can wait
SL (stop-loss limit)A limit order at the triggerA fill through a gapA normal exit
SL-M (stop-loss market)Getting out at the triggerAt what price you get outWhen getting out matters most
AMOA place in tomorrow's queueAnything elseThe market is closed

SL aur SL-M ka farak sabse mehenga farak hai. Gap-down mein SL limit chhoot jaata hai aur aap position mein phase rehte ho; SL-M nikaal deta hai, chahe bura bhaav mile.The gap between SL and SL-M is the costliest distinction here. In a gap-down an SL limit can be skipped entirely and leave you still in the position; SL-M gets you out, however bad the fill.

2

Ek din ka nakshaThe anatomy of one day

Vridhi

Din ek jaisa nahi hota, Arth. Uske hisse hote hain, aur har hisse ka apna character hota hai. Main ek hi strategy poore din nahi chalati.

The day isn't uniform, Arth. It has parts, and each part has its own character. I don't run one strategy across all of it.

Vridhi

Pehla ghanta sabse zyada volume aur sabse zyada dhoka deta hai. Naye log wahin sabse zyada trade karte hain, aur wahin sabse zyada haarte hain.

Main pehle 15 minute mein kuch nahi karti. Sirf dekhti hoon. Mera pehla trade aksar 9:30 ke baad hota hai.

The first hour carries the most volume and the most deception. Beginners trade it most, and lose in it most.

I do nothing in the first fifteen minutes. I just watch. My first trade is usually after 9:30.

Arth

Aur circuit? Woh kya hai?

And circuits? What are those?

Rahul Sir

Circuit ek band hai jo bhaav pe laga hota hai — 2%, 5%, 10%, 20%. Us se aage us din bhaav ja hi nahi sakta. Exchange trading rok deta hai.

Upper circuit mein sirf kharidaar hain, bechne wala koi nahi. Lower circuit mein ulta — aur wahi sabse khatarnaak hai: aap nikalna chahte ho, par koi kharidne wala hi nahi hai.

Index pe bhi market-wide circuit hai — 10%, 15%, 20% pe poora market rukta hai. Woh saalon mein ek-do baar hi lagta hai.

A circuit is a band on the price — 2%, 5%, 10%, 20%. The price cannot move beyond it that day. The exchange halts trading.

In an upper circuit there are only buyers and no sellers. In a lower circuit the reverse — and that is the dangerous one: you want out, and there is nobody to sell to.

There is a market-wide circuit on the index too — the whole market halts at 10%, 15% and 20%. That fires once or twice in a decade.

Lower circuit — exit ka bhramThe lower circuit — the exit that isn't

Stop-loss lagaya hua hai iska matlab yeh nahi ki aap nikal jaoge. Stop-loss ek order hai, guarantee nahi. Lower circuit mein doosri taraf koi kharidaar hi nahi hota, toh aapka order queue mein khada rehta hai — bina fill ke, kabhi-kabhi kai din.

Isiliye liquidity koi boring detail nahi hai. Woh aapka exit hai. Jis share mein roz ka volume bahut kam hai, uska stop-loss kaagaz pe hi rehta hai.

Having a stop-loss does not mean you will get out. A stop-loss is an order, not a guarantee. In a lower circuit there is no buyer on the other side, so your order simply queues — unfilled, sometimes for days.

This is why liquidity is not a boring detail. Liquidity is your exit. In a share that trades thinly, your stop-loss lives only on paper.

3

Order book padhnaReading the order book

Rahul Sir

Aakhri cheez. Har share ka ek order book hota hai — ek taraf kharidaar (bid), doosri taraf bechne wale (ask). Beech ka farak spread hai.

Achhe share mein spread ek paisa hota hai. Kharaab share mein do rupaye. Woh do rupaye aapka nuksaan hain — trade karte hi, kuch hue bina.

Spread pehla kharcha hai jo koi bill mein nahi dikhata. Roz ka volume dekhna seekho, warna aapka backtest jhoot bolega.

One last thing. Every share has an order book — buyers on one side (the bid), sellers on the other (the ask). The gap between them is the spread.

In a good share the spread is one paisa. In a bad one it's two rupees. Those two rupees are your loss — the instant you trade, before anything happens.

The spread is the first cost nobody bills you for. Learn to check daily volume, or your backtest will lie to you.

Chapter 2 · band karne se pehleChapter 2 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Market order = fill pakka, bhaav nahi. Limit order = bhaav pakka, fill nahi. Dono ek saath kabhi nahi.

Market order = certain fill, uncertain price. Limit order = certain price, uncertain fill. Never both.

2

SL-M nikalta hai, SL nahi bhi nikal sakta. Gap mein SL limit chhoot jaata hai aur aap phase rehte ho.

SL-M gets you out; SL might not. In a gap the SL limit can be skipped and leave you in the position.

3

Din ke hisse hote hain. Pehla ghanta sabse tez aur sabse dhokebaaz. Pre-open 9:00–9:08 opening price banata hai.

The day has parts. The first hour is fastest and most deceptive. The pre-open (9:00–9:08) sets the opening price.

4

Lower circuit mein stop-loss kaam nahi karta. Kharidaar hi nahi hai. Liquidity hi aapka exit hai.

A stop-loss does not work in a lower circuit. There is no buyer. Liquidity is your exit.

5

Spread pehla kharcha hai. Bill mein nahi dikhta, par har trade mein lagta hai.

The spread is your first cost. It never appears on a bill, and it applies to every trade.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har order lagate waqt. Ek sawaal: mujhe bhaav chahiye ya fill? Uska jawab order type chun leta hai.
  • 9:15 pe. Ab aap samjhoge ki opening bhaav kal ke close se door kyun hai, aur pehle 15 minute kyun chhodne chahiye.
  • Naya stock chunte waqt. Roz ka volume aur spread dekh lo. Woh aapka exit hai, chahe entry kitni bhi achhi ho.
  • Jab position lower circuit mein ho. Panic nahi — aapko pehle se pata hoga ki order queue mein hai, fill nahi hua.
  • Every time you place an order. One question: do I want price or fill? The answer picks the order type.
  • At 9:15. You'll understand why the open sits far from yesterday's close, and why the first fifteen minutes are worth skipping.
  • Picking a new stock. Check daily volume and spread. That is your exit, however good the entry looks.
  • When a position hits a lower circuit. No panic — you'll already know the order is queued, not filled.

Bhaav Kyun Hilta HaiWhy a Price Moves

Result, promoter, FII-DII flow, sector rotation, global cues — aur index banta kaise hai.

Results, promoters, FII-DII flows, sector rotation, global cues — and how an index is actually built.

M5–6M5–6~35 min~35 min
1

“Achhi khabar aayi, phir bhi gir gaya”“Good news came out, and it still fell”

Tejas ki dukaan. Shaam. Result ka din tha.

Tejas's shop. Evening. It was a results day.

Tejas

Yeh samajh nahi aaya. Company ka profit 22% badha. Poori news mein aaya. Aur stock 6% gir gaya. Market pagal hai.

I don't get it. Profit up 22%. It was all over the news. And the stock fell 6%. The market is insane.

Rahul Sir

Market pagal nahi hai, Tejas. Market ne 28% expect kiya tha.

Bhaav khabar pe nahi hilta. Bhaav ummeed aur haqeeqat ke farak pe hilta hai. Result achha tha. Par jitna achha maana gaya tha, utna nahi tha. Bas yahi.

Isiliye toh kehte hain: “buy the rumour, sell the news”. Jab tak khabar aati hai, bhaav usko pehle hi pi chuka hota hai.

The market isn't insane, Tejas. The market had expected 28%.

A price doesn't move on news. It moves on the gap between what was expected and what arrived. The result was good. Just not as good as it had already been assumed to be.

Which is the whole of “buy the rumour, sell the news”. By the time the news lands, the price has usually already drunk it.

Arth

Toh bhaav ko hilata kaun hai asal mein?

So what actually moves a price?

Rahul Sir

Paanch cheezein, motey taur pe. Aur unki taakat alag-alag hoti hai.

Five things, broadly. And they do not pull with equal strength.

2

FII aur DII — do bade haathFII and DII — the two big hands

Vridhi

Indian market mein do bade khiladi hain. FII — foreign institutional investors. DII — domestic, matlab hamare mutual fund, insurance, pension.

Dono ka data exchange roz shaam ko free mein publish karta hai. Koi paid subscription nahi chahiye. Aur yeh number aksar us din ki poori kahani bata deta hai.

Ek cheez dhyaan mein rakhna: FII bechte hain aur DII kharidte hain — yeh normal hai. Yeh zaroori nahi ki market girega. Iska matlab sirf itna hai ki paisa ek jeb se doosri jeb mein ja raha hai.

There are two large players in this market. FIIs — foreign institutional investors. DIIs — domestic ones: our mutual funds, insurers, pension money.

Both are published free by the exchanges every evening. No paid subscription needed. And that number often explains the entire day.

One thing to hold on to: FIIs selling while DIIs buy is normal. It doesn't mean the market must fall. It means money is moving from one pocket to another.

Arth

Aur SIP? Woh isme kahan aata hai?

And SIPs? Where do they fit?

Vridhi

SIP hi DII ka sabse bada engine ban gaya hai. Har mahine ek fixed raqam, bina market dekhe, mutual funds mein chali jaati hai — aur woh paisa khareedna hi padta hai.

Isiliye pichhle kuch saalon mein jab FII ne bada bechaa, market utna nahi gira jitna pehle girta tha. Yeh dhaancha badal gaya hai.

SIPs have become the biggest single engine behind DII money. A fixed amount goes into mutual funds every month regardless of the market — and that money has to buy something.

Which is why in recent years heavy FII selling has not knocked the market down the way it once did. That structure has changed.

3

Index — ek bhaav mein 50 kahaniyanThe index — fifty stories in one number

Rahul Sir

Ab NIFTY. Log kehte hain “NIFTY 200 point upar”, jaise woh koi ek cheez ho. Woh ek cheez nahi hai — woh 50 companies ka weighted average hai.

Aur weighted ka matlab hai: sab barabar nahi hain. Free-float market cap ke hisaab se weight milta hai. Sabse badi companies index ko kheench sakti hain, chhoti nahi.

Isiliye NIFTY green ho sakta hai aur 30 stocks red ho sakte hain — agar top ke 5 chal rahe hain. Yeh dhoka roz hota hai.

Now NIFTY. People say “NIFTY is up 200 points” as if it were one thing. It isn't — it is a weighted average of 50 companies.

And weighted means they are not equal. Weight follows free-float market capitalisation. The largest companies can drag the index; the small ones cannot.

This is why NIFTY can be green while 30 of its stocks are red — if the top five are running. That illusion happens most days.

Arth

Toh index dekhke market ka haal pata hi nahi chalta?

So the index doesn't actually tell you how the market is doing?

Vridhi

Poora nahi chalta. Isiliye hum breadth dekhte hain — kitne stock upar, kitne neeche. Agar NIFTY upar hai par advance-decline kharaab hai, toh rally kamzor hai.

Aur free-float ka ek aur asar hai: jab index rebalance hota hai, index funds ko majboori mein kharidna ya bechna padta hai. Us din volume phat jaata hai, bina kisi news ke.

Not fully. Which is why we look at breadth — how many stocks advanced versus declined. NIFTY up with poor advance-decline is a weak rally.

Free-float has one more effect: on a rebalance, index funds are forced to buy or sell. Volume explodes that day with no news at all.

Breadth — sabse sasta sachBreadth — the cheapest truth available

Har shaam exchange advance-decline number deta hai — free. Agar index 1% upar hai aur sirf 600 stock advance kiye jabki 1,800 decline, toh woh rally paanch companies ki hai, market ki nahi.

Every evening the exchanges publish advances and declines — free. If the index is up 1% but 600 stocks advanced against 1,800 declined, that rally belongs to five companies, not to the market.

Rahul Sir

Aur aakhri cheez — raat. Jab aap so rahe hote ho, GIFT Nifty chal raha hota hai, US market khulta hai, crude hilta hai, dollar hilta hai. 9:15 ka gap wahin banta hai.

Isiliye overnight position rakhna ek alag khel hai. Aapka stop-loss raat mein kaam nahi karta. Market band hai. Aap sirf subah ka intezaar kar sakte ho.

And last — the night. While you sleep, GIFT Nifty is trading, the US market opens, crude moves, the dollar moves. The 9:15 gap is built there.

Which is why holding overnight is a different game. Your stop-loss does not work at night. The market is shut. You can only wait for morning.

Tejas

Yeh mujhe pata chal gaya tha. Mehenga pada tha.

I found that one out. It was expensive.

Chapter 3 · band karne se pehleChapter 3 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Bhaav khabar pe nahi, ummeed aur haqeeqat ke farak pe hilta hai. Achha result bhi gira sakta hai.

Price moves on the gap between expectation and reality, not on news. A good result can still take a stock down.

2

FII aur DII ka data roz free milta hai. FII bechein aur DII kharidein — yeh normal hai, crash ka signal nahi.

FII and DII data is published free daily. FIIs selling while DIIs buy is normal, not a crash signal.

3

NIFTY weighted average hai. Top 5 companies index ko green rakh sakti hain jabki 30 stock red hon.

NIFTY is a weighted average. The top five can hold it green while thirty of its stocks are red.

4

Breadth (advance-decline) rally ki sachchai batata hai. Aur woh bhi free hai.

Breadth (advances vs declines) tells you if a rally is real. Also free.

5

Raat mein aapka stop-loss kaam nahi karta. Gap wahin banta hai — GIFT Nifty, US market, crude, dollar.

Your stop-loss does not work overnight. The gap is built there — GIFT Nifty, the US session, crude, the dollar.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Result ke din. Aap pehle poochoge: market ne kya expect kiya tha? Number akela kuch nahi batata.
  • Shaam ko 5 minute. FII-DII aur advance-decline dekh lena — din ki kahani samajh aa jaayegi, bina kisi channel ke.
  • Jab koi kahe “market upar hai”. Aap poochoge: breadth kaisa tha? Aksar jawab nahi milega.
  • Overnight position lete waqt. Aapko pata hoga ki raat mein aapka stop kaam nahi karta, isliye size chhota rakhoge.
  • On a results day. You'll ask first: what had the market expected? The number alone says nothing.
  • Five minutes each evening. Check FII-DII and advances-declines — you'll understand the day without any TV channel.
  • When someone says “the market is up”. You'll ask how breadth was. Usually there's no answer.
  • Taking an overnight position. You'll know your stop is offline at night, so you'll size smaller.

Asli KharchaThe Real Cost

Brokerage, STT, exchange charge, GST, stamp duty, DP charge — poora stack. Aap apna cost calculator khud banaoge. Aur phir woh number jisse course shuru hua tha, dobara — is baar samajh ke.

Modules 7, 8 · ~35 min

Modules 7, 8 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 1 Foundation · Chapter 4Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 1 Foundation · Chapter 4

Asli KharchaThe Real Cost

Poora charge stack — aur aap apna cost calculator khud banaoge. Phir woh 91% wala number, samajh ke.

The whole charge stack — and you build your own cost calculator. Then that 91% figure, with the mechanics behind it.

M7–8M7–8~35 min~35 min
1

“Profit toh hua tha”“But I was in profit”

Tejas ka ledger, screen pe khula hua.

Tejas's ledger, open on screen.

Tejas

Sir, mahine bhar mein 38 trade kiye. Har trade mein chhota-chhota profit tha. Par account 4,200 rupaye kam hai. Ganit samajh nahi aa raha.

Sir, 38 trades this month. Small profit on most of them. But the account is ₹4,200 lighter. The arithmetic isn't working.

Rahul Sir

Ganit bilkul sahi hai, Tejas. Tum sirf aadha ganit kar rahe the.

Har trade pe saat alag-alag charge lagte hain. Unme se kuch dono taraf lagte hain, kuch sirf ek taraf. Tumne 38 trade kiye, matlab yeh stack 38 baar laga — aur zyadatar baar donon taraf.

Frequency hi sabse mehenga faisla hai jo ek retail trader leta hai. Strategy nahi. Frequency.

The arithmetic is perfectly correct. You were only doing half of it.

Every trade carries seven separate charges. Some apply on both sides, some on one. You did 38 trades, so that stack applied 38 times — mostly on both sides.

Frequency is the most expensive single decision a retail trader makes. Not the strategy. The frequency.

Rate yaad mat karo — source yaad rakhoDon't memorise rates — memorise the source

STT, exchange transaction charges aur stamp duty samay-samay pe badalte hain — October 2024 mein bhi badle the aur uske baad bhi. Jo rate aaj sahi hai, woh agle saal galat ho sakta hai.

Isiliye is course mein hum koi rate table yaad nahi karwate. Do jagah hamesha sahi rehti hain: aapke broker ka official charges page aur exchange ki apni levies page. Aur sabse sahi jagah teesri hai — aapka apna contract note, jo har trade ke baad aata hai aur jisme har charge alag line mein likha hota hai.

STT, exchange transaction charges and stamp duty change from time to time — they changed in October 2024 and again since. A rate that is right today can be wrong next year.

So this course does not hand you a rate table to memorise. Two places are always current: your broker's official charges page and the exchange's own levies page. The most accurate place is a third — your own contract note, which arrives after every trade with each charge on its own line.

2

Ganit jo sab badal deta haiThe arithmetic that changes everything

Vridhi

Ek cheez pakad lo, Arth. Round trip ka matlab hai do baar charge. Ek baar kharidte waqt, ek baar bechte waqt.

Ab maan lo aapke round trip ka total cost 0.5% hai. Aapko har trade mein 0.5% sirf barabar aane ke liye kamaana padega. Profit uske baad shuru hota hai.

Mahine mein 20 round trip kiye? 10% cost. Saal mein 240 trade matlab 120% cost — aapke poore capital se zyada. Strategy chahe kitni achhi ho, yeh ganit usse pehle maar deta hai.

Hold on to one thing, Arth. A round trip means the charges apply twice. Once buying, once selling.

Now say your round-trip cost is 0.5%. You have to make 0.5% on every trade just to break even. Profit starts after that.

Twenty round trips a month? 10% in costs. 240 trades a year is 120% in costs — more than your entire capital. However good the strategy, this arithmetic kills it first.

Arth

Iska matlab kam trade karna behtar hai?

So fewer trades is just better?

Vridhi

Iska matlab har trade ka expected profit cost se kaafi bada hona chahiye. Agar aapki strategy 0.3% kamaati hai aur cost 0.5% hai, toh woh strategy nahi — woh donation hai.

Main isiliye swing trade karti hoon, scalp nahi. Mera cost per trade wahi hai, par profit target kaafi bada hai.

It means each trade's expected profit must comfortably exceed the cost. If your strategy makes 0.3% and costs 0.5%, that's not a strategy — that's a donation.

That is why I swing trade rather than scalp. My cost per trade is the same; my profit target is far larger.

Trade styleRound trips / saalCost ka bojhHar trade se kya chahiye
Long-term investing1–4Bahut kamKuch bhi upar
Positional / swing20–60KamCost se 3–5 guna
Intraday250–500Bahut bhaariHar trade cost se kaafi upar
Scalping2,000+GhaatakRetail ke liye aksar namumkin
Trade styleRound trips a yearCost dragWhat each trade must clear
Long-term investing1–4Very lowAlmost anything positive
Positional / swing20–60Low3–5× the cost
Intraday250–500Very heavyWell clear of cost, every trade
Scalping2,000+Usually fatalUsually impossible at retail scale

Yeh table koi strategy recommend nahi karta. Yeh sirf yeh dikhata hai ki frequency badhne pe strategy se kya maanga jaata hai — aur woh maang tezi se badhti hai.This table recommends no strategy. It only shows what rising frequency demands of a strategy — and that demand rises fast.

3

Ab woh number dobaraThat number, again

Rahul Sir

Chapter 1 mein humne SEBI ka aankda dekha tha — FY25 mein 91% individual F&O traders ne net loss kiya, kul ₹1.06 lakh crore. Tab woh sirf ek number tha. Ab aapke paas uski mechanics hai.

Dhyaan se padho: woh number “transaction costs ke baad” hai. Matlab kuch log gross mein barabar the — aur cost ne unhe loss mein daal diya.

In Chapter 1 we saw SEBI's figure — 91% of individual F&O traders made a net loss in FY25, ₹1.06 lakh crore in total. Then it was just a number. Now you have its mechanics.

Read it carefully: that figure is “after transaction costs”. Which means some of those people were flat before costs — and costs pushed them into loss.

Arth

Toh sabne galat trade nahi kiya. Kuch log sirf kharche mein mare gaye?

So they weren't all trading badly. Some were simply killed by costs?

Rahul Sir

Bilkul. Aur yahi is chapter ka asli sabak hai. Cost koi detail nahi hai jo baad mein dekh lenge. Cost hi woh line hai jo profit aur loss ko alag karti hai.

Isiliye mera pehla rule hai: pehle kharcha, phir munafa. Koi bhi strategy tab tak strategy nahi hai jab tak uska cost ka hisaab na ho.

Exactly. And that is the real lesson here. Cost is not a detail to look at later. Cost is the line that separates profit from loss.

Which is my first rule: costs first, profit later. No idea is a strategy until its costs are counted.

Chapter 4 · band karne se pehleChapter 4 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Har trade pe saat parat ka charge stack lagta hai. Spread, brokerage, STT, exchange charge, SEBI fee, stamp duty, GST — plus delivery sell pe DP charge.

Seven layers of cost sit on every trade. Spread, brokerage, STT, exchange charge, SEBI fee, stamp duty, GST — plus a DP charge on a delivery sell.

2

Rates badalte rehte hain — structure nahi. Rate broker ke charges page, exchange ki levies page, aur apne contract note se lo.

Rates change; the structure doesn't. Take rates from your broker's charges page, the exchange's levies page, and your own contract note.

3

Round trip = do baar charge. Har trade ko sirf barabar aane ke liye poora round-trip cost kamaana padta hai.

A round trip charges you twice. Every trade must earn the full round-trip cost just to break even.

4

Frequency sabse mehenga faisla hai. Strategy se pehle frequency aapka P&L tay karti hai.

Frequency is the most expensive decision. It shapes your P&L before the strategy gets a say.

5

SEBI ka 91% wala aankda “costs ke baad” hai. Kuch log gross mein barabar the — cost ne unhe loss mein daala.

SEBI's 91% figure is “after transaction costs”. Some of those traders were flat before costs; costs made them losers.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Strategy banate waqt. Pehla sawaal: iska round-trip cost kitna hai, aur yeh strategy usse kitna upar kamaati hai?
  • Broker chunte waqt. Flat fee aur percentage ka farak aapke trade size pe nirbhar karta hai. Ab aap khud calculate kar paoge.
  • Har contract note pe. Aap use padhoge, ignore nahi karoge. Har line ka matlab pata hoga.
  • Jab koi “zero brokerage” bole. Aap poochoge: theek hai, par baaki chhe parat ka kya?
  • Backtest padhte waqt. Jis backtest mein cost nahi lagi, woh backtest nahi — woh ek kahani hai.
  • Designing a strategy. First question: what is the round-trip cost, and how far above it does this strategy earn?
  • Choosing a broker. Flat fee versus percentage depends on your trade size. You'll now be able to work it out yourself.
  • On every contract note. You'll read it instead of ignoring it, and know what each line means.
  • When someone says “zero brokerage”. You'll ask what happens to the other six layers.
  • Reading a backtest. A backtest without costs isn't a backtest — it's a story.

Freeze Aur FilterFreezes and Filters

ASM, GSM, trade-to-trade — stock freeze kyun hota hai. Aur automation ka poora raasta, naam lekar.

ASM, GSM, trade-to-trade — why a stock freezes. And the whole automation path, named up front.

M9–10M9–10~30 min~30 min
1

Jo stock bikta hi nahiThe stock that wouldn't sell

Tejas

Ek chhota stock liya tha. Ab bechne ja raha hoon toh broker keh raha hai 100% margin chahiye, aur intraday allowed nahi. Yeh kya bakwaas hai?

I bought a small stock. Now I try to sell and the broker says 100% margin, no intraday allowed. What is this nonsense?

Rahul Sir

Woh bakwaas nahi hai, Tejas. Woh ek surveillance framework hai, aur woh tumhare liye hi laga hai — chahe abhi bura lag raha ho.

Exchange aur SEBI aise stocks pe nazar rakhte hain jinme bhaav ya volume asaadharan tarike se hil raha ho. Jab kuch ajeeb lagta hai, woh stock ek list mein daal diya jaata hai.

Us list mein aate hi rules badal jaate hain: zyada margin, price band tight, kabhi-kabhi sirf delivery. Maqsad ek hi hai — jo log us stock mein phans sakte the, unki sankhya kam karna.

That is not nonsense. It is a surveillance framework, and it exists for you — however annoying it feels right now.

The exchanges and SEBI watch stocks whose price or volume is moving in unusual ways. When something looks off, the stock goes onto a list.

Once it's on that list the rules change: higher margin, tighter price bands, sometimes delivery only. The aim is single — to reduce how many people can get trapped in it.

FrameworkKis liyeAapke liye kya badalta hai
ASMAsaadharan bhaav ya volume ki harkatMargin badh jaata hai, price band tight, kabhi T2T
GSMKamzor fundamentals ke saath bada moveTrade sirf periodic call auction mein, bhaari margin
Trade-to-trade (T2T)Bahut zyada speculationIntraday band — delivery lena hi padega
Circuit / price bandEk din mein bahut bada moveUs band ke aage bhaav ja hi nahi sakta
FrameworkWhat it watches forWhat changes for you
ASMUnusual price or volume behaviourMargin rises, bands tighten, sometimes T2T
GSMBig moves with weak fundamentalsTrading only in periodic call auction, heavy margin
Trade-to-trade (T2T)Excessive speculationNo intraday — delivery is compulsory
Circuit / price bandToo large a move in one dayPrice cannot go beyond the band

Yeh chaaron alag cheezein hain aur ek saath bhi lag sakte hain. Dono exchange apni ASM/GSM list roz publish karte hain — free, bina login ke.These are four separate things and can apply together. Both exchanges publish their ASM/GSM lists daily — free, no login needed.

Position lene se pehleBefore you take a positionExchange ki ASM aur GSM list mein us stock ka naam check karo. Do minute ka kaam hai. Yeh check na karne ki keemat aksar poori position hoti hai.Check the stock against the exchange's ASM and GSM lists. It takes two minutes. The cost of skipping it is often the whole position.
2

Sirf naya nahi — bhaari bhiNot just new — heavy too

Vridhi

Ek cheez jo log samajhte nahi: ASM mein aane ka matlab yeh nahi ki company kharaab hai. Iska matlab hai ki us stock mein trading ka behaviour ajeeb hai. Company achhi bhi ho sakti hai.

Par aapke liye jo badalta hai woh practical hai — margin bhaari ho gaya, exit tang ho gaya, aur aapki position size ab kaam nahi karegi.

One thing people misread: an ASM listing does not mean the company is bad. It means the trading behaviour in that stock is unusual. The company may be perfectly fine.

But what changes for you is practical — margin got heavy, the exit got narrow, and your position size no longer works.

Arth

Toh main pehle se kaise bachun?

So how do I avoid it in advance?

Vridhi

Do aadatein. Ek — position lene se pehle list check karo. Do — roz ka average volume dekho. Jis stock mein roz ka volume kam hai, wahi stock aksar in liston mein aata hai, aur wahi stock aapko phansaata hai.

Mera apna rule: agar mera position size us stock ke roz ke average volume ka ek chhota hissa bhi paar karta hai, toh main woh trade leti hi nahi.

Two habits. One — check the lists before taking a position. Two — look at average daily volume. Thin stocks are the ones that end up on these lists, and they are the ones that trap you.

My own rule: if my position size is anything more than a small fraction of that stock's average daily volume, I don't take the trade at all.

3

Algo ki seedhi — pehle din naam lekarThe algo ladder — named on day one

Rahul Sir

Ab ek alag cheez, par isi chapter mein — kyunki aage ka poora raasta abhi saaf hona chahiye.

Is course mein automation teen dande ki seedhi hai. Aaj aap Level 0 pe ho. Aur aapko theek pata hoga ki agla danda kab kamaya.

Now something different, in the same chapter — because the whole road ahead should be clear now.

Automation in this course is a three-rung ladder. Today you are at Level 0. And you will know exactly when you have earned the next rung.

Level 2 ab kaanoon ke andar haiLevel 2 now sits inside the law

Auto-execution ab shauk ki baat nahi rahi. SEBI ka retail algo framework 1 April 2026 se poori tarah lागu hai. Uske under broker ke API se aane wale orders ke liye registered static IP chahiye, har algo order pe exchange ka Algo-ID chahiye, aur 10 orders per second ki threshold hai — usse upar jaane pe strategy exchange ke paas register karni padti hai.

Iska poora detail Chapter 25 mein aata hai. Abhi bas itna yaad rakhna: Level 2 ek regulatory danda hai, sirf technical nahi. Aur is course mein woh sabse aakhir mein aata hai — jaan-boojh kar.

Auto-execution is no longer a hobbyist matter. SEBI's retail algo framework applies in full from 1 April 2026. Under it, orders through a broker's API need a registered static IP, every algo order carries an exchange-issued Algo-ID, and there is a 10 orders-per-second threshold — above which the strategy must be registered with the exchange.

The detail comes in Chapter 25. For now, hold this: Level 2 is a regulatory rung, not just a technical one. And it comes last in this course — deliberately.

Arth

Toh Level 0 ka matlab hua — main abhi bhi khud trade karunga, par likhe hue rules se?

So Level 0 means I still trade by hand, but from written rules?

Rahul Sir

Haan. Aur yeh sabse zaroori danda hai. Jo rule aap likh nahi sakte, use aap automate bhi nahi kar sakte. Machine aapki soch tez karti hai — theek nahi karti.

Agar aapke rules mein confusion hai, toh Level 2 sirf usi confusion ko 100 guna speed pe chalayega. Aur woh bahut mehenga padta hai.

Yes. And it is the most important rung. A rule you cannot write down is a rule you cannot automate. A machine makes your thinking faster — not better.

If your rules are muddled, Level 2 simply runs that muddle a hundred times faster. And that gets expensive quickly.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

ASM, GSM aur T2T nazar rakhne ke framework hain. Stock us list mein aate hi margin, price band aur intraday ke rules badal jaate hain.

ASM, GSM and T2T are surveillance frameworks. Once a stock is listed, its margin, price bands and intraday rules change.

2

ASM mein hona company kharaab hone ka matlab nahi. Iska matlab us stock mein trading ka behaviour ajeeb hai.

An ASM listing doesn't mean the company is bad. It means the trading behaviour in that stock is unusual.

3

Position se pehle list check karna do minute ka kaam hai. Na karne ki keemat aksar poori position hoti hai.

Checking the lists before a position takes two minutes. Skipping it often costs the whole position.

Automation is a three-rung ladder — 0, 1, 2. You are at Level 0: written rules, run by hand.

5

Level 2 regulatory danda hai. SEBI ka retail algo framework 1 April 2026 se poori tarah lagu — static IP, Algo-ID, 10 orders/sec threshold.

Level 2 is a regulatory rung. SEBI's retail algo framework applies in full from 1 April 2026 — static IP, Algo-ID, a 10 orders/sec threshold.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Naya stock dekhte hi. ASM/GSM check — ek aadat, har baar, bina soche.
  • Jab margin achanak badh jaaye. Aap ghabraoge nahi. Aapko pata hoga ki stock kisi list mein aa gaya hai.
  • Position size tay karte waqt. Average daily volume dekhoge, sirf chart nahi.
  • Jab koi “algo bot” bech raha ho. Aap poochoge: Algo-ID hai? Static IP registered hai? Broker-routed hai?
  • The moment you look at a new stock. Check ASM/GSM — a habit, every time, without thinking.
  • When margin suddenly jumps. You won't panic. You'll know the stock has gone onto a list.
  • Setting position size. You'll look at average daily volume, not just the chart.
  • When someone sells you an “algo bot”. You'll ask: does it carry an Algo-ID? Is the static IP registered? Is it broker-routed?

Bina Paise Ke ShuruaatStarting With Zero Rupees

Practice account, journal template, aur pehle das observations. Foundation yahan poora hota hai.

A practice account, a journal template, and your first ten observations. Foundation ends here.

M11M11~25 min~25 min
1

Paanch hafte, ek bhi trade nahiFive weeks, not one trade

Arth

Sir, paanch hafte ho gaye. Maine ab tak ek bhi trade nahi kiya. Kya main pichhad raha hoon?

Sir, it's been five weeks. I haven't placed a single trade. Am I falling behind?

Rahul Sir

Pichhad rahe ho? Arth, tumne paanch hafte mein ek rupaya nahi haara. Tejas ne isi arse mein kitna haara, woh use bhi theek se nahi pata.

Is kaam mein na haarna bhi ek nateeja hai. Aur shuruaat mein woh sabse bada nateeja hai.

Falling behind? Arth, you haven't lost a rupee in five weeks. Tejas couldn't tell you precisely what he lost in the same period.

In this work, not losing is a result. And early on, it is the biggest one available.

Vridhi

Main tumhe apni shuruaat batati hoon. Maine pehle char mahine sirf likha. Koi paisa nahi. Roz shaam ko teen line: aaj maine kya dekha, mujhe kya lagta hai ki hoga, aur kal main check karunga ki hua ya nahi.

Char mahine baad mere paas 80 likhe hue observation the. Unme se 51 galat nikle. Woh 51 hi meri asli training thi.

Let me tell you how I started. I wrote for four months. No money. Three lines every evening: what I saw today, what I think happens next, and I check tomorrow whether it did.

After four months I had 80 written observations. 51 of them turned out wrong. Those 51 were my actual training.

Paper trading ka ek imaandaar ustaadOne honest caveat about paper trading

Paper trading ek cheez sikhaata hai bahut achhi tarah: mechanics. Order type, timing, rules ko follow karna, record rakhna. Yeh sab asli hota hai aur asli mein kaam aata hai.

Par woh ek cheez bilkul nahi sikhaata: apne asli paise ke saath baithne ka ehsaas. Jab ₹800 ka asli nuksaan screen pe dikhta hai, toh dimaag wahi nahi rehta jo paper pe tha. Isiliye paper se live jaate waqt sabse chhota size lena padta hai — dobara se seekhne ke liye, is baar bhavnaon ke saath.

Paper trading teaches one thing extremely well: the mechanics. Order types, timing, following your rules, keeping records. All of that is real and transfers.

What it does not teach at all is what it feels like to have your own money in the trade. An ₹800 real loss on screen does not meet the same brain that was calm on paper. Which is why the step from paper to live starts at the smallest size available — you are learning it again, this time with the emotions attached.

2

Journal — aath column, aur basThe journal — eight columns, no more

Vridhi

Log journal isliye chhod dete hain kyunki woh use bahut bada bana lete hain. Mera aath column ka hai, aur woh maine nau saal se nahi badla.

Sabse zaroori column aakhri wala hai — “kya maine apne rule follow kiye?” Sirf haan ya nahi. Profit ya loss se koi lena-dena nahi.

Rule follow karke haarna achha trade hai. Rule tod ke jeetna bura trade hai. Jo log yeh ulta samajhte hain, woh do saal mein khatam ho jaate hain.

People abandon journals because they build them too big. Mine has eight columns, and I haven't changed it in nine years.

The most important column is the last one — “did I follow my rules?” Just yes or no. It has nothing to do with whether the trade made money.

A loss that followed your rules is a good trade. A win that broke them is a bad trade. People who have that backwards are finished within two years.

ColumnKya likhna haiKyun
1. Date & timeEntry ka exact waqtDin ka kaunsa hissa kaam karta hai
2. InstrumentKya trade kiyaKahan edge hai, kahan nahi
3. Setup ka naamKaunsa likha hua ruleBina naam ke setup = koi rule nahi
4. Entry, SL, targetTeeno, entry se pehleBaad mein likha = bahana
5. Size aur risk ₹Kitne rupaye risk pe% nahi, rupaye. Rupaye chubhte hain
6. Exit aur RNikle kahan, kitne RR hi asli paimana hai
7. BhavnaEk shabd: shaant, jaldi, dar, lalachPattern yahin milta hai
8. Rule follow kiya?Sirf HAAN ya NAHIYahi ek column aapko bachaata hai
ColumnWhat goes in itWhy
1. Date & timeExact time of entryWhich part of the day works for you
2. InstrumentWhat you tradedWhere your edge is and isn't
3. Setup nameWhich written ruleAn unnamed setup means no rule
4. Entry, SL, targetAll three, before entryWritten after = an excuse
5. Size and risk in ₹How many rupees at riskNot %, rupees. Rupees sting
6. Exit and RWhere you exited, in RR is the real unit
7. EmotionOne word: calm, rushed, afraid, greedyThis is where the pattern hides
8. Followed the rules?Just YES or NOThis single column saves you

Aath column. Na nau, na saat. Bada journal woh journal hai jo teen hafte mein band ho jaata hai.Eight columns. Not nine, not seven. A bigger journal is a journal that gets abandoned in three weeks.

3

Foundation poora huaFoundation is complete

Rahul Sir

Arth, aaj Foundation khatam hota hai. Dekho tumne kya kamaya hai.

Tumhe pata hai ki share kya hai aur paisa kahan jaata hai. Tumhe pata hai ki order kaise lagta hai aur kaunsa kab. Tumhe pata hai bhaav kyun hilta hai. Tumhe poora cost stack pata hai aur tumne apna calculator banaya hai. Tumhe pata hai stock kab freeze hota hai.

Aur sabse zaroori — tumne abhi tak ek rupaya risk pe nahi lagaya. Zyadatar log yeh sab tab seekhte hain jab paisa ja chuka hota hai. Tumne pehle seekh liya.

Arth, Foundation ends today. Look at what you've earned.

You know what a share is and where the money goes. You know how an order works and which one to use. You know why a price moves. You know the whole cost stack and you've built your own calculator. You know when a stock freezes.

And most important — you have not risked a single rupee. Most people learn all of this after the money is gone. You learned it first.

Arth

Ab Level 2 mein kya aayega?

So what comes in Level 2?

Rahul Sir

Ab strategy. Chart, structure, indicators — aur teen poori likhi hui strategies jo tum chala sakoge. Saath mein woh risk wrapper jo tumhe itna zinda rakhta hai ki tum unhe chala sako.

Par ek shart. Journal roz bharna hai. Bina journal ke Level 2 ka koi matlab nahi.

Now strategy. Charts, structure, indicators — and three complete written strategies you can actually run. Along with the risk wrapper that keeps you alive long enough to run them.

On one condition. The journal gets filled every day. Without it, Level 2 means nothing.

1

Na haarna bhi ek nateeja hai. Shuruaat mein woh sabse bada nateeja hai jo mil sakta hai.

Not losing is a result. Early on, it is the biggest one available.

2

Paper trading mechanics sikhaata hai, bhavnaayein nahi. Isiliye live jaate waqt sabse chhota size — dobara seekhne ke liye.

Paper trading teaches mechanics, not emotion. Which is why going live starts at the smallest size — you're learning it again.

Journal aath column ka hai. Bada journal woh hota hai jo teen hafte mein band ho jaata hai.

The journal has eight columns. A bigger one is a journal that gets abandoned in three weeks.

The last column matters most: “did I follow my rules?” Just yes or no.

5

A loss that followed the rules is a good trade; a win that broke them is a bad one.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har shaam paanch minute. Journal bharna — chahe us din trade kiya ho ya nahi.

  • Jab koi trade ke baare mein poochhe. Aap R mein jawab doge, rupaye mein nahi. Wahi bhasha hai.
  • Mahine ke aakhir mein. Column 8 gino: kitne trade mein rule toota? Wahi aapka asli score hai.
  • Five minutes each evening. Fill the journal — whether or not you traded that day.
  • On your first real trade. The smallest size, because you know paper and live meet different brains.
  • When someone asks about a trade. You'll answer in R, not rupees. That's the language.
  • At month end. Count column 8: in how many trades did you break a rule? That is your actual score.

Modules 12, 13 · ~35 min

Modules 12, 13 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 7Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 7

Chart Jo Bolte HainCharts That Say Something

Candlestick, timeframe, volume — aur utna hi time is baat pe ki chart kya nahi bata sakta.

Candlesticks, timeframes, volume — and equal time on what a chart cannot tell you.

M12–13M12–13~35 min~35 min
1

Ek candle kya kehti haiWhat one candle says

Rahul Sir

Arth, ek candle chaar number dikhati hai: open, high, low, close. Bas. Woh bhavishya nahi batati — woh ek arse ka record hai.

Par uska aakaar ek cheez zaroor batata hai: us arse mein kharidaar aur bechne wale ke beech kya hua. Lambi wick ka matlab hai bhaav wahan gaya, par tika nahi — kisi ne use wapas dhakel diya.

Isiliye candle ke naam yaad karna bekaar hai. Naam yaad karne ki jagah yeh poochho: is candle mein kaun haara?

Arth, one candle shows four numbers: open, high, low, close. That's all. It doesn't predict — it is a record of a period.

But its shape does tell you one thing: what happened between buyers and sellers in that period. A long wick means price went there and could not stay — someone pushed it back.

Which is why memorising candle names is useless. Instead of the name, ask: who lost inside this candle?

Tejas

Par sir, main toh 30 pattern yaad kiye baitha hoon. Hammer, doji, engulfing, three black crows…

But sir, I've memorised thirty patterns. Hammer, doji, engulfing, three black crows…

Rahul Sir

Aur unme se kitne pe tumne kabhi ginti ki hai ki woh kitni baar sahi nikle?

And on how many of them have you ever counted how often they actually worked?

Tejas kuch nahi bolta.

Tejas says nothing.

Rahul Sir

Yahi farak hai. Pattern pehchanna aasaan hai. Pattern ki hit rate nikalna mushkil hai — aur sirf wahi kaam ka hai.

That is the difference. Recognising a pattern is easy. Measuring its hit rate is hard — and only the measurement is worth anything.

Chart kya nahi bata saktaWhat a chart cannot tell you

Chart aapko yeh nahi batata: company ka business kaisa chal raha hai; promoter ne share girvi rakhe hain ya nahi; kal result kya aayega; koi bada order book mein chhupa hai ya nahi; ya us bhaav ke peeche wajah kya thi.

Chart ek hi cheez batata hai: abhi tak kya hua. Woh bahut kaam ki cheez hai — par woh bhavishya ka nakshaa nahi hai. Jo log chart ko bhavishya maan lete hain, woh har galat signal pe hairaan hote hain.

A chart does not tell you: how the business is doing; whether the promoter has pledged shares; what tomorrow's results will say; whether a large order is hidden in the book; or the reason behind any move.

A chart tells you one thing: what has happened so far. That is genuinely useful — but it is not a map of the future. People who treat it as one are surprised by every false signal.

2

Timeframe — ek hi chart, teen jawabTimeframe — one chart, three answers

Vridhi

Ek hi stock ka 5-minute chart, daily chart aur weekly chart teen alag kahaniyan bolte hain. Teeno sach hain.

Naye log yahin phaste hain: daily pe trade lete hain, phir 5-minute pe dar ke nikal jaate hain. Aapka stop-loss aur aapka chart ek hi timeframe pe hone chahiye.

Mera rule simple hai. Jis timeframe pe main entry leti hoon, usi pe exit ka faisla hota hai. Chhoti timeframe sirf entry ka timing sudhaarne ke liye — faisla badalne ke liye nahi.

The 5-minute, the daily and the weekly of the same stock tell three different stories. All three are true.

This is where beginners get caught: they enter on the daily, then panic out on the 5-minute. Your stop and your chart must live on the same timeframe.

My rule is simple. The timeframe I enter on is the timeframe I decide the exit on. A smaller one is only for sharpening the entry — never for changing the decision.

TimeframeKya dikhata haiShor kitnaKiske liye
1–5 minAaj ki hulchalBahut zyadaIntraday, poore dhyaan ke saath
15–60 minDin ka dhaanchaTheek-thaakIntraday aur positional entry
DailyAsli trendKamSwing — zyadatar log yahin
WeeklyBada raastaBahut kamPositional aur investing
TimeframeWhat it showsHow noisyWho it suits
1–5 minToday's churnVery highIntraday, with full attention
15–60 minThe day's structureModerateIntraday and positional entries
DailyThe real trendLowSwing — where most people belong
WeeklyThe larger roadVery lowPositional and investing

Zyadatar retail traders ko daily chart chahiye hota hai aur woh 5-minute pe baithe rehte hain. Ulta kabhi nahi hota — aur yeh sabse aam galti hai.Most retail traders need the daily and sit on the 5-minute. It is never the other way round — and it is the most common mistake there is.

3

Support aur resistance — line nahi, zoneSupport and resistance — zones, not lines

Arth

Sir maine support pe kharida tha, aur bhaav do rupaye neeche chala gaya. Phir wapas upar. Mera SL lag gaya aur trade chala gaya.

Sir, I bought at support and price went two rupees below it. Then came back up. My stop was hit and the trade left without me.

Rahul Sir

Kyunki tumne support ko ek line maana. Woh line nahi hai. Woh ek zone hai — ek patti jahan pehle kharidaar aaye the.

Line ek exact number hai. Zone ek ilaaka hai. Market ko aapke exact number ki koi khabar nahi hai. Woh us ilaake mein kaam karta hai, uske ek point pe nahi.

Isiliye stop zone ke neeche lagta hai, zone pe nahi. Aur isiliye zone jitna purana aur jitni baar test hua ho, utna wazan rakhta hai — par har test uski taakat thodi kam bhi karta hai.

Because you treated support as a line. It isn't one. It is a zone — a band where buyers turned up before.

A line is an exact number. A zone is an area. The market has no idea about your exact number. It works in that area, not at one point in it.

So the stop goes below the zone, not on it. And the older a zone is and the more often it has been tested, the more weight it carries — though every test also wears it down a little.

Vridhi

Aur ek cheez. Toota hua resistance aksar support ban jaata hai. Kyunki jo log wahan phanse the, unka nuksaan ab munafa ban gaya — aur ab woh us bhaav pe bechte nahi, kharidte hain.

Chart pe har line ke peeche ek insaan ka faisla hai. Jab aap yeh samajh jaate ho, toh chart yaad karne ki cheez nahi rehti — padhne ki cheez ban jaati hai.

One more thing. Broken resistance often becomes support. Because the people trapped there are now in profit — and at that price they no longer sell, they buy.

Behind every line on a chart is a human decision. Once you see that, a chart stops being something to memorise and becomes something to read.

Chapter 7 · band karne se pehleChapter 7 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Candle ek record hai, bhavishyavani nahi. Naam yaad karne ki jagah poochho: is candle mein kaun haara?

A candle is a record, not a prediction. Instead of the name, ask who lost inside it.

2

Pattern pehchanna aasaan, hit rate naapna mushkil. Sirf naapa hua pattern kaam ka hai.

Spotting a pattern is easy; measuring its hit rate is hard. Only the measured one is worth anything.

3

Chart sirf yeh batata hai ki ab tak kya hua. Business, promoter, result — kuch nahi.

A chart tells you only what has happened. Not the business, the promoter, or the results.

4

Entry aur exit ek hi timeframe pe. Daily pe trade lekar 5-minute pe darr jaana sabse aam galti hai.

Enter and exit on the same timeframe. Entering on the daily and panicking on the 5-minute is the commonest error.

5

Support-resistance zone hain, line nahi. Stop zone ke neeche lagta hai, zone pe nahi.

Support and resistance are zones, not lines. The stop goes below the zone, not on it.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Chart kholte hi. Pehle timeframe tay karo, phir dekho. Ulta karne se aap wahi timeframe chun lete ho jo aapko pasand aata hai.
  • Support-resistance kheenchte waqt. Do line kheencho, ek nahi — upar aur neeche. Beech ka hissa hi zone hai.
  • Jab koi pattern bataye. Aap poochoge: aapne yeh kitni baar test kiya aur kitni baar chala?
  • Jab SL lagne ke baad bhaav wapas aa jaaye. Ab aapko pata hoga ki galti stop ki jagah mein thi, market mein nahi.
  • Every time you open a chart. Decide the timeframe first, then look. The other way round, you pick the timeframe that flatters you.
  • Drawing support and resistance. Draw two lines, not one — an upper and a lower. The space between is the zone.
  • When someone shows you a pattern. You'll ask how many times they tested it and how often it worked.
  • When a stop is hit and price comes right back. You'll know the error was in the stop's placement, not the market.

Indicator Ka SachThe Truth About Indicators

EMA, RSI, ATR, VWAP — har ek ka: kya calculate karta hai, kitna lag karta hai, aur kis tarah jhooth bolta hai. Aur phir aapki pehli poori strategy: Opening Range Breakout.

EMA, RSI, ATR, VWAP — for each: what it computes, how much it lags, and the specific way it lies. Then your first complete strategy: the Opening Range Breakout.

Modules 14, 15 · ~40 min

Modules 14, 15 · ~40 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 8Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 8

Indicator Ka SachThe Truth About Indicators

EMA, RSI, ATR, VWAP — kya naapte hain, kitna lag karte hain, kaise jhooth bolte hain. Plus Strategy #1.

EMA, RSI, ATR, VWAP — what they measure, how they lag, how they lie. Plus Strategy #1.

M14–15M14–15~40 min~40 min
1

Indicator kuch naya nahi jaantaAn indicator knows nothing new

Tejas

Maine 6 indicator laga rakhe hain. Jab saare green hon tabhi kharidta hoon. Phir bhi kaam nahi karta.

I've got six indicators up. I only buy when they're all green. It still doesn't work.

Rahul Sir

Kyunki chhe ke chhe ek hi data se bane hain — bhaav aur volume. Woh chhe raay nahi hain. Woh ek hi raay chhe tarike se likhi hui hai.

Koi bhi indicator koi nayi jaankari nahi deta. Woh sirf purani jaankari ko dobara pack karta hai. Uska faayda yeh hai ki woh use aankhon ke liye aasaan bana deta hai.

Aur har repack ki ek keemat hai: lag. Har indicator peeche chalta hai. Ismein kuch galat nahi — par jo aadmi yeh bhool jaata hai, woh har turn pe late hota hai.

Because all six are built from the same data — price and volume. They are not six opinions. They are one opinion written six ways.

No indicator adds information. It repackages information you already had. Its value is that it makes that information easier for your eye.

And every repack has a price: lag. Every indicator trails. Nothing wrong with that — but whoever forgets it is late at every turn.

IndicatorKya naapta haiKaise jhooth bolta haiKab kaam ka
EMAAverage bhaav, naye ko zyada wazanSideways market mein baar-baar crossoverTrend hone pe, direction ke liye
RSIRecent upar-neeche ka anupaatStrong trend mein hafton tak “overbought” dikhata haiRange mein, ya divergence ke liye
ATRRoz ki aam hulchalDisha bilkul nahi batataStop aur size tay karne ke liye
VWAPVolume se weighted aaj ka averageSirf aaj ka — agle din resetIntraday, reference ke liye
IndicatorWhat it measuresHow it liesWhen it earns its place
EMAAverage price, weighted to the recentEndless crossovers in a rangeIn a trend, for direction
RSIRatio of recent up to down movesReads “overbought” for weeks in a strong trendIn a range, or for divergence
ATRTypical daily movementSays nothing at all about directionFor placing stops and sizing
VWAPToday's volume-weighted averageOnly today's — it resets tomorrowIntraday, as a reference

Dhyaan do: ATR disha nahi batata. Zyadatar log use entry ke liye dhoondte hain — woh uska kaam hai hi nahi. ATR aapko batata hai ki stop kitna door hona chahiye.Note ATR says nothing about direction. Most people look to it for entries — that is not its job. ATR tells you how far away the stop belongs.

2

ATR — sabse kam bola gaya indicatorATR — the least discussed of them

Vridhi

Mera sabse zyada istemaal hone wala indicator ATR hai, aur woh mujhe kabhi entry nahi deta.

Ek stock roz ₹8 hilta hai, doosra ₹42. Dono pe ₹10 ka stop lagana bewakoofi hai. Pehle mein aap har roz nikal jaoge, doosre mein aapka stop bemaani hai.

Stop bhaav se nahi, us stock ki apni hulchal se tay hota hai. Isiliye mera stop hamesha ATR ke multiple mein hota hai, rupaye ke round number mein nahi.

My most-used indicator is ATR, and it has never once given me an entry.

One stock moves ₹8 a day, another ₹42. A ₹10 stop on both is nonsense. On the first you're stopped out daily; on the second the stop is meaningless.

A stop is set by the stock's own movement, not by the price. So my stop is always a multiple of ATR, never a round rupee figure.

Arth

Aur position size?

And position size?

Vridhi

Wahi se aata hai. Stop ki doori pata chal gayi, risk ki raqam pata hai — toh size ek division ban jaata hai. Chapter 10 mein poora karenge.

It follows from the same place. Once you know the stop distance and the rupees you'll risk, size is a division. We do it fully in Chapter 10.

3

Strategy #1 — Opening Range BreakoutStrategy #1 — the Opening Range Breakout

Rahul Sir

Ab aapki pehli poori strategy. Poori ka matlab hai: har condition likhi hui, har branch likhi hui, har exit likha hua. Do log ise padh ke bilkul ek jaisa chala sakein — tabhi woh strategy hai.

Idea simple hai. Din ke pehle kuch minute mein bhaav ek range banata hai. Us range ke bahar nikalna ek signal hai — kyunki din ka pehla faisla ho chuka hai.

Now your first complete strategy. Complete means: every condition written, every branch written, every exit written. Two people should read it and run it identically — only then is it a strategy.

The idea is simple. In the first few minutes of the day, price builds a range. Leaving that range is a signal — because the day's first decision has been made.

“Kab nahi” wala step sabse zaroori haiThe “when not to” step matters most

Har strategy mein entry ke rules hote hain. Bahut kam strategies mein na khelne ke rules hote hain — aur wahi rules zyadatar paisa bachate hain.

ORB ka sabse bada dushman ek aisa din hai jahan range bahut tight ho: tab har breakout jhootha nikalta hai aur aap din bhar aage-peeche kat te ho. Isiliye step 2 ka filter entry rule se zyada keemti hai.

Every strategy has entry rules. Very few have rules for not playing — and those are the rules that save most of the money.

ORB's worst enemy is a day with a very tight range: every breakout is false and you get chopped up all day. Which makes the step-2 filter more valuable than the entry rule.

Chapter 8 · band karne se pehleChapter 8 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Indicator koi nayi jaankari nahi deta. Woh bhaav aur volume ko dobara pack karta hai — aankhon ke liye aasaan banake.

An indicator adds no information. It repackages price and volume — making them easier for your eye.

2

Chhe indicator ek hi raay ke chhe roop hain. Woh ek doosre ki tasdeek nahi karte.

Six indicators are six versions of one opinion. They do not confirm each other.

3

ATR disha nahi batata. Woh batata hai ki stop kitna door hona chahiye — aur wahi se size nikalta hai.

ATR says nothing about direction. It tells you how far the stop belongs — and size follows from that.

4

Strategy woh hai jise do log ek jaisa chala sakein. Har condition, har branch, har exit likha hua.

A strategy is one two people can run identically. Every condition, branch and exit written down.

5

“Kab nahi khelna” ke rules sabse zyada paisa bachate hain. Entry rules se zyada.

The “when not to play” rules save the most money. More than the entry rules.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Chart pe indicator lagate waqt. Ek sawaal: yeh mujhe kya bata raha hai jo bhaav khud nahi bata raha?
  • Stop lagate waqt. Round number chhod do. ATR ka multiple lo — stock ki apni hulchal ke hisaab se.
  • Jab strong trend mein RSI 75 dikhaye. Aap ulta trade nahi karoge. Aapko pata hai ki trend mein RSI hafton tak wahan reh sakta hai.
  • Koi bhi strategy likhte waqt. “Kab nahi khelna” ka section zaroor likhoge — kyunki wahi bachaata hai.
  • Adding an indicator to a chart. One question: what does this tell me that price alone doesn't?
  • Placing a stop. Drop the round number. Use a multiple of ATR — the stock's own movement.
  • When RSI reads 75 in a strong trend. You won't fade it. You know RSI can sit there for weeks in a trend.
  • Writing any strategy. You'll always write the “when not to play” section — because that's the part that saves you.
