Do Aur StrategyTwo More Strategies

Strategy #2 — EMA pullback swing, multi-day holds aur gap ka risk. Strategy #3 — VWAP mean reversion, aur woh trending din jo use tabah kar dete hain.

Strategy #2 — the EMA pullback swing, multi-day holds and gap risk. Strategy #3 — VWAP mean reversion, and the trending days that destroy it.

Modules 16, 17 · ~40 min

Modules 16, 17 · ~40 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 9Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 9

Do Aur StrategyTwo More Strategies

EMA pullback swing — multi-day hold aur gap ka risk. VWAP mean reversion — aur jo din use maar dete hain.

The EMA pullback swing — multi-day holds and gap risk. VWAP mean reversion — and the days that kill it.

M16–17M16–17~40 min~40 min
1

Breakout ke peeche mat bhaagoStop chasing the breakout

Vridhi

ORB intraday hai. Ab ek positional strategy, jo mere apne trading ka aadha hissa hai.

Idea ulta hai. Breakout pe kharidne ki jagah, aap trend ke thakne ka intezaar karte ho. Trend upar hai, bhaav thoda peeche aata hai, phir aage badhta hai — us peeche aane pe entry.

Breakout pe aapka stop door hota hai. Pullback pe paas. Wahi poora farak hai — kyunki stop paas hai toh usi risk mein aap bada size le sakte ho, ya usi size mein kam risk.

ORB is intraday. Now a positional one, which is half of my own trading.

The idea is inverted. Instead of buying the breakout, you wait for the trend to catch its breath. The trend is up, price pulls back, then resumes — you enter on the pullback.

On a breakout your stop is far. On a pullback it's close. That is the entire difference — a closer stop means more size for the same risk, or less risk for the same size.

Overnight gap — woh risk jiska stop nahi hotaThe overnight gap — the risk a stop cannot hold

Aapka stop ₹480 pe hai. Stock ₹455 pe khulta hai. Aapka stop ₹455 pe trigger hoga — ₹480 pe nahi. Jo nuksaan aapne socha tha, woh usse kaafi bada hai.

Isiliye positional position ka size intraday se chhota hota hai. Yeh kayarta nahi hai — yeh ganit hai. Result wale din aur bade event ke aas-paas yeh gap ka khatra kai guna badh jaata hai.

Your stop is at ₹480. The stock opens at ₹455. Your stop triggers at ₹455 — not ₹480. The loss you planned for is not the loss you take.

Which is why a positional position is smaller than an intraday one. That isn't timidity — it's arithmetic. Around results and large events, that gap risk multiplies.

2

Strategy #3 — jab bhaav apne average ke paas lautta haiStrategy #3 — when price returns to its average

Rahul Sir

Teesri strategy poori ulti soch pe chalti hai. Pehli do trend pe chalti hain. Yeh mean reversion pe chalti hai — yani bhaav apne average se bahut door gaya toh wapas aayega.

Intraday ka average VWAP hai — volume se weighted aaj ka average bhaav. Bade institutional order isi ke aas-paas bharte hain, isiliye woh ek asli reference hai, sirf ek line nahi.

Aur yahi strategy sabse khatarnaak bhi hai — kyunki strong trending din pe bhaav average se door jaata rehta hai, aur mean reversion wala aadmi baar-baar ulta khada rehta hai.

The third runs on the opposite idea. The first two ride trend. This one runs on mean reversion — that price stretched far from its average tends to come back.

Intraday, that average is VWAP — today's volume-weighted average price. Large institutional orders fill around it, which makes it a real reference rather than just a line.

And it is also the most dangerous — because on a strongly trending day price keeps stretching, and the mean-reversion trader keeps standing in front of it.

3

Teen strategy, teen alag mausamThree strategies, three different climates

Arth

Toh teeno mein se kaunsi sabse achhi hai?

So which of the three is best?

Vridhi

Galat sawaal. Teeno alag mausam ke liye hain. ORB tab chalti hai jab din mein saaf disha ho. Pullback tab jab trend saaf ho. VWAP reversion tab jab din range mein ho.

Jo aadmi sirf ek strategy jaanta hai, woh har mausam mein wahi chalata hai — aur do-tihai waqt haarta hai. Jo teen jaanta hai, woh chun sakta hai. Aur sabse zaroori — woh teeno band bhi kar sakta hai.

Mere saal mein aise hafte aate hain jab main ek bhi trade nahi leti. Kyunki mausam kisi bhi strategy ke liye theek nahi tha. Woh bhi ek faisla hai, aur woh journal mein likha jaata hai.

Wrong question. They're built for three different climates. ORB works when a day has clear direction. The pullback when the trend is clean. VWAP reversion when the day is range-bound.

Someone who knows one strategy runs it in every climate — and loses two-thirds of the time. Someone with three can choose. And, most importantly, can switch all three off.

There are weeks in my year with no trades at all. Because the climate suited none of them. That's a decision too, and it goes in the journal.

Chapter 9 · band karne se pehleChapter 9 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Pullback pe stop paas hota hai, breakout pe door. Wahi poora farak hai — paas ka stop matlab behtar risk-reward.

A pullback puts the stop close; a breakout puts it far. That's the whole difference — a closer stop means better risk-reward.

2

Positional mein size hi aapka asli stop hai. Raat mein stop band hai; gap-down usse neeche khul sakta hai.

In positional trading, size is your real stop. The stop is offline overnight, and a gap can open below it.

3

Mean reversion trending din pe marti hai. Isiliye rule 1 hi sabse zaroori rule hai — aaj khelna hai ya nahi.

Mean reversion dies on trending days. Which makes rule 1 the most important rule — whether to play at all today.

4

Teen strategies teen mausam ke liye hain. Ek strategy wala aadmi har mausam mein wahi chalata hai.

Three strategies for three climates. Someone with one runs it in all weather.

5

Kuch hafte bina trade ke jaate hain. Woh bhi ek faisla hai, aur woh journal mein likha jaata hai.

Some weeks pass with no trades. That is a decision too, and it belongs in the journal.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Entry chunte waqt. Aap poochoge: is entry pe mera stop kitna door hai? Door hai toh shayad better entry ka intezaar karna chahiye.
  • Overnight position lete waqt. 5% gap-down maan ke size nikaaloge — har baar, bina exception.
  • Din shuru karte waqt. Pehla sawaal: aaj ka mausam kaunsa hai? Uske baad strategy chuni jaati hai.
  • Jab doosra trade haar jaaye. Aap teesra nahi loge. Rule 6 pehle se likha hua hai.
  • Choosing an entry. You'll ask how far the stop sits. If it's far, a better entry may be worth waiting for.
  • Taking a position overnight. You'll size against a 5% gap-down — every time, no exceptions.
  • Starting the day. First question: what's today's climate? The strategy is chosen after that.
  • When the second trade loses. You won't take a third. Rule 6 was written in advance.

Kitna Lagana HaiHow Much to Risk

1% rule — ₹25,000, ₹1 lakh aur ₹5 lakh ke liye poora solve karke. R-multiple kya hai. Aur stop-loss ka woh contract jo aap apne aap se karte ho.

The 1% rule — worked in full for ₹25,000, ₹1 lakh and ₹5 lakh. What an R-multiple is. And the stop-loss contract you sign with yourself.

Modules 18, 19 · ~35 min

Modules 18, 19 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 10Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 10

Kitna Lagana HaiHow Much to Risk

1% rule teen account size pe solve karke. R-multiple. Aur stop-loss ka contract.

The 1% rule worked across three account sizes. R-multiples. And the stop-loss contract.

M18–19M18–19~35 min~35 min
1

Sabse zaroori sawaalThe question that matters most

Vridhi

Arth, naye trader poochte hain “kya kharidun?” Purane trader poochte hain “kitna?”

Kyunki aapki strategy chahe 40% sahi ho ya 60%, aap zinda tabhi rahoge jab size sahi ho. Galat size ke saath sahi strategy bhi account khatam kar deti hai.

Rule ek line ka hai: ek trade pe apne capital ka 1% se zyada risk mat karo. Risk ka matlab hai — stop lagne pe kitne rupaye jaayenge. Position ki value nahi.

Yeh do cheezein log hamesha mila dete hain. Aur usi galti se account marte hain.

Arth, new traders ask “what do I buy?” Old traders ask “how much?”

Because whether your strategy is right 40% or 60% of the time, you survive only if the size is right. At the wrong size, even a correct strategy empties the account.

The rule is one line: never risk more than 1% of capital on one trade. Risk means the rupees you lose if the stop is hit. Not the position's value.

People conflate those two constantly. And that confusion is what kills accounts.

Chhote account ka sachThe small-account problem, honestly

₹25,000 pe 1% ka matlab hai ₹250 per trade. Aur Chapter 4 ka cost stack usi ₹250 mein se apna hissa leta hai. Isiliye chhote account pe percentage dhokha deta hai — 1% technically sahi hai, par practically woh kaafi tang hai.

Iska imaandaar jawab yeh nahi hai ki 3% risk le lo. Imaandaar jawab yeh hai: chhote account pe kam trade karo, bade stop wale setups chhodo, aur capital badhne tak sabar rakho. Risk badhane se account jaldi khatam hota hai, jaldi bada nahi hota.

On ₹25,000, 1% is ₹250 a trade. And Chapter 4's cost stack takes its share out of that same ₹250. Which is why percentages mislead at small size — 1% is technically right and practically very tight.

The honest answer is not to risk 3% instead. It is: trade less often at small size, skip wide-stop setups, and be patient until capital grows. Raising risk empties an account faster; it does not grow one faster.

2

R — trader ki apni bhashaR — the trader's own unit

Rahul Sir

Ab ek shabd jo poore course mein chalega: R. R ka matlab hai aapka ek trade ka risk. Bas.

Agar aapne ₹1,000 risk kiya aur ₹3,000 kamaaye, toh woh +3R hai. ₹25,000 wale account pe bhi +3R, ₹5 lakh wale pe bhi +3R. R rupaye ko hata deta hai aur sirf faisla dikhata hai.

Isiliye traders R mein baat karte hain. “Maine 40,000 kamaaye” se kuch pata nahi chalta. “Mera mahina +6R tha” se poori kahani pata chal jaati hai.

Now a word that runs through the rest of this course: R. R means the risk on one trade. That's all.

If you risked ₹1,000 and made ₹3,000, that's +3R. It's +3R on a ₹25,000 account and +3R on a ₹5 lakh one. R strips out the rupees and leaves the decision.

Which is why traders speak in R. “I made ₹40,000” tells you nothing. “My month was +6R” tells you the whole story.

CheezRupaye meinR meinKaunsa zyada kaam ka
Ek jeeta hua trade+₹3,000+3RR — size ka asar hat gaya
Ek haara trade−₹1,000−1RR — yeh hamesha −1R hona chahiye
Bura mahina−₹8,000−8RR — 8 galtiyan, ek tabahi nahi
Ek “chhota” nuksaan−₹4,000−4RR — yeh chhota nahi tha
ThingIn rupeesIn RWhich is more useful
One winning trade+₹3,000+3RR — size is removed
One losing trade−₹1,000−1RR — it should always be −1R
A bad month−₹8,000−8RR — eight mistakes, not one disaster
One “small” loss−₹4,000−4RR — that was not small

Aakhri row hi asli kaam ki hai. Rupaye mein ₹4,000 “chhota” lag sakta hai. −4R kabhi chhota nahi lagta — aur woh sach hai.The last row is the point. ₹4,000 can feel “small”. −4R never feels small — and −4R is the truth.

3

Stop-loss ka contractThe stop-loss contract

Tejas

Main stop lagata hoon. Bas kabhi-kabhi hata deta hoon jab lagta hai ki bhaav wapas aayega.

I do use stops. I just move them sometimes, when I think it'll come back.

Rahul Sir

Toh tumhare paas stop nahi hai, Tejas. Tumhare paas ek suggestion hai.

Stop ka poora matlab yeh hai ki woh us waqt lagaya gaya jab tum shaant the, aur woh us waqt chalega jab tum shaant nahi ho. Agar tum use us waqt hata sakte ho, toh usne apna ek hi kaam nahi kiya.

Aur “wapas aa jayega” — yeh Indian retail trading ka sabse mehenga vaakya hai. Kabhi-kabhi wapas aata hai. Aur us ek baar ki yaad aapse agle bees baar yahi karwaati hai.

Then you don't have a stop, Tejas. You have a suggestion.

The whole point of a stop is that it was set while you were calm, to act at a moment when you are not. If you can move it in that moment, it has failed at the only job it had.

And “it'll come back” — that is the most expensive sentence in Indian retail trading. Sometimes it does come back. And the memory of that one time makes you do it the next twenty.

Vridhi

Mera apna contract teen line ka hai, aur main use har saal dobara likhti hoon, haath se:

Ek — stop entry se pehle likha jaayega. Do — stop sirf munafe ki taraf khisakega, kabhi nuksaan ki taraf nahi. Teen — averaging down nahi hoga, kabhi nahi, kisi bhi haalat mein nahi.

My own contract is three lines, and I rewrite it by hand every year:

One — the stop is written before entry. Two — the stop only ever moves toward profit, never toward loss. Three — no averaging down, ever, under any circumstances.

Chapter 10 · band karne se pehleChapter 10 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

“Kitna?” sabse zaroori sawaal hai, “kya?” nahi. Galat size ke saath sahi strategy bhi account khatam karti hai.

“How much?” matters more than “what?” At the wrong size, even a correct strategy empties an account.

2

Size = (Capital × 1%) ÷ (Entry − Stop). Stop ki doori size tay karti hai — aapka bharosa nahi.

Size = (Capital × 1%) ÷ (Entry − Stop). Stop distance sets size — not your conviction.

3

Chhote account pe 1% tang hota hai. Jawab risk badhana nahi — kam trade karna aur sabar rakhna hai.

1% is tight on a small account. The answer isn't more risk — it's fewer trades and patience.

4

R aapka paimana hai. +3R har account size pe +3R hai. Rupaye jhooth bolte hain, R nahi.

R is your unit. +3R is +3R on any account size. Rupees flatter; R doesn't.

5

Stop entry se pehle likha jaata hai aur sirf munafe ki taraf khisakta hai. Warna woh stop nahi, suggestion hai.

The stop is written before entry and only ever moves toward profit. Otherwise it's a suggestion, not a stop.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har trade se pehle. Teen number likho: entry, stop, size. Teesra pehle do se nikalta hai — guess se nahi.
  • Jab bahut bharosa ho. Size wahi rahega. Bharosa size ka input nahi hai — yahi rule aapko bade nuksaan se bachata hai.
  • Mahine ke aakhir mein. Apna P&L R mein likho, rupaye mein nahi. Aapko turant pata chalega ki mahina kaisa tha.
  • Jab stop hatane ka mann kare. Aapko pata hoga ki yeh faisla aap nahi le rahe — woh contract pehle hi likha ja chuka hai.
  • Before every trade. Write three numbers: entry, stop, size. The third comes from the first two — never from a guess.
  • When you feel very confident. The size doesn't change. Conviction isn't an input — that rule is what saves you from the big one.
  • At month end. Write your P&L in R, not rupees. You'll see immediately what kind of month it was.
  • When you want to move a stop. You'll know that decision isn't yours to make now — the contract was signed earlier.

Modules 20, 21 · ~40 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 11Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 11

Likho, Warna Bhool JaogeWrite It Down or Lose It

Journal ki discipline, weekly review. Phir tees trades haath se replay — bina aage jhaanke.

Journal discipline and a weekly review. Then thirty trades replayed by hand, with no peeking ahead.

M20–21M20–21~40 min~40 min
1

Yaaddasht jhooth bolti haiMemory lies

Vridhi

Arth, ek prayog. Bina journal dekhe batao: pichhle mahine tumhare kitne paper trades jeete?

Arth, an experiment. Without looking at your journal: how many of last month's paper trades won?

Arth

Shayad… 60% ke aas-paas? Achha mahina tha.

Maybe… around 60%? It felt like a good month.

Vridhi

Ab journal kholo.

Now open the journal.

Arth ginta hai. 31 mein se 13.

Arth counts. Thirteen out of thirty-one.

Arth

42%. Mujhe laga tha 60.

42%. I'd have said 60.

Vridhi

Yeh galti nahi hai, Arth. Yeh dimaag ka design hai. Aap jeete hue trade yaad rakhte ho aur haare hue trade ki wajah yaad rakhte ho. Do alag cheezein — aur dono milke ek jhoothi yaaddasht banati hain.

Journal isliye nahi hota ki aap accha mehsoos karo. Journal isliye hota hai ki aap apne aap se jhooth na bol sako.

That's not a mistake, Arth. It's how the brain is built. You remember the trades you won, and you remember the reasons you lost. Two different things — and together they manufacture a false memory.

A journal doesn't exist to make you feel good. It exists so you cannot lie to yourself.

2

Tees trades, haath seThirty trades, by hand

Rahul Sir

Ab is level ka sabse zaroori kaam. Aap apni ek strategy ko haath se backtest karoge. Koi software nahi. Koi one-click report nahi.

Tareeka yeh hai: chart ko kisi purani date pe le jaao aur dayein taraf dhak do. Ab din-ba-din aage badho. Har din woh hi faisla lo jo us din tumhare paas ki jaankari se ban sakta tha.

Aage jhaankna hi woh ek cheez hai jo har backtest ko bekaar kar deti hai. Software mein yeh galti chhup jaati hai. Haath se karte waqt aap use mehsoos karte ho.

Now the most important exercise at this level. You will backtest one of your strategies by hand. No software. No one-click report.

The method: take the chart back to an old date and cover the right-hand side. Now step forward day by day. Each day, take only the decision the information available that day could support.

Peeking ahead is the single thing that makes any backtest worthless. In software that error hides. Doing it by hand, you feel it happen.

Arth

Tees hi kyun? Zyada behtar nahi hoga?

Why thirty? Wouldn't more be better?

Rahul Sir

Zyada behtar hai — par tees pehla imaandaar number hai. Tees ke neeche aap sirf shor dekh rahe ho. Aur haath se tees karne mein jo waqt lagta hai, wahi aapko woh strategy sikhaata hai jo koi report nahi sikha sakti.

More is better — but thirty is the first honest number. Below thirty you're looking at noise. And the time it takes to do thirty by hand teaches you things about the strategy that no report can.

3

Expectancy — ek line ka ganitExpectancy — the one-line arithmetic

Vridhi

Tees trade ho gaye? Ab ek formula. Expectancy = (hit rate × average jeet) − (miss rate × average haar), sab R mein.

Maan lo 40% trade jeete, average jeet +2.5R, average haar −1R. Toh: (0.4 × 2.5) − (0.6 × 1) = 1.0 − 0.6 = +0.4R per trade.

Dhyaan do: 40% hit rate ke saath bhi yeh strategy paisa banati hai. Kyunki jeet haar se dhaai guna badi hai. Hit rate akela kuch nahi batata.

Thirty trades done? Now one formula. Expectancy = (hit rate × average win) − (miss rate × average loss), all in R.

Say 40% win, average win +2.5R, average loss −1R. Then: (0.4 × 2.5) − (0.6 × 1) = 1.0 − 0.6 = +0.4R per trade.

Note that this makes money at a 40% hit rate. Because the wins are two and a half times the losses. Hit rate alone tells you nothing.

Tejas

Mera hit rate 65% hai. Par mahina red mein jaata hai.

My hit rate is 65%. And my month still ends red.

Vridhi

Toh aapki average haar aapki average jeet se badi hai. Aap chhote profit jaldi book kar lete ho aur nuksaan ko lambe samay tak rakhte ho. 65% hit rate ke saath bhi expectancy negative ho sakti hai — aur aapki hai.

Aur yeh cheez aapko sirf tab dikhti hai jab aapne tees trade likh ke gino ho. Isliye yeh chapter yahan hai.

Then your average loss is bigger than your average win. You book small profits quickly and hold losses long. Expectancy can be negative at a 65% hit rate — and yours is.

And you only see this once you've written down and counted thirty trades. Which is why this chapter sits here.

Backtest jo aapko dhokha dete hainThe backtests that fool you

Chaar galtiyan har haath-se-backtest mein ghus sakti hain. Ek — aage jhaankna (“yahan toh obvious tha”). Do — cost na lagana. Teen — woh trades chhod dena jo “main na leta”. Chaar — beech mein rules badal dena.

Chaaron ek hi kaam karte hain: woh aapki strategy ko us se behtar dikhate hain jo woh hai. Aur us jhoothi report pe asli paisa lagta hai. Isiliye tees trades likh ke karne padte hain — yaad se nahi.

Four errors creep into every hand-backtest. One — peeking ahead (“that was obvious here”). Two — leaving costs out. Three — skipping trades you “wouldn't have taken”. Four — changing the rules midway.

All four do the same thing: they make the strategy look better than it is. And real money gets placed on that flattering report. Which is why the thirty are written down, not remembered.

Chapter 11 · band karne se pehleChapter 11 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Yaaddasht jhooth bolti hai. Aap jeet yaad rakhte ho aur haar ki wajah — dono milke jhoothi tasveer banate hain.

Memory lies. You remember wins and you remember reasons for losses — together they build a false picture.

2

Weekly review teesh minute ka hai aur usme sirf ek badlav hota hai. Paanch badlav matlab kuch nahi seekha.

The weekly review is thirty minutes and produces one change. Five changes means you learned nothing.

3

Haath se backtest karo, chart ka dayan hissa dhak ke. Aage jhaankna har backtest ko bekaar kar deta hai.

Backtest by hand with the right side of the chart covered. Peeking ahead voids any backtest.

4

Expectancy = (hit rate × avg jeet) − (miss rate × avg haar), R mein. Hit rate akela kuch nahi batata.

Expectancy = (hit rate × avg win) − (miss rate × avg loss), in R. Hit rate alone says nothing.

5

65% hit rate ke saath bhi aap haar sakte ho — agar average haar average jeet se badi hai.

You can lose with a 65% hit rate — if your average loss exceeds your average win.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har Shanivaar. Teesh minute ka review, aur us hafte ke liye ek badlav. Bas ek.
  • Koi nayi strategy dekhte hi. Aap use haath se tees baar chalaoge, phir faisla karoge. Kabhi ulta nahi.
  • Jab koi backtest report dikhaye. Aap poochoge: cost andar hain? Skipped trades kitne the? Rules beech mein badle?
  • Jab hit rate pe garv ho. Aap expectancy nikaaloge. Hit rate akela ek bekaar number hai.
  • Every Saturday. A thirty-minute review and one change for the week. Just one.
  • The moment you see a new strategy. You'll run it by hand thirty times, then decide. Never the other way round.
  • When shown a backtest. You'll ask: are costs in? How many trades were skipped? Did the rules change midway?
  • When you're proud of a hit rate. You'll compute expectancy. Hit rate alone is a useless number.

Using AI as a junior analyst — Context / Task / Format, and the verify loop. Then turning your strategy into a flowchart two people could run identically. This is Algo Level 1.

Modules 22, 23 · ~35 min

Modules 22, 23 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 12Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 12

AI Aur Pehli MachineAI and Your First Machine

AI ko junior analyst banao — aur verify loop. Phir strategy ko flowchart mein badlo. Yeh Algo Level 1 hai.

Make AI your junior analyst — and the verify loop. Then turn a strategy into a flowchart. This is Algo Level 1.

M22–23M22–23~35 min~35 min
1

AI se kya poochna hai, aur kya nahiWhat to ask AI, and what not to

Tejas

Maine AI se poocha ki kaunsa stock kharidun. Usne teen naam diye. Do gir gaye.

I asked an AI which stock to buy. It gave three names. Two fell.

Rahul Sir

Tumne ek aise aadmi se sawaal poocha jisne aaj ka bhaav dekha hi nahi. Aur phir uske jawab pe paisa laga diya.

AI ka kaam alag hai, Tejas. Woh likhta hai, samjhaata hai, dhoondhta hai, aur draft banata hai. Woh faisla nahi leta aur data verify nahi karta.

AI draft karta hai; verify aap karte ho — exchange se. Ulta kabhi nahi. Yeh ek line poore is chapter ka saar hai.

You asked a question of something that hasn't seen today's price. And then put money on the answer.

AI's job is different. It writes, explains, searches and drafts. It does not decide, and it does not verify data.

AI drafts; you verify — against the exchange. Never the reverse. That single line is this chapter.

2

Context / Task / FormatContext / Task / Format

Vridhi

Achha prompt teen hisson ka hota hai. Context — main kaun hoon aur haalat kya hai. Task — mujhe theek kya chahiye. Format — jawab kis shakal mein chahiye.

Bura prompt: “options samjhao”. Achha prompt: “Main Indian retail trader hoon, 6 mahine ka experience, sirf defined-risk spreads. Mujhe theta ko ek chai ki dukaan wale example se samjhao, 150 shabd mein, koi formula nahi.”

Aur uske baad sabse zaroori kadam: verify loop. AI ka jawab lo, usme se har number nikaalo, aur har number exchange ya broker ki site se milao. Jo number verify na ho, woh delete.

A good prompt has three parts. Context — who I am and what the situation is. Task — exactly what I want. Format — what shape the answer should take.

A bad prompt: “explain options”. A good one: “I'm an Indian retail trader, six months in, defined-risk spreads only. Explain theta with a tea-stall analogy, 150 words, no formulas.”

And then the step that matters most: the verify loop. Take the answer, pull out every number in it, and check each against the exchange or broker site. Any number you can't verify gets deleted.

Arth

Aur agar AI galat bole toh?

And if the AI is wrong?

Vridhi

Woh galat bolega. Kabhi-kabhi bahut bharose ke saath galat bolega. Isiliye verify loop optional nahi hai. AI ka sabse khatarnaak jawab woh hota hai jo sahi lagta hai.

It will be wrong. Sometimes confidently wrong. Which is why the verify loop isn't optional. The dangerous AI answer is the one that sounds right.

3

Algo Level 1 — rules se flowchartAlgo Level 1 — rules to flowchart

Rahul Sir

Ab seedhi ka agla danda. Aapne teen strategies likhi hain. Ab unme se ek ko flowchart mein badalna hai — har condition, har branch, har exit.

Test yeh hai: agar do log us flowchart ko padh ke bilkul ek jaisa na chala sakein, toh woh abhi rule set hai hi nahi.

Yeh boring kaam hai. Aur yahi woh kaam hai jo discretionary trader ko systematic trader se alag karta hai.

Now the next rung. You've written three strategies. Turn one of them into a flowchart — every condition, every branch, every exit.

The test is this: if two people can't read that flowchart and run it identically, it isn't a rule set yet.

It's boring work. And it is exactly the work that separates a discretionary trader from a systematic one.

AI + flowchart — asli jodiAI + flowchart — the real pairing

AI ka sabse achha istemaal yahi hai: apna likha hua rule set usko do aur kaho — “ismein kaunsi condition ambiguous hai? Kahan do log alag faisla le sakte hain?” Woh aksar teen-chaar aisi jagah nikaal dega jo aapko dikhi hi nahi.

Par dhyaan rahe: woh aapke rules ko saaf karta hai, behtar nahi. Strategy achhi hai ya nahi, yeh sirf aapka haath-se-kiya-hua backtest bata sakta hai — jo aapne pichhle chapter mein kiya.

This is AI's best use: hand it your written rule set and ask — “which condition here is ambiguous? Where could two people decide differently?” It will usually find three or four gaps you couldn't see.

But note: it clarifies your rules, it does not improve them. Whether the strategy is any good is answered only by the hand-backtest you did in the last chapter.

Chapter 12 · band karne se pehleChapter 12 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

AI draft karta hai; verify aap karte ho — exchange se. Ulta kabhi nahi.

AI drafts; you verify — against the exchange. Never the reverse.

2

AI se kabhi bhaav, OI, lot size, margin ya rule ka current status mat poocho. Woh official source se aata hai.

Never ask AI for prices, OI, lot sizes, margins or the current status of a rule. Those come from the official source.

3

Prompt = Context + Task + Format. Aur uske baad verify loop — jo number verify na ho, woh delete.

Prompt = Context + Task + Format. Then the verify loop — any number you can't verify gets deleted.

4

Algo Level 1 = rules ka aisa flowchart jise do log ek jaisa chala sakein. Warna woh rule set nahi hai.

Algo Level 1 = a flowchart two people can run identically. Otherwise it isn't a rule set.

5

“Trend strong hai” raay hai; “9 EMA > 21 EMA, 5 din se upar dhalaan” rule hai.

“The trend is strong” is an opinion; “9 EMA above 21, sloping up five days” is a rule.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har baar AI se kaam lete waqt. Context, Task, Format — teeno. Aur jawab ke har number ko verify karo.
  • Jab AI bahut confident lage. Wahi sabse khatarnaak waqt hai. Number nikaalo aur exchange se milao.
  • Koi bhi strategy likhne ke baad. Use AI ko do aur poocho: kahan do log alag faisla le sakte hain?
  • Jab apna rule “strong” ya “achha” jaise shabd use kare. Woh abhi rule nahi hai. Use number mein badlo.
  • Every time you use AI. Context, Task, Format — all three. And verify every number in the answer.
  • When the AI sounds very confident. That is the dangerous moment. Pull the numbers and check them.
  • After writing any strategy. Hand it to AI and ask where two people could decide differently.
  • When your own rule uses words like “strong” or “good”. It isn't a rule yet. Turn it into a number.

Modules 24, 25 · ~40 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 13Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 2 Basic · Chapter 13

Screener Aur Sarkar Ka HissaScreeners and the Taxman

Screen banao, alert jodo — ab market aapko bulaata hai. Aur phir trader ka tax, seedhe shabdon mein.

Build the screen, wire the alert — the market calls you now. Then a trader's tax, in plain terms.

M24–25M24–25~40 min~40 min
1

Screen ghoorna kaam nahi haiStaring at screens is not work

Tejas

Main roz 9:15 se 3:30 screen ke saamne baitha rehta hoon. Phir bhi achhe move chhoot jaate hain.

I sit in front of the screen from 9:15 to 3:30. And I still miss the good moves.

Vridhi

Kyunki aankh ek saath paanch chart dekh sakti hai. Screener paanch sau dekh sakta hai.

Aur ek aur cheez — jo aadmi din bhar screen ghoorta hai, woh bore hota hai. Aur bore aadmi trade dhoondhta hai jo hai hi nahi. Screen ghoorna ek trading strategy nahi, ek trading risk hai.

Level 1 ka poora matlab yahi hai: aap market nahi dhoondhte. Market aapko bulaata hai.

Because your eye can watch five charts. A screener can watch five hundred.

And one more thing — someone staring all day gets bored. A bored person finds trades that aren't there. Staring at a screen is not a trading strategy; it's a trading risk.

That is the whole meaning of Level 1: you don't go looking for the market. The market calls you.

2

Alert — screen se azaadiAlerts — freedom from the screen

Vridhi

Screener raat ko chalta hai, alert din mein. Main apne shortlist ke har naam pe entry trigger ka alert laga deti hoon. Phir screen band.

Din mein do-teen alert aate hain. Main tab chart kholti hoon, checklist chalati hoon, aur ya toh trade leti hoon ya nahi leti. Poora kaam das minute ka.

Par dhyaan rakho: alert order nahi lagata. Aap lagate ho. Yahi Level 1 aur Level 2 ka farak hai — aur wahi farak abhi jaan-boojh kar rakha gaya hai.

The screener runs at night; the alerts run in the day. I set an alert at the entry trigger on every name in my shortlist. Then I close the screen.

Two or three alerts come in during the day. I open the chart then, run the checklist, and either take the trade or don't. The whole job takes ten minutes.

But note: the alert does not place the order. You do. That is the difference between Level 1 and Level 2 — and it is deliberately still there.

Arth

Auto-execution abhi kyun nahi?

Why not auto-execution yet?

Rahul Sir

Do imaandaar wajahein. Ek — tumhare rules abhi kaafi baar test nahi hue. Level 2 ek kamzor rule set ko bahut tezi se chalata hai. Do — woh ab ek regulatory kaam hai: static IP, Algo-ID, order-rate threshold. Chapter 25 mein poora.

Two honest reasons. One — your rules haven't been tested enough yet, and Level 2 runs a weak rule set very fast. Two — it is now a regulatory exercise: static IP, Algo-ID, order-rate thresholds. Full detail in Chapter 25.

3

Sarkar ka hissaThe government's share

Rahul Sir

Ab woh cheez jise 90% retail traders March mein yaad karte hain. Tax.

Sabse zaroori baat pehle: aapki trading ek hi tarah se tax nahi hoti. Kaunsa segment, kitna hold — usi se tay hota hai ki woh capital gain hai ya business income.

Aur yeh farak sirf rate ka nahi hai. Yeh farak yeh bhi tay karta hai ki aapka nuksaan kis cheez se set off ho sakta hai, aur kitne saal aage le jaaya ja sakta hai.

Now the thing 90% of retail traders remember in March. Tax.

First and most important: your trading is not taxed in one way. Which segment, and how long you held, decide whether it is a capital gain or business income.

And the difference isn't only the rate. It also decides what your losses can be set off against, and for how many years they can be carried forward.

Aap kya karte hoKaise tax hota haiRateLoss ka kya
Equity delivery, 12 mahine se kamShort-term capital gain, Sec 111A20%Sirf capital gains se set off
Equity delivery, 12 mahine se zyadaLong-term capital gain, Sec 112A₹1.25 lakh ke upar 12.5%, bina indexationSirf long-term capital gains se
Intraday equitySpeculative business incomeAapke slab peSirf speculative profit se, 4 saal carry-forward
Equity F&ONon-speculative business incomeAapke slab peSalary chhod ke kisi bhi income se, 8 saal carry-forward
What you doHow it's taxedRateWhat about losses
Equity delivery, held under 12 monthsShort-term capital gain, s.111A20%Set off only against capital gains
Equity delivery, held over 12 monthsLong-term capital gain, s.112A12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh, no indexationOnly against long-term capital gains
Intraday equitySpeculative business incomeAt your slabOnly against speculative profit, 4 years carry-forward
Equity F&ONon-speculative business incomeAt your slabAgainst most income except salary, 8 years carry-forward

Rates: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024 ke tahat STCG 20% aur LTCG 12.5% (₹1.25 lakh exemption ke upar), AY 2026–27 ke liye unchanged. Yeh ek parichay hai, tax salah nahi — apna ITR bharne se pehle CA se baat karo.Rates: STCG 20% and LTCG 12.5% above the ₹1.25 lakh exemption under the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, unchanged for AY 2026–27. This is an introduction, not tax advice — speak to a CA before filing.

Do cheezein jo March mein mehengi padti hainTwo things that get expensive in March

Ek — turnover. F&O mein turnover woh nahi hota jo aapko lagta hai. Woh contract value nahi hai. Aam tareeke se woh aapke profits aur losses ka absolute jod hota hai. Isi number se tay hota hai ki tax audit lagega ya nahi — aur zyadatar log ise galat nikaalte hain.

Do — advance tax. Agar aapki trading income kaafi hai, toh tax saal ke aakhir mein ek saath nahi, saal bhar kist mein dena hota hai. Chook jaane pe interest lagta hai. Yeh interest chhota lagta hai aur saal bhar mein bada ho jaata hai.

In dono ka theek hisaab ek CA se karwana chahiye — khaas kar pehle saal. Is chapter ka maqsad yeh hai ki aap sahi sawaal poochh sako, khud filing nahi.

One — turnover. In F&O, turnover is not what you assume. It is not contract value. It is commonly the absolute sum of your profits and losses. That number decides whether a tax audit applies — and most people compute it wrong.

Two — advance tax. If your trading income is significant, tax is payable in instalments through the year, not in one lump at the end. Missing them attracts interest. That interest looks small and compounds through the year.

Both belong with a CA — especially in your first year. The point of this chapter is that you can ask the right questions, not that you file it yourself.

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Screener paanch sau chart dekh sakta hai; aapki aankh paanch. Aur bore aadmi trade dhoondhta hai jo hai hi nahi.

A screener watches five hundred charts; your eye watches five. And a bored person finds trades that aren't there.

2

Liquidity filter hamesha pehla. Jis stock se nikal nahi sakte, uska trend bekaar hai.

The liquidity filter always comes first. A stock you can't exit has a useless trend.

3

Level 1 mein alert bulaata hai, order aap lagate ho. Yeh farak jaan-boojh kar rakha gaya hai.

At Level 1 the alert calls you; you place the order. That gap is deliberate.

4

Segment tay karta hai ki tax kaise lagega. Delivery = capital gains; intraday = speculative; F&O = non-speculative business.

The segment decides the tax treatment. Delivery = capital gains; intraday = speculative; F&O = non-speculative business.

5

F&O turnover contract value nahi hai. Aam tareeke se woh profits aur losses ka absolute jod hota hai — aur usi se audit tay hota hai.

F&O turnover is not contract value. It is commonly the absolute sum of profits and losses — and that decides the audit.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har raat das minute. Screener chalao, shortlist banao, alert lagao. Din mein screen band.
  • Jab screen ghoorne ka mann kare. Aapko pata hoga ki woh kaam nahi, risk hai.
  • Trade lene se pehle. Aapko pata hoga ki yeh trade kis bucket mein girega — aur uska tax alag hoga.
  • Saal bhar. Har trade ka record rakhoge, March ka intezaar nahi karoge. Turnover saal ke ant mein nahi banta.
  • Ten minutes each night. Run the screener, build the shortlist, set the alerts. Screen shut during the day.
  • When you feel like watching the screen. You'll know that's a risk, not work.
  • Before taking a trade. You'll know which bucket it falls into — and that its tax differs.
  • All year. You'll keep records as you go rather than waiting for March. Turnover isn't built in one evening.

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 14Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 14

Futures Ka DarwazaThe Futures Door

Lot size, margin, mark-to-market, rollover, basis. Phir options ki grammar — strategy se pehle.

Lot size, margin, mark-to-market, rollover, basis. Then the grammar of options — before any strategy.

M26–27M26–27~40 min~40 min
1

Ek din ka ₹80,000The ₹80,000 day

Tejas

Sir maine ek future lot liya. Bhaav mere against 1.2% gaya. Broker ne shaam ko ₹80,000 maang liye. Maine toh sirf ₹85,000 margin diya tha!

Sir, I took one futures lot. Price went 1.2% against me. The broker asked for ₹80,000 by evening. I'd only put up ₹85,000 as margin!

Rahul Sir

Kyunki futures mein aap margin pe nahi, poore contract pe khade hote ho. Margin sirf aapki security deposit hai — woh aapka maximum nuksaan nahi hai.

Cash equity mein aapka nuksaan aapke lagaye paise tak seemit hai. Futures mein nahi. Aur yeh ek line hi poora farak hai.

Aur roz shaam ko mark-to-market hota hai: us din ka nuksaan usi din aapke account se kat jaata hai. Woh “kal wapas aa jayega” ka intezaar nahi karta.

Because in futures you stand on the full contract, not on the margin. Margin is only your security deposit — it is not your maximum loss.

In cash equity your loss stops at what you paid. In futures it does not. That single line is the whole difference.

And there is mark-to-market every evening: that day's loss is deducted from your account that day. It does not wait for “it'll come back tomorrow”.

Lot size ek faisla nahi haiLot size is not a choice

Cash mein aap ek share bhi le sakte ho. Futures mein ek lot sabse chhoti ikai hai — usse chhota kuch hai hi nahi. Aur SEBI ne index derivatives ka minimum contract value badha kar ₹15–20 lakh kar diya hai (November 2024 se phased).

Iska seedha matlab yeh hai: chhote account ke liye ek lot bhi 1% rule ke andar nahi baithta. Chapter 10 ka formula yahan jawab de deta hai — agar ek lot ka risk aapke 1% se bada hai, toh woh trade aapke liye hai hi nahi. Aadha lot jaisi koi cheez nahi hoti.

In cash you can buy one share. In futures a lot is the smallest unit — there is nothing below it. And SEBI raised the minimum contract value for index derivatives to ₹15–20 lakh (phased from November 2024).

Which means plainly: for a small account, even one lot does not fit inside the 1% rule. Chapter 10's formula answers it — if one lot risks more than your 1%, that trade is not available to you. There is no such thing as half a lot.

2

Basis aur rolloverBasis and rollover

Vridhi

Do aur cheezein jo cash trader ko nahi pata hoti. Basis — future ka bhaav aur spot ka bhaav ek nahi hote. Farak interest aur time ka hota hai, aur expiry pe woh shoonya ho jaata hai.

Rollover — expiry aane pe aapko current mahine ka contract band karke agle mahine ka kholna padta hai. Woh apne aap nahi hota, aur uska apna cost hota hai.

Jo log rollover bhool jaate hain, unki position expiry pe apne aap settle ho jaati hai — chahe unka view abhi bhi sahi ho. Futures mein aapka view sahi ho aur trade phir bhi khatam ho jaaye — yeh normal hai.

Two more things a cash trader never meets. Basis — the futures price and the spot price are not the same. The gap reflects interest and time, and it goes to zero at expiry.

Rollover — at expiry you must close the current month and open the next. It doesn't happen by itself, and it has its own cost.

People who forget to roll have the position settled at expiry — even if their view is still right. In futures your view can be correct and the trade still ends. That is normal.

3

Options ki grammarThe grammar of options

Rahul Sir

Ab options. Aaj sirf shabd. Koi strategy nahi. Jo log shabd samjhe bina strategy seekhte hain, woh do mahine mein confused ho jaate hain.

Call = kharidne ka haq. Put = bechne ka haq. Dono mein haq shabd asli hai — farz nahi. Aap chaho toh use karo, na chaho toh chhod do.

Strike = woh bhaav jispe haq hai. Premium = us haq ki keemat, jo aap aaj dete ho. Expiry = us haq ki aakhri tareekh.

Aur sabse zaroori: premium ke do hisse hote hain. Intrinsic value — abhi is haq ki asli keemat kitni hai. Time value — baaki sab, yani “abhi waqt bacha hai” ki keemat. Time value har din ghatti hai, aur expiry pe shoonya ho jaati hai.

Now options. Today, only the words. No strategy. People who learn strategies before the vocabulary are confused within two months.

Call = the right to buy. Put = the right to sell. In both, the real word is right — not obligation. Use it if you want, walk away if you don't.

Strike = the price the right is at. Premium = what that right costs you today. Expiry = the last date the right exists.

And most important: premium has two parts. Intrinsic value — what the right is actually worth right now. Time value — everything else, the price of “there's still time left”. Time value decays every day and reaches zero at expiry.

Arth

Toh option kharidne wale ko sirf disha sahi nahi chahiye?

So an option buyer needs more than just the direction to be right?

Rahul Sir

Bilkul. Use disha chahiye, doori chahiye, aur waqt chahiye — teeno. Agle chapter mein hum yahi kholenge, aur uske baad wale mein woh number samjhenge jo course ke shuru mein aaya tha.

Exactly. He needs direction, distance and time — all three. We open that up in the next chapter, and the one after explains the number this course opened with.

Chapter 14 · band karne se pehleChapter 14 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Futures mein aap margin pe nahi, poore contract pe khade ho. Nuksaan margin se bada ho sakta hai.

In futures you stand on the full contract, not the margin. The loss can exceed the margin.

2

Mark-to-market roz shaam hota hai. Us din ka nuksaan usi din kat jaata hai — woh intezaar nahi karta.

Mark-to-market settles every evening. That day's loss leaves that day — it doesn't wait.

3

Lot sabse chhoti ikai hai. SEBI ne index derivatives ka minimum contract value ₹15–20 lakh kiya — chhote account ke liye ek lot bhi 1% rule se bahar ho sakta hai.

A lot is the smallest unit. SEBI raised the minimum index-derivatives contract value to ₹15–20 lakh — on a small account even one lot can fall outside the 1% rule.

4

Rollover apne aap nahi hota. View sahi hote hue bhi expiry pe trade khatam ho sakta hai.

Rolling over doesn't happen by itself. Your view can be right and the trade still ends at expiry.

5

Premium = intrinsic + time value. Time value har din ghatti hai aur expiry pe shoonya ho jaati hai.

Premium = intrinsic + time value. Time value decays daily and hits zero at expiry.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Pehla futures trade lene se pehle. Ek lot ka risk nikaalo aur apne 1% se milao. Na baithe toh trade nahi.
  • Har shaam. MTM ka matlab hai account roz badlega — aapko iske liye cash ready rakhna hoga.
  • Expiry hafte mein. Rollover ka faisla pehle se likha hoga, expiry ke din nahi.
  • Option ka bhaav dekhte hi. Aap poochoge: ismein intrinsic kitna hai aur time value kitni? Sasta option aksar poora time value hota hai.
  • Before your first futures trade. Work out one lot's risk against your 1%. If it doesn't fit, there is no trade.
  • Every evening. MTM means the account changes daily — you need cash ready for it.
  • In expiry week. The rollover decision is written in advance, not on expiry day.
  • Looking at an option price. You'll ask how much is intrinsic and how much is time value. A cheap option is usually all time value.

Modules 28, 29 · ~40 min

Modules 28, 29 · ~40 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 15Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 15

Greeks Se Mat DaroDon't Fear the Greeks

Delta, theta, gamma, vega — aaj aapka premium kaun kha raha hai. Aur live option chain padhna.

Delta, theta, gamma, vega — which one is eating your premium today. And reading a live option chain.

M28–29M28–29~40 min~40 min
1

Chaar Greek, chaar sawaalFour Greeks, four questions

Rahul Sir

Greeks ko formula ki tarah mat padho. Har Greek ek sawaal ka jawab hai jo aap waise bhi roz poochte ho.

Delta — “index 100 point hila toh mera premium kitna hilega?” Theta — “kal subah bina kuch hue mera premium kitna kam hoga?”

Gamma — “delta khud kitni tezi se badal raha hai?” Vega — “agar market ka dar badh jaaye toh mera premium kitna badhega?”

Chaar sawaal, chaar jawab. Bas. Aur inme se ek aapke against roz kaam karta hai — theta.

Don't read the Greeks as formulas. Each one answers a question you already ask every day.

Delta — “if the index moves 100 points, how much does my premium move?” Theta — “how much less will my premium be tomorrow morning if nothing happens?”

Gamma — “how fast is delta itself changing?” Vega — “if the market gets more fearful, how much does my premium rise?”

Four questions, four answers. That's all. And one of them works against you every single day — theta.

GreekSawaal jo woh poochta haiBuyer ke liyeSeller ke liye
DeltaBhaav hilne pe premium kitna hilegaDost — agar disha sahi hoDushman — agar disha galat ho
ThetaRoz kitna premium khud khatam hogaRoz ka dushmanRoz ka dost
GammaDelta kitni tezi se badal raha haiDost — bade move peSabse bada khatra — expiry ke paas
VegaDar badhne pe premium kitna badhegaDost — event se pehleDushman — event se pehle
GreekThe question it answersFor the buyerFor the seller
DeltaHow far premium moves when price movesA friend — if direction is rightAn enemy — if direction is wrong
ThetaHow much premium evaporates each dayA daily enemyA daily friend
GammaHow fast delta itself is changingA friend — on a big moveThe biggest danger — near expiry
VegaHow premium reacts to rising fearA friend — before an eventAn enemy — before an event

Dhyaan do: har row mein buyer aur seller ulte khade hain. Options mein har Greek ka ek dost aur ek dushman hota hai — aur aap tay karte ho ki aap kaun ho.Note that buyer and seller stand on opposite sides of every row. In options every Greek has a friend and an enemy — and you choose which you are.

2

Theta — woh ghadi jo ulti chalti haiTheta — the clock that runs backwards

Vridhi

Theta hi woh cheez hai jo option kharidne wale ko sabse zyada nuksaan deti hai, aur sabse kam samjhi jaati hai.

Option kharidne ka matlab hai: aapne ek aisi cheez kharidi jiski expiry date hai. Har guzarte din ke saath woh apne aap thodi mar jaati hai — chahe market hile ya na hile.

Aur theta seedhi line mein nahi chalta. Expiry jitni paas aati hai, utni tezi se woh premium khaata hai. Aakhri do-teen din mein woh sabse tez hota hai.

Isiliye sasta weekly OTM option sabse mehenga faisla hota hai. Woh sasta isiliye hai kyunki usme kuch hai hi nahi — sirf ghatta hua waqt.

Theta is what hurts option buyers most, and is understood least.

Buying an option means buying something with an expiry date. With every passing day it dies a little on its own — whether the market moves or not.

And theta isn't linear. The closer expiry gets, the faster it eats. In the last two or three days it is at its fastest.

Which is why a cheap weekly OTM option is the most expensive decision available. It is cheap because there is nothing in it — only shrinking time.

3

Option chain padhnaReading the option chain

Rahul Sir

Ab live chain. Usme sabse kaam ki cheez bhaav nahi — Open Interest hai. OI batata hai ki us strike pe kitne contract abhi khule hue hain.

Aur usse bhi zyada kaam ka hai change in OI. Bhaav badh raha hai aur OI bhi badh raha hai — naya paisa aa raha hai. Bhaav badh raha hai par OI gir raha hai — purani position band ho rahi hai. Do bilkul alag kahaniyan.

PCR (put-call ratio) aur max pain aksar over-use hote hain. Woh reference hain, signal nahi. Aur India VIX market ke dar ka paimana hai — woh badhta hai toh saare premium bhaari ho jaate hain.

Now the live chain. The most useful thing in it isn't price — it's Open Interest. OI tells you how many contracts are currently open at that strike.

More useful still is change in OI. Price up with OI up means new money coming in. Price up with OI down means old positions closing. Two entirely different stories.

PCR and max pain are routinely over-used. They are references, not signals. And India VIX measures market fear — when it rises, every premium gets heavier.

Tejas

Mujhe kisi ne bataya tha ki max pain pe expiry hoti hai. Maine us pe trade kiya tha.

Someone told me expiry lands on max pain. I traded on that.

Rahul Sir

Aur hui?

And did it?

Tejas

Kabhi-kabhi.

Sometimes.

Rahul Sir

“Kabhi-kabhi” ek strategy nahi hai, Tejas. Jo cheez naapi nahi gayi, woh raay hai — chahe woh option chain pe likhi ho. Chapter 19 mein hum isi ko naapna seekhenge.

“Sometimes” is not a strategy, Tejas. Anything unmeasured is an opinion — even when it's printed on an option chain. Chapter 19 is where we learn to measure it.

Chapter 15 · band karne se pehleChapter 15 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Har Greek ek roz ke sawaal ka jawab hai. Delta — bhaav; theta — waqt; gamma — delta ki raftaar; vega — dar.

Each Greek answers an everyday question. Delta — price; theta — time; gamma — delta's speed; vega — fear.

2

Theta buyer ka roz ka dushman hai aur seller ka roz ka dost. Expiry ke paas woh sabse tez hota hai.

Theta is the buyer's daily enemy and the seller's daily friend. It runs fastest near expiry.

3

Buyer ko disha, doori aur waqt — teeno chahiye. Seller ko sirf ek galat hona chahiye.

The buyer needs direction, distance and time. The seller needs only one of them to fail.

4

Option chain mein change in OI, OI se zyada kaam ka hai. Bhaav upar + OI upar = naya paisa; bhaav upar + OI neeche = position band.

Change in OI beats OI. Price up with OI up is new money; price up with OI down is positions closing.

5

PCR aur max pain reference hain, signal nahi. Jo naapa nahi gaya woh raay hai.

PCR and max pain are references, not signals. Anything unmeasured is an opinion.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Option kharidne se pehle. Teen sawaal: disha, doori, waqt. Teeno ka jawab likho. Ek bhi na ho toh trade nahi.
  • Jab option sasta lage. Aap poochoge: sasta kyun hai? Aksar jawab hai — kyunki usme kuch hai hi nahi.
  • Option chain kholte hi. Pehle change in OI dekhoge, phir premium. Ulta nahi.
  • Jab koi max pain ka level bataye. Aap poochoge: aapne kitni expiry pe test kiya, aur kitni baar chala?
  • Before buying an option. Three questions: direction, distance, time. Write all three answers. If one is missing, no trade.
  • When an option looks cheap. You'll ask why. Usually the answer is that there's nothing in it.
  • Opening an option chain. You'll look at change in OI first, premium second. Not the reverse.
  • When someone quotes a max-pain level. You'll ask across how many expiries they tested it, and how often it held.

Buyer Kyun Haarta HaiWhy the Buyer Loses

91% wale aankde ke peeche ka poora ganit. Aur phir defined-risk structures: bull call aur bear put spread, iron condor, straddle aur strangle — maximum loss entry se pehle likha hua, har baar.

Modules 30, 31 · ~40 min

Modules 30, 31 · ~40 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 16Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 16

Buyer Kyun Haarta HaiWhy the Buyer Loses

91% ke peeche ka ganit. Aur defined-risk structures — max loss entry se pehle likha hua.

The arithmetic behind the 91%. And defined-risk structures — max loss written before entry.

M30–31M30–31~40 min~40 min
1

Teen bets, ek ticketThree bets, one ticket

Vridhi

Chapter 15 mein humne dekha ki buyer ko teen cheezein chahiye. Ab uska ganit dekhte hain — motey andaze se.

Maan lo disha sahi hone ka mauka 50% hai. Doori kaafi hone ka 50%. Aur waqt ke andar hone ka 60%. Teeno saath chahiye, toh: 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.6 = 15%.

Yeh number bilkul sahi nahi hai — yeh padhane ke liye hai. Par jo baat sahi hai woh yeh: teen shart ek saath lagane se sambhavna gunaa hoti hai, jodi nahi jaati. Aur gunaa hamesha chhota karta hai.

In Chapter 15 we saw the buyer needs three things. Now the arithmetic — roughly.

Say direction is right half the time. Distance is enough half the time. And it arrives in time 60% of the time. You need all three: 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.6 = 15%.

That number is not precise — it's a teaching device. What is precise is this: stacking three conditions multiplies their probabilities, it doesn't add them. And multiplying always shrinks.

Arth

Toh seller ka kaam aasaan hai. Phir sab seller kyun nahi ban jaate?

So the seller has the easier job. Why isn't everyone a seller?

Rahul Sir

Kyunki aasaan aur surakshit alag cheezein hain.

Naked option seller aksar jeetta hai — chhota-chhota. Aur jab woh haarta hai, toh bahut bada haarta hai. Uska nuksaan theoretically unlimited hai.

Buyer chhote-chhote nuksaan se marta hai. Naked seller ek hi din mein marta hai. Dono raaste account khatam karte hain — bas raftaar alag hoti hai.

Because easy and safe are different things.

A naked option seller wins often — small amounts. And when he loses, he loses very large. His loss is theoretically unlimited.

The buyer dies of a thousand small losses. The naked seller dies in one afternoon. Both routes end the account — only the speed differs.

2

Teesra raasta — defined riskThe third road — defined risk

Vridhi

Main na naked buy karti hoon, na naked sell. Main spread lagati hoon. Aur uski wajah bahut simple hai.

Spread mein aap ek option lete ho aur doosra bech dete ho. Bechne wala option aapka kharcha kam karta hai. Aur kharida hua option aapke nuksaan pe dhakkan laga deta hai.

Nateeja: maximum profit aur maximum loss dono entry se pehle pata hote hain. Dono number. Likhe hue. Koi surprise nahi.

Iski keemat yeh hai ki aapka upside bhi capped ho jaata hai. Main woh keemat khushi se deti hoon — kyunki jo aadmi ek raat mein khatam nahi hota, wahi agle saal bhi yahan hota hai.

I neither buy naked nor sell naked. I use spreads. And the reason is simple.

In a spread you buy one option and sell another. The sold one reduces your cost. The bought one puts a lid on your loss.

The result: maximum profit and maximum loss are both known before entry. Two numbers. Written down. No surprises.

The price is that your upside is capped too. I pay that price gladly — because the person who isn't wiped out overnight is the one still here next year.

StructureViewMax lossKab use karein
Bull call spreadHalka bullishNet premium jo diyaUpar jaana hai par limited
Bear put spreadHalka bearishNet premium jo diyaNeeche jaana hai par limited
Iron condorRange mein rahegaWings ka farak minus premiumVolatility kam ho, range saaf ho
Long straddleBada move aayega, disha pata nahiDono premiumBade event se pehle — par IV crush ka dhyan
Long strangleBahut bada moveDono premium (sasta)Straddle jaisa, par move aur bada chahiye
StructureViewMax lossWhen to use
Bull call spreadModerately bullishThe net premium paidUp, but with a ceiling
Bear put spreadModerately bearishThe net premium paidDown, but with a floor
Iron condorIt stays in a rangeWing width minus premiumLow volatility, a clear range
Long straddleA big move, direction unknownBoth premiumsBefore a big event — mind the IV crush
Long strangleA very big moveBoth premiums (cheaper)Like a straddle, needing an even bigger move

Yeh table padhane ke liye hai, koi recommendation nahi. Har structure ka apna max loss hai — aur wahi number aapko entry se pehle likhna hai. Rate aur margin apne broker se verify karo.This table is for teaching, not a recommendation. Every structure has its own max loss — and that number is what you write down before entry. Verify rates and margins with your broker.

3

Ek rule jo sab kuch badal deta haiThe one rule that changes everything

Rahul Sir

Is level ka sabse zaroori rule ek line ka hai: jab tak aap apna maximum loss rupaye mein likh nahi lete, tab tak order nahi lagta.

Naked sell mein aap woh line likh hi nahi sakte — kyunki jawab “pata nahi” hai. Aur isi wajah se yeh course naked selling nahi sikhata.

Defined-risk structure ka poora faayda yahi hai: woh aapko yeh line likhne pe majboor karta hai. Woh discipline structure ke andar hi bani hui hai.

The most important rule at this level is one line: no order goes in until you have written your maximum loss in rupees.

In a naked sell you cannot write that line — because the answer is “unknown”. Which is exactly why this course does not teach naked selling.

That is the whole benefit of a defined-risk structure: it forces you to write that line. The discipline is built into the structure itself.

Tejas

Aur agar main naked bech doon aur stop laga doon?

And if I sell naked but put a stop on it?

Vridhi

Gap. Chapter 9 yaad hai? Raat mein aapka stop band hai. Naked short option pe gap aapke stop ke bahut neeche khul sakta hai — aur wahan nuksaan ki koi seema nahi hoti.

Stop ek order hai, guarantee nahi. Dhakkan sirf ek kharida hua option lagata hai.

The gap. Remember Chapter 9? Your stop is offline overnight. On a naked short option the gap can open far beyond your stop — and there, the loss has no boundary.

A stop is an order, not a guarantee. The only thing that puts a lid on it is a bought option.

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Buyer ko teen shart ek saath chahiye. Teen sambhavnaayein gunaa hoti hain — aur gunaa hamesha chhota karta hai.

The buyer needs three conditions at once. Three probabilities multiply — and multiplying always shrinks.

2

Buyer chhote nuksaan se dheere marta hai; naked seller ek din mein. Dono raaste account khatam karte hain.

The buyer dies slowly of small losses; the naked seller dies in a day. Both routes end the account.

3

Spread mein aap ek option lete ho aur doosra bechte ho. Becha hua kharcha ghataata hai; kharida hua nuksaan pe dhakkan lagata hai.

A spread buys one option and sells another. The sold one cuts the cost; the bought one caps the loss.

4

Defined risk ka matlab hai dono sire flat. Max profit aur max loss dono entry se pehle pata hote hain.

Defined risk means both ends are flat. Max profit and max loss are both known before entry.

5

Maximum loss rupaye mein likhe bina order nahi lagta. Jahan yeh line nahi likhi ja sakti, wahan trade nahi hai.

No order goes in until max loss is written in rupees. Where that line can't be written, there is no trade.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har option trade se pehle. Max loss rupaye mein likho. Likh nahi paa rahe? Toh woh trade nahi hai.
  • Jab koi “option selling se monthly income” bataye. Aap poochoge: aapka max loss kitna hai, aur woh number kahan likha hai?
  • Jab sasta OTM lene ka mann kare. Aapko pata hai ki woh teen bets ek ticket mein hai, aur sasta hone ki wajah hi uska khaali hona hai.
  • Position banate waqt. Payoff diagram banao — aur dekho ki koi sira khula toh nahi hai.
  • Before every option trade. Write the max loss in rupees. Can't write it? Then it isn't a trade.
  • When someone pitches “monthly income from option selling”. You'll ask what their max loss is and where that number is written.
  • When a cheap OTM tempts you. You know it's three bets on one ticket, and that its cheapness is its emptiness.
  • Building a position. Draw the payoff — and check that no end is left open.

Expiry Ka DinExpiry Day

Current SEBI F&O norms — ek exchange, ek weekly expiry; badha hua contract size; aur chhote accounts ke liye kya badla. Plus portfolio hedging, aur imaandaari se yeh bhi ki kab hedge nahi karna.

Current SEBI F&O norms — one weekly expiry per exchange, the raised contract size, and what that changed for small accounts. Plus portfolio hedging, and an honest look at when not to hedge.

Modules 32, 33 · ~35 min

Modules 32, 33 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 17Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 17

Expiry Ka DinExpiry Day

Current F&O norms — ek weekly expiry, bada contract size. Aur hedging: kab karo, kab bilkul nahi.

Current F&O norms — one weekly expiry, a bigger contract. And hedging: when to, and when not to at all.

M32–33M32–33~35 min~35 min
1

Rules jo 2024 mein badleThe rules that changed in 2024

Rahul Sir

Expiry ka maidan 2024–25 mein kaafi badal gaya. SEBI ne index derivatives ke rules kaafi sakht kiye, aur woh badlav November 2024 se April 2025 ke beech phase-wise aaye.

Do badlav sabse zyada asar daalte hain. Ek — har exchange pe ab sirf ek weekly expiry hai, ek benchmark index pe. Pehle hafte ke har din kisi na kisi index ki expiry hoti thi.

Do — index derivatives ka minimum contract value badha kar ₹15–20 lakh kar diya gaya. Iska seedha asar lot size pe pada aur isliye margin pe bhi.

The expiry landscape changed considerably in 2024–25. SEBI tightened the index derivatives rules, and the changes came in phases between November 2024 and April 2025.

Two of them matter most. One — each exchange now has just one weekly expiry, on one benchmark index. Before, some index expired on nearly every day of the week.

Two — the minimum contract value for index derivatives was raised to ₹15–20 lakh. That fed straight into lot sizes, and therefore into margins.

Arth

Toh chhote account wale ke liye kya badla?

So what changed for someone with a small account?

Rahul Sir

Bahut kuch. Bada contract size matlab har trade ka risk bada — aur Chapter 10 ka 1% rule usi ganit se chalta hai. Bahut se chhote accounts ke liye ek lot ab 1% ke andar nahi baithta.

Aur ek weekly expiry ka matlab hai ki roz-roz ka lottery khatam. Jo log har din expiry khelte the, unke paas ab hafte mein ek din hai.

A great deal. A bigger contract means bigger risk per trade — and Chapter 10's 1% rule runs on exactly that arithmetic. For many small accounts, one lot no longer fits inside 1%.

And one weekly expiry means the daily lottery is over. People who played an expiry every day now have one day a week.

2

Hedging — aur kab nahi karniHedging — and when not to

Vridhi

Ab doosri cheez. Portfolio hedging. Idea seedha hai: aapke paas stocks hain, aap index put kharid ke neeche girne se bachna chahte ho.

Yeh kaam karta hai. Par ek baat jo bahut kam log kehte hain: hedge muft nahi hai, aur lagataar hedge rakhna aapki expectancy chupke se kha jaata hai.

Har mahine put kharidna matlab har mahine premium dena. Agar market 10 mahine upar jaata hai aur 2 mahine neeche, toh aapne 10 mahine ka insurance bekaar diya taaki 2 mahine bach sako.

Now the other thing. Portfolio hedging. The idea is simple: you hold stocks and buy an index put to protect against a fall.

It works. But something few people say: a hedge isn't free, and a permanent hedge quietly eats your expectancy.

Buying a put every month means paying a premium every month. If the market rises for ten months and falls for two, you paid ten months of insurance to be protected in two.

Arth

Toh hedge kab karni chahiye?

So when should you hedge?

Vridhi

Teen haalat mein. Ek — jab ek pehle se pata event aa raha ho aur aap position band nahi kar sakte. Do — jab aapka portfolio itna bada ho gaya ho ki ek bada gir jaana aapke liye nuksaan nahi, aapdaa hai. Teen — jab kisi wajah se aapko position rakhni hi hai, bechne ka vikalp hai hi nahi.

Baaki har waqt, sabse sasta hedge chhota size hai. Yeh line aapko kisi option seminar mein nahi milegi, par yeh sach hai.

In three situations. One — a known event is coming and you can't close the position. Two — the portfolio has grown to where a big fall is not a loss but a disaster. Three — you must hold for some reason and selling isn't an option.

The rest of the time, the cheapest hedge is a smaller position. You won't hear that at an options seminar, but it's true.

Hedge ka cost drag — ek imaandaar hisaabThe cost drag of a hedge — honestly

Maan lo aap har mahine apne portfolio ka 1% premium deke protective put lete ho. Saal ka 12%. Aapka portfolio pehle 12% kamaayega, tab jaake aap barabar aaoge.

Yeh number kabhi-kabhi jaayaz hota hai — jaise ek bade pehle se pata event se pehle. Aur aksar nahi hota. Faisla yeh nahi hai ki “hedge achhi cheez hai ya buri”. Faisla yeh hai: is hedge ka cost mere liye is haalat mein jaayaz hai ya nahi — aur woh hisaab aap entry se pehle karte ho, baad mein nahi.

Say you spend 1% of the portfolio each month on a protective put. That's 12% a year. Your portfolio must make 12% before you break even.

Sometimes that number is justified — before a large known event, say. Often it isn't. The decision isn't “is hedging good or bad”. It is: is this hedge's cost justified for me in this situation — and you do that arithmetic before entry, not after.

Chapter 17 · band karne se pehleChapter 17 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Har exchange pe ab ek weekly expiry hai, ek benchmark index pe. Roz-roz wali expiry khatam.

Each exchange now has one weekly expiry, on one benchmark index. The daily expiry is gone.

2

Index derivatives ka minimum contract value ₹15–20 lakh hai. Bada contract matlab har trade ka risk bada.

The minimum index-derivatives contract value is ₹15–20 lakh. A bigger contract means bigger risk per trade.

3

Expiry din gamma sabse tez hota hai. Chhota move delta ko poora ulta kar sakta hai.

Gamma is at its highest on expiry day. A small move can flip delta entirely.

4

Expiry ka sabse aam nuksaan: disha sahi, move chhota. Theta baaki kaam kar deta hai.

The commonest expiry loss: right direction, small move. Theta finishes the job.

5

Hedge muft nahi hai. Lagataar hedge expectancy chupke se khaata hai — aksar sabse sasta hedge chhota size hai.

A hedge isn't free. A permanent hedge quietly eats expectancy — often the cheapest hedge is a smaller position.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Expiry wale hafte mein. Aapko pata hoga ki gamma tez hai, toh size chhota rakhoge — ya baithe rahoge.
  • Jab sasta expiry-day option dikhe. Aapko pata hoga ki 100% nuksaan yahan normal hai, exception nahi.
  • Hedge lene se pehle. Saal ka cost drag nikaaloge, aur poochoge ki woh is haalat mein jaayaz hai ya nahi.
  • Jab lot size badle. Aap turant apna 1% dobara nikaaloge — kyunki risk badal gaya hai, aapki marzi ke bina.
  • In expiry week. You'll know gamma is fast, so you'll size down — or sit out.
  • When a cheap expiry-day option appears. You'll know a 100% loss is ordinary here, not an exception.
  • Before hedging. You'll compute the annual drag and ask whether it's justified in this situation.
  • When a lot size changes. You'll recompute your 1% immediately — the risk changed without your consent.

Modules 34, 35 · ~35 min

Modules 34, 35 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 18Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 18

Event Wale DinEvent Days

IV run-up aur IV crush — disha sahi hone pe bhi trade kaise haarta hai. Aur idea se rule set tak.

The IV run-up and the IV crush — how a right direction still loses. And turning an idea into a rule set.

M34–35M34–35~35 min~35 min
1

Disha sahi, trade failRight call, failed trade

Tejas

Result se pehle maine call kharida. Result achha aaya, stock 4% upar khula. Mera option 30% neeche tha. Sir, yeh kaise ho sakta hai?

I bought a call before results. The result was good, the stock opened 4% up. My option was down 30%. Sir, how?

Rahul Sir

Kyunki tumne stock nahi khareeda tha. Tumne dar khareeda tha — aur result ke baad dar khatam ho gaya.

Event se pehle koi nahi jaanta ki kya hoga. Toh option bechne wale zyada premium maangte hain. Implied volatility chadh jaati hai. Aapka option mehenga ho jaata hai — sirf anishchitta ki wajah se.

Result aate hi anishchitta khatam. IV ek hi jhatke mein girti hai. Usko IV crush kehte hain. Aur woh crush itna bada ho sakta hai ki 4% ka sahi move bhi use nahi bhar paata.

Because you didn't buy the stock. You bought fear — and after the result the fear was gone.

Before an event nobody knows what's coming. So option sellers demand more premium. Implied volatility rises. Your option gets expensive — purely because of uncertainty.

The moment the result lands, the uncertainty is over. IV collapses in one move. That's the IV crush. And it can be large enough that a correct 4% move doesn't cover it.

2

Event playbook — pehle se likha huaThe event playbook — written in advance

Vridhi

Main event wale din faisla nahi leti. Main playbook follow karti hoon, jo event se hafta bhar pehle likha jaata hai.

Playbook mein teen hi cheezein hoti hain. Ek — is event pe main kya karungi: kuch nahi, size kam, ya defined-risk structure. Do — position event se kitna pehle band ya kam hogi. Teen — event ke baad pehle 30 minute mein main kuch nahi karungi.

Aur sabse zyada baar mera jawab hota hai: kuch nahi karna. “Flat rehna” ek poora jaayaz playbook entry hai — aur zyadatar retail traders ke paas woh option hai hi nahi, kyunki unhone use likha nahi.

I don't make decisions on event days. I follow a playbook, written a week before.

A playbook has three things. One — what I do for this event: nothing, reduced size, or a defined-risk structure. Two — how long before the event the position closes or shrinks. Three — I do nothing in the first 30 minutes after it.

And most often my answer is: do nothing. “Stay flat” is a completely legitimate playbook entry — and most retail traders don't have that option, because they never wrote it down.

The money in an event is still there afterwards — only then you aren't paying for the uncertainty.

3

Idea se rule set takFrom idea to rule set

Rahul Sir

Ab is level ka doosra kaam. Aapke paas ek discretionary idea hai — “mujhe lagta hai yeh kaam karta hai”. Use aise rule set mein badalna hai jise koi aur bhi bilkul waise hi chala sake.

Tareeka yeh hai: apne idea ko likho, phir har vaakya pe ungli rakh ke poochho — iska jawab naapne laayak hai? Jahan jawab nahi hai, wahin aapka rule abhi raay hai.

Chapter 12 mein humne yeh AI ke saath kiya tha. Ab aap khud karoge, aur ismein ek aur cheez jodenge: har rule ke saath uska kaaran likhna. Kyunki jo rule ka kaaran nahi pata, us rule ko aap pehle bure daur mein tod doge.

Now the second job at this level. You have a discretionary idea — “I think this works”. Turn it into a rule set someone else could run identically.

The method: write the idea down, then put a finger on each sentence and ask — can this be measured? Wherever the answer is no, that rule is still an opinion.

We did this with AI in Chapter 12. Now you do it yourself, with one addition: write the reason beside each rule. Because a rule whose reason you don't know is a rule you'll break in the first bad stretch.

Rule ke saath kaaran — ek udaharanA rule with its reason — an example

Sirf rule: “Result wale din trade nahi karunga.” Yeh rule pehle bure hafte mein toot jaayega, kyunki us din ek bada mauka dikh raha hoga.

Rule + kaaran: “Result wale din trade nahi karunga, kyunki mere paas earnings ka koi edge nahi hai aur IV crush meri disha sahi hone pe bhi mujhe haara sakta hai.” Yeh rule tikta hai — kyunki ab aap sirf rule nahi, uske peeche ka ganit maan rahe ho.

Rule alone: “I won't trade on results days.” That rule breaks in the first bad week, because a big opportunity will be visible that day.

Rule + reason: “I won't trade on results days, because I have no edge in earnings and the IV crush can beat me even when my direction is right.” That one survives — because you're now agreeing with the arithmetic, not just the rule.

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Event se pehle option mehenga hota hai kyunki IV chadhti hai. Aap dar kharid rahe ho, stock nahi.

Options are expensive before an event because IV rises. You're buying fear, not the stock.

2

Event ke baad IV crush hoti hai. Sahi disha bhi crush ko nahi bhar paati — yahi “sahi call, haara trade” hai.

IV crushes after the event. A right direction may not cover it — that's the right call, lost trade.

3

Event playbook event se pehle likha jaata hai, us din nahi. Aur “flat rehna” ek poora jaayaz entry hai.

The playbook is written before the event, not on the day. And “stay flat” is a legitimate entry.

4

Event ke baad pehle 30 minute mein kuch nahi. Us waqt bhaav khoj raha hota hai, bata nahi raha.

Nothing in the first 30 minutes after an event. Price is discovering then, not telling.

5

Har rule ke saath uska kaaran likho. Jis rule ka kaaran nahi pata, woh pehle bure daur mein tootega.

Write the reason beside every rule. A rule without its reason breaks in the first bad stretch.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Har result season mein. Aap pehle se tay karoge ki kaunse stocks mein flat rehna hai — us din nahi sochoge.
  • Jab event se pehle option sasta lage. Aapko pata hoga ki woh sasta nahi — IV usme pehle se bhari hui hai.
  • RBI policy ke din 11:45 pe. Aap screen se door rahoge. 30 minute ka rule pehle likha hua hai.
  • Koi bhi rule likhte waqt. Uske saath ek line kaaran ki likhoge — taaki woh rule bure hafte mein tike.
  • Every results season. You'll decide in advance which names you stay flat in — not on the day.
  • When an option looks cheap before an event. You'll know it isn't — IV is already loaded into it.
  • At 11:45 on RBI policy day. You'll be away from the screen. The 30-minute rule was written in advance.
  • Writing any rule. You'll add a line of reasoning — so the rule survives the bad week.

Imaandaar BacktestAn Honest Backtest

Costs andar, in-sample vs out-of-sample, walk-forward. Aur overfitting ke traps. Plus scanner banana.

Costs in, in-sample versus out-of-sample, walk-forward. And the overfitting traps. Plus building a scanner.

M36–37M36–37~40 min~40 min
1

Strategy jo sirf kaagaz pe chalti thiThe strategy that only worked on paper

Tejas

Maine ek strategy dhoondhi. Backtest mein 3 saal mein 340% return. Live chalaayi — do mahine mein 18% neeche.

I found a strategy. 340% over three years in the backtest. I ran it live — down 18% in two months.

Vridhi

Teen sawaal. Backtest mein costs the? Slippage tha? Aur aapne kitne parameter try karke yeh 340% wala version chuna tha?

Three questions. Were costs in it? Slippage? And how many parameter combinations did you try before picking the 340% one?

Tejas

Costs nahi the. Aur… shayad 200 combination try kiye the. Jo sabse achha tha wahi liya.

No costs. And… I tried maybe 200 combinations. I took the best one.

Vridhi

Toh aapne strategy nahi dhoondhi. Aapne 200 mein se sabse lucky number dhoondha.

Agar main 200 sikke uchaalun aur unme se woh chunun jo sabse zyada baar heads aaya, toh kya woh sikka jaadui hai? Nahi. Woh bas 200 mein se sabse lucky tha.

Ise overfitting kehte hain. Aur yeh zyadatar retail backtests ki asli kahani hai.

Then you didn't find a strategy. You found the luckiest of 200 numbers.

If I toss 200 coins and pick the one that landed heads most often, is that coin magic? No. It was just the luckiest of 200.

This is called overfitting. And it is the real story of most retail backtests.

Chaar traps jo har backtest ko sundar bana dete hainFour traps that flatter every backtest

Survivorship bias — aaj ke index ki list pe 10 saal ka test karna. Jo companies delist ho gayi ya index se nikal gayi, woh list mein hain hi nahi. Aapne sirf bache hue logon pe test kiya.

Look-ahead bias — aise data se faisla lena jo us din available hi nahi tha. Jaise quarter ka result us tareekh pe use karna jab woh publish hi nahi hua tha.

Parameter mining — 200 combination try karke sabse achha chunna. Chapter 11 wala sikka wala example.

Liquidity ignore karna — aise stocks mein trade maanna jinme aapka size ghusta hi nahi. Backtest ko liquidity ki parwah nahi hoti; aapko hoti hai.

Survivorship bias — testing ten years on today's index list. Companies that delisted or dropped out aren't in it. You tested only the survivors.

Look-ahead bias — using data that wasn't available that day. Like applying a quarterly result on a date before it was published.

Parameter mining — trying 200 combinations and keeping the best. The coin-toss example.

Ignoring liquidity — assuming fills in stocks that can't absorb your size. A backtest doesn't care about liquidity; you do.

2

Scanner — rank karo, sirf filter mat karoThe scanner — rank, don't just filter

Rahul Sir

Chapter 13 mein aapne filter lagaana seekha. Ab ek kadam aur: ranking.

Filter binary hota hai — andar ya bahar. Ranking batata hai ki bache hue naamon mein se sabse achha kaunsa hai. Aur jab aapke paas roz 40 setup milte hain par paisa sirf 4 ke liye hai, toh ranking hi asli kaam hai.

Rank kis cheez pe? Momentum, volatility-adjusted return, volume ka quality — kuch bhi jo aapki strategy ke matlab ka ho. Par ek shart: rank ka rule bhi naapne laayak hona chahiye, aur woh bhi backtest hona chahiye.

Kyunki ranking khud ek strategy hai. Log filter test karte hain aur ranking “feel” se chun lete hain — aur phir hairaan hote hain.

In Chapter 13 you learned to filter. Now one step further: ranking.

A filter is binary — in or out. Ranking tells you which of the survivors is best. And when 40 setups appear daily but you have capital for four, ranking is the actual job.

Rank on what? Momentum, volatility-adjusted return, volume quality — whatever matters to your strategy. One condition: the ranking rule must also be measurable, and it must also be backtested.

Because ranking is itself a strategy. People test the filters and pick the ranking by feel — then wonder what went wrong.
