3

Ek backtest kab bharose laayak haiWhen a backtest deserves trust

Vridhi

Main kisi backtest pe tabhi paisa lagati hoon jab woh chaar sawaalon ka jawab de de.

Ek — kitne trade? 30 se kam matlab shor. Do — kitne alag market daur mein? Ek hi bull run mein achha chalna kuch nahi sabit karta.

Teen — sabse bura daur kitna bura tha, aur kitna lamba? Chaar — kitne parameter try kiye gaye the?

Chautha sawaal koi nahi poochta, aur wahi sabse zaroori hai. Jitne zyada combination try kiye, utna zyada aapka result luck ka hissa hai.

I put money behind a backtest only when it answers four questions.

One — how many trades? Under 30 is noise. Two — across how many market regimes? Working through one bull run proves nothing.

Three — how bad was the worst stretch, and how long? Four — how many parameters were tried?

Nobody asks the fourth, and it matters most. The more combinations tried, the more of the result is luck.

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Bina cost wala backtest ek kahani hai. Chapter 4 ka poora stack andar daalo, dono taraf.

A backtest without costs is a story. Put Chapter 4's whole stack in, on both sides.

2

Data ko 70/30 mein baanto. 30% ko mat chhuo. Out-of-sample pe ek hi baar chalta hai.

Split the data 70/30 and don't touch the 30%. Out-of-sample runs once.

3

Out-of-sample bura aaya toh strategy fail hai. Tweak karke dobara chalana test ko khatam kar deta hai.

A poor out-of-sample result means the strategy failed. Tweaking and retrying ends the test.

4

Chaar traps: survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, parameter mining, liquidity ignore karna.

Four traps: survivorship bias, look-ahead bias, parameter mining, ignoring liquidity.

5

Ranking khud ek strategy hai. Use bhi naapna aur backtest karna padta hai — feel se nahi chunte.

Ranking is itself a strategy. It must also be measured and backtested — not picked by feel.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Koi bhi backtest dekhte hi. Chaar sawaal poochoge — aur chautha (kitne parameter) sabse zyada bataayega.
  • Apni strategy test karte waqt. Data pehle baantoge, phir kaam shuru karoge. Baad mein baantna bemaani hai.
  • Jab koi “200% return wali strategy” beche. Aap poochoge: costs andar the? Out-of-sample kya tha?
  • Scanner banate waqt. Ranking ka rule bhi likha hua aur test kiya hua hoga — filter ki tarah.
  • Looking at any backtest. You'll ask the four questions — and the fourth (how many parameters) will tell you most.
  • Testing your own strategy. You'll split the data first, then start work. Splitting afterwards means nothing.
  • When someone sells a “200% strategy”. You'll ask whether costs were in and what the out-of-sample showed.
  • Building a scanner. The ranking rule will be written and tested too — just like the filters.

Modules 38, 39 · ~35 min

Modules 38, 39 · ~35 min

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 20Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 3 Intermediate · Chapter 20

Tax Aur Kill-SwitchTax and the Kill-Switch

F&O business income, expenses, carry-forward, advance tax. Aur woh kill-switch jo shaant-aap likhta hai.

F&O as business income, expenses, carry-forward, advance tax. And the kill-switch the calm you writes.

M38–39M38–39~35 min~35 min
1

Business income hone ke faaydeThe upside of being a business

Rahul Sir

Chapter 13 mein humne dekha ki F&O non-speculative business income hai. Zyadatar log ise ek bojh samajhte hain. Uske do bade faayde bhi hain.

Pehla — expenses. Business income mein aap us business ke jaayaz kharche claim kar sakte ho: brokerage, data subscription, internet ka hissa, salaah ki fees, laptop ki depreciation, bijli ka hissa. Capital gains mein yeh sab nahi milta.

Doosra — loss ka behtar treatment. Non-speculative business loss salary chhod ke zyadatar income se set off ho sakta hai, aur 8 saal carry-forward hota hai. Speculative loss sirf speculative profit se aur sirf 4 saal.

In Chapter 13 we saw that F&O is non-speculative business income. Most people treat that as a burden. It carries two real advantages.

First — expenses. Business income lets you claim the legitimate costs of that business: brokerage, data subscriptions, a share of internet, advisory fees, laptop depreciation, a share of electricity. None of that exists in capital gains.

Second — better loss treatment. A non-speculative business loss sets off against most income other than salary, and carries forward eight years. A speculative loss offsets only speculative profit, and only for four.

Arth

Aur iske liye kya karna padta hai?

And what does that require?

Rahul Sir

Record. Poore saal ka record. Loss carry-forward ka faayda sirf tabhi milta hai jab aapne return samay pe file kiya ho. Deadline chook gaye toh woh carry-forward chala gaya — hamesha ke liye.

Yeh un chhoti baaton mein se hai jo saal bhar ki mehnat ka faayda ek din mein khatam kar deti hai.

Records. A full year of them. A carried-forward loss survives only if the return was filed on time. Miss the deadline and that carry-forward is gone — permanently.

It is one of those small things that can wipe out a year's worth of benefit in a single day.

Your own case can differ — particularly on audit, presumptive taxation, and in your first year. Talk to a CA.

2

Kill-switch — shaant-aap ka faislaThe kill-switch — a decision by the calm you

Vridhi

Ab is poore level ki sabse zaroori cheez. Aur woh tax nahi hai.

Har trader ke andar do log hote hain. Shaant-aap — jo Shanivaar ko rules likhta hai. Aur tilted-aap — jo Mangal ko teen loss ke baad size double karna chahta hai.

Kill-switch ka poora maqsad yeh hai ki tilted-aap ko vote hi na mile. Woh faisla pehle se liya ja chuka hai, aur us waqt liya gaya jab dimaag kaam kar raha tha.

Now the most important thing in this entire level. And it isn't tax.

Every trader contains two people. Calm-you — who writes rules on a Saturday. And tilted-you — who wants to double size on a Tuesday after three losses.

A kill-switch exists so tilted-you never gets a vote. The decision was already made, at a moment when the mind was working.

Tejas

Par kabhi-kabhi teesre loss ke baad hi asli mauka aata hai.

But sometimes the real opportunity comes right after the third loss.

Vridhi

Bilkul aata hai. Aur usi ek yaad ki wajah se aap agle bees baar rule todoge. Yeh line aapko mahenga padegi, Tejas — aur aap yeh jaante ho.

Kill-switch ka matlab yeh nahi ki aap us mauke ko miss nahi karoge. Kill-switch ka matlab yeh hai ki aap us din tak zinda rahoge jab aisa mauka phir aaye.

It certainly does. And that one memory will make you break the rule the next twenty times. That sentence will cost you, Tejas — and you know it.

A kill-switch doesn't mean you won't miss that opportunity. It means you'll still be here the day the next one comes.

Kill-switch tabhi kaam karta hai jab woh aapke haath mein na hoA kill-switch works only when it isn't in your hands

Ek rule jo aap us waqt hata sakte ho jab woh lagu ho raha hai, woh rule nahi hai. Isiliye kill-switch ko mechanical banao: platform se logout, app delete for the day, trading terminal band, ya kisi aur ko batana ki aaj band hai.

Yeh bachkana nahi lagta chahiye. Jo aadmi teen loss ke baad shaant hai, woh is chapter ka target hi nahi hai. Jo aadmi us waqt shaant nahi rehta — aur woh hum mein se zyadatar hain — use mechanical switch chahiye, aur uska chaabi doosri jagah honi chahiye.

A rule you can lift at the moment it binds is not a rule. So make the kill-switch mechanical: log out of the platform, remove the app for the day, shut the terminal, or tell someone else that you're done for the day.

This shouldn't feel childish. Someone who stays calm after three losses isn't this chapter's audience. Someone who doesn't — which is most of us — needs a mechanical switch, with the key kept somewhere else.

Chapter 20 · band karne se pehleChapter 20 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

F&O business income hai — iske do faayde hain. Expenses claim ho sakte hain, aur loss 8 saal carry-forward hota hai.

F&O is business income — with two advantages. Expenses are claimable and losses carry forward eight years.

2

Carry-forward tabhi milta hai jab return samay pe file ho. Deadline chooki toh woh faayda hamesha ke liye gaya.

Carry-forward survives only with a timely return. Miss the deadline and that benefit is gone permanently.

3

Har trader ke andar do log hain. Shaant-aap rules likhta hai; tilted-aap unhe todna chahta hai.

Every trader contains two people. Calm-you writes the rules; tilted-you wants to break them.

4

Teen circuit breakers chahiye: din ka, hafte ka, mahine ka. Numbers aapke, par teeno hone chahiye.

You need three circuit breakers: daily, weekly, monthly. Your own numbers — but all three must exist.

5

Kill-switch mechanical hona chahiye. Jo rule aap us waqt hata sako, woh rule hai hi nahi.

The kill-switch must be mechanical. A rule you can lift in the moment isn't a rule.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Saal bhar, har mahine. Expenses ka record rakhoge — March mein yaad nahi karoge.
  • Teesre loss ke baad. Aap faisla nahi loge. Faisla pehle liya ja chuka hai — aur platform band ho jaayega.
  • Bure hafte ke baad. Aap aadhe size pe wapas aaoge, poore pe nahi. Paanch clean trades ke baad hi poora size.
  • Return file karte waqt. Aapko pata hoga ki deadline sirf ek tareekh nahi — woh aapke carry-forward ki shart hai.
  • Every month, all year. You'll keep expense records rather than reconstructing them in March.
  • After the third loss. You won't decide. The decision was made earlier — and the platform closes.
  • After a bad week. You'll return at half size, not full. Full size comes after five clean trades.
  • Filing your return. You'll know the deadline isn't just a date — it's the condition on your carry-forward.

Aankdon Ki BuniyaadStatistical Foundations

Aankdon Ki BuniyaadStatistical Foundations

Stationarity, ADF, Hurst, half-life, cointegration — NSE pe. Phir pairs trading.

Stationarity, ADF, Hurst, half-life, cointegration — on NSE data. Then pairs trading.

M40–41M40–41~45 min~45 min
1

Ek sawaal jo sab kuch tay karta haiThe question that decides everything

Vridhi

Level 4 ek hi sawaal se shuru hota hai, Arth: yeh series wapas aati hai, ya chalti rehti hai?

Agar wapas aati hai — mean reverting — toh door jaane pe ulta trade karo. Agar chalti rehti hai — trending — toh saath mein chalo. Ulta karoge toh dono mein maar khaoge.

Ab tak humne yeh aankhon se tay kiya. Is level mein hum ise naapenge. Aur naapne ke baad aapki aankh dobara wahi nahi dekhegi.

Level 4 opens on one question, Arth: does this series come back, or does it keep going?

If it comes back — mean reverting — you fade the extremes. If it keeps going — trending — you follow. Get it backwards and both hurt.

Until now we judged this by eye. At this level we measure it. And after you measure it, your eye never sees the same thing again.

ToolKya poochta haiJawab ka matlabSeedha istemaal
ADF testKya yeh series stationary hai?p-value chhota → haan, wapas aati haiPair ka spread trade karne laayak hai ya nahi
Hurst exponentYeh trend karta hai ya revert?H < 0.5 revert · H ≈ 0.5 random · H > 0.5 trendKaunsi strategy is instrument pe lagegi
Half-lifeWapas aane mein kitna waqt?Din mein — agar bahut lamba hai toh bekaarAapka holding period aur stop ka waqt
CointegrationDo series ek saath chalti hain?Haan → unka spread trade ho sakta haiPairs trading ki buniyaad
ToolWhat it asksWhat the answer meansDirect use
ADF testIs this series stationary?Small p-value → yes, it revertsWhether a pair's spread is tradeable
Hurst exponentDoes it trend or revert?H < 0.5 reverts · H ≈ 0.5 random · H > 0.5 trendsWhich strategy family fits this instrument
Half-lifeHow long to revert?In days — too long and it's unusableYour holding period and time stop
CointegrationDo two series move together?Yes → their spread is tradeableThe foundation of pairs trading

Dhyaan do: yeh chaar tools signal nahi dete. Yeh batate hain ki kaunsi tarah ki strategy is instrument pe lag sakti hai. Yeh strategy se pehle ka kaam hai.Note these four give no signals. They tell you which family of strategy can apply to this instrument. This is the work that comes before a strategy.

2

Correlation aur cointegration — ek nahi hainCorrelation and cointegration are not the same

Rahul Sir

Yeh do shabd log roz mila dete hain, aur wahi galti pairs trading ke zyadatar nuksaan ki jadd hai.

Correlation kehta hai: dono ek saath hilte hain. Cointegration kehta hai: dono ek doosre se bandhe hue hain — door ja sakte hain, par rishta kheench ke wapas laata hai.

Do sharabi ek hi raaste pe chal rahe hain — correlated. Do sharabi ek rassi se bandhe hue — cointegrated. Pairs trade rassi pe chalta hai, saath chalne pe nahi.

People conflate these two daily, and that confusion is the root of most losses in pairs trading.

Correlation says they move together. Cointegration says they are tethered — they can drift apart, but the relationship pulls them back.

Two drunks walking the same road — correlated. Two drunks tied by a rope — cointegrated. A pairs trade rides the rope, not the shared direction.

Arth

Aur rassi toot jaaye toh?

And if the rope breaks?

Vridhi

Bas. Wahi poora khel hai. Rassi chupchap toot-ti hai — koi ghanti nahi bajti. Merger ho jaata hai, business model badal jaata hai, regulation badal jaata hai, promoter badal jaata hai.

Isiliye mera rule hai: har pair ka cointegration rolling window pe dobara test hota hai. Aur ek time stop hota hai — agar half-life se do-teen guna waqt mein spread wapas nahi aaya, toh main maan leti hoon ki rassi toot gayi. Chahe nuksaan ho.

That's it. That's the whole game. The rope breaks quietly — no bell rings. A merger happens, a business model changes, a regulation changes, a promoter changes.

So my rule is: cointegration is retested on a rolling window. And there is a time stop — if the spread hasn't reverted within two or three times its half-life, I assume the rope broke. Even at a loss.

Indian market mein pairs trading ki asli dikkateinThe real constraints on pairs trading in India

Ek — shorting. Cash segment mein intraday ke alawa short nahi kar sakte. Toh pair ka short leg aksar futures mein lena padta hai — aur wahan lot size, margin aur expiry apne rules laati hain.

Do — lot size ka mismatch. Hedge ratio kehta hai 1:1.37, par futures mein aap sirf poore lot le sakte ho. Aapka hedge kabhi perfect nahi hoga.

Teen — do taraf ka cost. Pair mein do legs hain, toh Chapter 4 ka cost stack do baar lagta hai, aur exit pe phir do baar. Chaar baar. Yeh bahut si “profitable” pairs strategies ko khatam kar deta hai.

One — shorting. You cannot short in the cash segment beyond intraday. So the short leg usually has to sit in futures — which brings lot size, margin and expiry with it.

Two — lot-size mismatch. The hedge ratio says 1:1.37, but futures trade in whole lots. Your hedge will never be exact.

Three — double costs. A pair has two legs, so Chapter 4's stack applies twice on entry and twice on exit. Four times. That alone kills many “profitable” pairs strategies.

First question: does this series revert or trend? Get it backwards and both hurt.

2

ADF, Hurst, half-life, cointegration signal nahi dete. Woh batate hain ki kaunsi strategy lag sakti hai.

3

Correlation ≠ cointegration. Saath chalna alag hai, rassi se bandha hona alag. Pair rassi pe chalta hai.

Correlation ≠ cointegration. Moving together is not being tethered. A pair rides the tether.

4

5

A pair pays costs four times — two legs, entry and exit. That alone finishes many strategies.

  • Koi bhi naya instrument dekhte waqt. Pehle naapoge ki woh revert karta hai ya trend — phir strategy chunoge.

  • Do-leg wali koi bhi strategy dekhte waqt. Cost ko chaar se gunaa karoge, phir expectancy dekhoge.
  • Approaching any new instrument. You'll measure whether it reverts or trends first, then pick the strategy.
  • When someone says “these two move together”. You'll ask: correlated or cointegrated? Two different claims.
  • Taking a reversion trade. You'll derive a time stop from the half-life — because what doesn't revert ties up your capital.
  • Looking at any two-leg strategy. You'll multiply costs by four before looking at expectancy.

Volatility Ka KhelThe Volatility Game

Realised vs implied, IV rank, VIX term structure. Delta-neutral, gamma scalping, skew.

Realised versus implied, IV rank, the VIX term structure. Delta-neutral, gamma scalping, skew.

M42–43M42–43~45 min~45 min
1

Do volatility, do alag cheezeinTwo volatilities, two different things

Rahul Sir

Volatility ke do roop hain aur unka farak samajhna is poore chapter ki chaabi hai.

Realised volatility — jo hua. Guzre hue dinon mein bhaav kitna hila. Yeh itihaas hai, aur ise naapa ja sakta hai.

Implied volatility — jo market soch raha hai ki hoga. Yeh option ke premium se nikalti hai. Yeh ek raay hai, aankda nahi.

Volatility trading ka poora khel in dono ke farak pe chalta hai. Jab IV, realised se kaafi upar ho, toh option mehenge hain. Jab neeche ho, toh saste.

Volatility comes in two forms, and the difference between them is the key to this chapter.

Realised volatility — what happened. How much price actually moved over past days. It is history, and it can be measured.

Implied volatility — what the market thinks will happen. It's extracted from option premiums. It is an opinion, not a measurement.

The whole game of volatility trading lives in the gap between the two. When IV sits well above realised, options are expensive. When below, cheap.

“IV zyada hai” ek adhoora vaakya hai“IV is high” is an incomplete sentence

IV ka number akela bekaar hai. 18% ek stock ke liye bahut zyada ho sakta hai aur doosre ke liye bahut kam. Isiliye IV rank aur IV percentile use hote hain — woh poochte hain: is instrument ke apne itihaas mein aaj ka IV kahan khada hai?

Aur ek aur cheez jo aksar chhoot jaati hai: IV zyada hone ka matlab yeh nahi ki woh galat hai. Kabhi-kabhi market sach mein jaanta hai ki kuch aa raha hai. Mehenga option bechne wale aksar isi jaal mein girte hain.

An IV number alone is useless. 18% can be very high for one stock and very low for another. Which is why IV rank and IV percentile exist — they ask: where does today's IV sit within this instrument's own history?

And one more thing that gets missed: high IV does not mean IV is wrong. Sometimes the market genuinely knows something is coming. Sellers of expensive options fall into exactly that trap.

2

Delta-neutral — disha se aazaadiDelta-neutral — freedom from direction

Vridhi

Ab tak humne har trade disha pe liya. Volatility trading alag hai: aap disha se nikal jaate ho aur sirf volatility pe khelte ho.

Delta-neutral ka matlab hai ki aapka position abhi kisi disha mein nahi jhuka. Index upar jaaye ya neeche — pehle jhatke mein aapko koi khaas farak nahi padta.

Par “abhi” shabd asli hai. Bhaav hilte hi delta badal jaata hai. Position dobara neutral karni padti hai. Usi ko gamma scalping kehte hain.

Aur yahin Indian retail ki sabse badi dikkat aati hai: har re-neutralisation ek trade hai, aur har trade Chapter 4 ka poora cost stack le kar aata hai.

Every trade so far has been directional. Volatility trading is different: you step out of direction and trade volatility alone.

Delta-neutral means your position leans in no direction right now. Index up or down — on the first move it barely matters to you.

But the word “now” is doing real work. As price moves, delta changes. You must re-neutralise. That is gamma scalping.

And here comes Indian retail's biggest constraint: each re-neutralisation is a trade, and each trade brings Chapter 4's whole cost stack with it.

Arth

Toh gamma scalping retail ke liye chal sakti hai?

So can gamma scalping work for retail?

Vridhi

Imaandaar jawab: aksar nahi. Ismein bahut baar adjust karna padta hai, aur retail cost pe woh maths tikti nahi. Institutional desks ka cost aapse bahut kam hota hai.

Main yeh chapter isliye padha rahi hoon taaki aap samjho, na ki isliye ki aap kal se gamma scalp karo. Samajhna aur karna alag faisle hain.

The honest answer: usually not. It needs frequent adjustment, and at retail costs the maths doesn't hold. Institutional desks pay far less than you do.

I'm teaching this chapter so you understand it, not so you start gamma scalping tomorrow. Understanding and doing are separate decisions.

3

Skew — market ka dar ka nakshaSkew — a map of the market's fear

Rahul Sir

Ek aur cheez jo option chain pe likhi hoti hai par kam log padhte hain: skew.

Agar aap alag-alag strike ka IV dekho, toh woh ek seedhi line nahi hoti. Aam taur pe neeche ke put strikes ka IV upar ke call strikes se zyada hota hai.

Iska matlab seedha hai: market girne se zyada darta hai, badhne se kam. Aur woh dar premium mein likha hua hai — roz, har chain pe.

Skew ka badalna aksar mood ka badalna hota hai. Par yeh ek reference hai, signal nahi — wahi baat jo humne PCR aur max pain ke liye kahi thi.

One more thing written on the option chain that few people read: skew.

If you look at IV across strikes it isn't a flat line. Typically the IV on downside puts sits above the IV on upside calls.

The meaning is direct: the market fears falls more than rises. And that fear is written into the premium — daily, on every chain.

A change in skew is often a change in mood. But it is a reference, not a signal — the same thing we said about PCR and max pain.

2

3

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this

  • Option chain kholte waqt. Ab aap skew bhi dekhoge — market ka mood wahan likha hota hai.
  • Before selling an option. You'll check IV rank, then ask why IV is high. Is there an event?
  • When someone says “IV is high, sell”. You'll ask: high against what? And high why?
  • Looking at any adjustment-heavy strategy. Count the adjustments, multiply by cost, then look at expectancy.
  • Opening an option chain. You'll now also read the skew — the market's mood is written there.

Factor Aur PortfolioFactors and Portfolios

Value, momentum, quality, low-vol — aur unka decay. Phir portfolio, asli rupaye ki limit mein.

Value, momentum, quality, low-vol — and their decay. Then portfolios, under a real rupee constraint.

M44–45M44–45~45 min~45 min
1

Factor kya haiWhat a factor is

Rahul Sir

Factor ek aisi khoobi hai jo bahut saare stocks mein milti hai aur jiska return se ek lamba rishta dekha gaya hai.

Chaar sabse zyada padhe gaye: value (sasta), momentum (jo chal raha hai), quality (achha business), low volatility (kam hilne wala).

Ab do imaandaar baatein. Ek — yeh saare research se aaye hain, aur zyadatar research US data pe hua hai. India mein inka behaviour alag ho sakta hai.

Do — jo factor mashhoor ho jaata hai, uska faayda ghat-ta hai. Kyunki jab sab ek hi cheez kharidne lagte hain, toh woh sasta rehta hi nahi.

A factor is a characteristic shared by many stocks that has shown a long relationship with returns.

The four most studied: value (cheap), momentum (what's already running), quality (good businesses), low volatility (steady names).

Now two honest points. One — these come from research, and most of that research used US data. Their behaviour in India can differ.

Two — a factor's edge decays once it becomes famous. Because when everyone buys the same thing, it stops being cheap.

FactorKya dhoondhta haiKab bura chalta haiDhyaan dene laayak
ValueSasta bhaav vs businessLambe bull run meinSasta hone ki wajah — kabhi-kabhi woh wajah sahi hoti hai
MomentumJo pehle se chal raha haiAchanak mud jaane parTurnover bahut zyada — cost kha jaata hai
QualityAchha ROE, kam debt, sthir profitJab sasta kachra chalta haiAksar mehenga milta hai
Low volatilityKam hilne wale stocksTez rally mein peeche reh jaata haiBore lagta hai — isiliye log chhod dete hain
FactorWhat it looks forWhen it does badlyWorth watching for
ValueA cheap price against the businessIn a long bull runWhy it's cheap — sometimes the reason is right
MomentumWhat is already runningAt sharp reversalsVery high turnover — costs eat it
QualityGood ROE, low debt, stable profitWhen junk ralliesIt's usually already expensive
Low volatilityNames that move lessIt lags in a fast rallyIt's boring — so people abandon it

Chauthe column ki har line ek hi baat keh rahi hai: har factor ka apna bura daur hota hai, aur woh daur saalon tak chal sakta hai. Jo aadmi us daur mein factor chhod deta hai, use factor ka faayda kabhi nahi milta.Every line in the last column says one thing: every factor has its bad stretch, and that stretch can run for years. Whoever abandons a factor during it never receives the factor's benefit.

2

Turnover — factor ka chhupa hua billTurnover — a factor's hidden bill

Vridhi

Factor research aksar cost ke bina likhi jaati hai. Aur momentum jaisi strategy mein turnover bahut zyada hota hai — har rebalance pe portfolio ka bada hissa badalta hai.

Ab Chapter 4 yaad karo. Har badla hua position ek round trip hai. Jo factor kaagaz pe 4% extra kamaata hai, woh 3% turnover cost ke baad 1% reh sakta hai.

Isiliye mera rule hai: factor strategy ka pehla test return nahi hota. Pehla test turnover hota hai. Agar turnover bahut zyada hai, toh return dekhne ka koi matlab hi nahi.

Factor research is often written without costs. And a strategy like momentum turns over heavily — a large share of the portfolio changes at every rebalance.

Now recall Chapter 4. Every position changed is a round trip. A factor earning 4% extra on paper can be left with 1% after 3% of turnover cost.

So my rule is: the first test of a factor strategy isn't its return. It's turnover. If turnover is too high, the return is irrelevant.

3

Portfolio — jahan asli capital ghusta haiPortfolios — where real capital shows up

Rahul Sir

Ab portfolio construction. Kitaabein teen tareeke batati hain: equal weight (sabko barabar), risk parity (sabka risk barabar), aur correlation clustering (ek jaise stocks ko ek group maano).

Teeno kaam ke hain. Aur teeno ek hi cheez maan ke chalte hain jo aapke paas hai nahi: infinite divisible capital.

Asli duniya mein aapke paas ₹3 lakh hain aur 15 stocks chahiye. Har stock pe ₹20,000. Agar ek stock ka bhaav ₹3,800 hai, toh aap 5 share le sakte ho — ₹19,000. Aapka “equal weight” kabhi equal nahi hoga.

Now portfolio construction. Textbooks give three approaches: equal weight (same amount each), risk parity (same risk each), and correlation clustering (treat similar names as one group).

All three are useful. And all three assume something you don't have: infinitely divisible capital.

In the real world you have ₹3 lakh and want 15 names. That's ₹20,000 each. If one trades at ₹3,800 you can buy 5 shares — ₹19,000. Your “equal weight” is never equal.

Arth

Toh chhote portfolio mein kya karna chahiye?

So what should a small portfolio do?

Vridhi

Kam naam rakho. Correlation clustering yahan sabse zyada kaam ka hai — kyunki 15 stocks jo ek hi sector ke hain, woh 15 positions nahi, ek position hai.

Chhote portfolio mein diversification ka bhram sabse khatarnaak cheez hai. 20 naam rakhne se aap diversified nahi ho jaate agar woh 20 ek hi cheez pe daanv hain.

Hold fewer names. Correlation clustering matters most here — because 15 stocks from one sector aren't 15 positions, they're one.

In a small portfolio the illusion of diversification is the dangerous thing. Holding 20 names doesn't diversify you if all 20 are one bet.

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Factor ek khoobi hai jiska return se lamba rishta dekha gaya hai. Chaar mukhya: value, momentum, quality, low-vol.

A factor is a characteristic with a long observed link to returns. Four main ones: value, momentum, quality, low-vol.

2

Mashhoor hota hi factor ka faayda ghat-ta hai. Jab sab ek hi cheez kharidte hain, woh sasti rehti hi nahi.

A factor's edge decays as it becomes famous. When everyone buys the same thing, it stops being cheap.

3

Har factor ka bura daur saalon tak chal sakta hai. Jo us daur mein chhod deta hai, use faayda milta hi nahi.

Every factor's bad stretch can run for years. Whoever quits during it never gets the benefit.

4

Factor ka pehla test return nahi, turnover hai. 4% ka edge 3% cost ke baad 1% reh jaata hai.

A factor's first test is turnover, not return. A 4% edge can be 1% after 3% in costs.

5

15 stocks jo ek hi sector ke hain, woh ek position hain. Chhote portfolio mein diversification ka bhram sabse khatarnaak hai.

Fifteen names from one sector are one position. In a small portfolio the illusion of diversification is the danger.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Koi bhi factor strategy dekhte waqt. Pehle turnover poochoge, phir return. Ulta nahi.
  • Jab aapka factor 18 mahine se pichhad raha ho. Aapko pata hoga ki yeh normal hai — aur chhodne ka sabse bura waqt yahi hai.
  • Portfolio banate waqt. Naam nahi, cluster ginoge. Aur risk cluster ko doge.
  • Jab market ek saath gire. Aapko pata hoga ki correlation badh gayi — aur aapka diversification aaj kaam nahi kar raha.
  • Looking at any factor strategy. You'll ask about turnover first, return second. Not the reverse.
  • When your factor has lagged for 18 months. You'll know that's normal — and the worst possible moment to quit.
  • Building a portfolio. You'll count clusters, not names. And give risk to clusters.
  • When everything falls at once. You'll know correlations rose — and that your diversification isn't working today.

Machine Seekh Sakti Hai?Can a Machine Learn This?

Indian OHLCV aur OI se features, regression aur classification, aur woh leakage traps jo har result ko sundar bana dete hain. Plus imaandaari se: zyadatar ML trading fail kyun hoti hai. Aur alpha research ka log — jo failures ko utni hi imaandaari se likhta hai jitni wins ko.

Features from Indian OHLCV and OI data, regression and classification, and the leakage traps that flatter every result. Plus an honest look at why most ML trading fails. And the research log that records failures as carefully as wins.

Machine Seekh Sakti Hai?Can a Machine Learn This?

Features, regression, classification, leakage traps. Aur imaandaari se: ML trading fail kyun hoti hai.

Features, regression, classification, leakage traps. And honestly: why most ML trading fails.

M46–47M46–47~45 min~45 min
1

Machine kya seekh sakti haiWhat a machine can actually learn

Arth

Sir, agar machine patterns dhoondh sakti hai toh woh market ke patterns kyun nahi dhoondh legi?

Sir, if machines can find patterns, why can't they find market patterns?

Rahul Sir

Woh dhoondh legi. Bahut saare. Aur wahi poori dikkat hai.

Machine learning ek cheez bahut achhi tarah karta hai: jo data usne dekha, usme pattern dhoondhna. Uska maqsad yahi hai.

Par market ka data shor se bhara hua hai. Aur shor mein bhi pattern hota hai — woh bas aage nahi chalta. Machine ko shor aur signal ka farak khud se pata nahi chalta.

Toh sawaal yeh nahi ki machine pattern dhoondh sakti hai. Sawaal yeh hai ki aap us pattern ko shor se alag kar sakte ho ya nahi. Aur woh kaam aapka hai, machine ka nahi.

It will. Lots of them. And that is the entire problem.

Machine learning does one thing extremely well: find patterns in the data it has seen. That is its purpose.

But market data is mostly noise. And noise contains patterns too — they just don't continue. A machine cannot tell noise from signal on its own.

So the question isn't whether a machine finds patterns. It's whether you can separate them from noise. And that job is yours, not the machine's.

Chaar leakage traps — har ek result ko sundar bana deta haiFour leakage traps — each flatters the result

Look-ahead leakage — feature mein aisa data ghus gaya jo us waqt available hi nahi tha. Sabse aam: quarterly numbers ko us tareekh se use karna jab woh publish hue hi nahi the.

Target leakage — feature mein woh jaankari chhup gayi jo aap predict karne nikle the. Aksar galti se banaye gaye ratios ke through.

Scaling leakage — poore data pe normalisation karna, phir train-test split. Aapne test data ka average train mein daal diya.

Random split — time series ko random tarike se baantna. Aapne model ko kal dikha ke aaj ke bare mein poocha. Time series hamesha time ke hisaab se banti hai.

Look-ahead leakage — a feature carries data that wasn't available at the time. Most common: using quarterly numbers from before they were published.

Target leakage — a feature secretly encodes what you're trying to predict, often through a carelessly built ratio.

Scaling leakage — normalising across all the data and splitting afterwards. You've put the test set's mean into training.

A random split — splitting a time series randomly. You showed the model tomorrow and asked about today. Time series always split by time.

2

Feature banana — asli kaam yahi haiBuilding features — where the real work is

Vridhi

Model chunna sabse aasaan hissa hai. Asli kaam features banane mein hai — yani machine ko kya dikhana hai.

Indian data se kaam ke features: return ke alag-alag window, realised volatility, volume ka ratio, delivery percentage, OI ka change, India VIX, aur index ke saapeksh relative strength.

Par ek shart: har feature ke peeche ek kaaran hona chahiye. 200 features daal dena aur model ko chunne dena — woh Chapter 19 wala parameter mining hai, bas naye kapde mein.

Choosing a model is the easy part. The real work is in features — deciding what to show the machine.

Useful features from Indian data: returns over several windows, realised volatility, volume ratios, delivery percentage, change in OI, India VIX, and relative strength against the index.

One condition: every feature must have a reason. Throwing in 200 and letting the model choose is Chapter 19's parameter mining in new clothes.

Arth

Aur target kya rakhna chahiye?

And what should the target be?

Vridhi

Yeh sabse zyada galat hone wala faisla hai. “Kal ka return” ek bura target hai — woh lagbhag poora shor hai.

Behtar target aksar classification hota hai: kya agle N din mein move X se bada hoga? Ya kya stop se pehle target lagega? Yeh sawaal trading ke sawaal hain — aur inka jawab kaam ka hota hai.

That's the most commonly mis-made decision. “Tomorrow's return” is a bad target — it is almost entirely noise.

A better target is usually classification: will the move over the next N days exceed X? Or will the target be hit before the stop? Those are trading questions — and their answers are usable.

3

Research log — failures bhi likhoThe research log — write the failures too

Rahul Sir

Aakhri cheez, aur yeh Level 4 ki sabse keemti aadat hai: research log.

Har hypothesis ke liye ek entry: kya soch thi, kaise test kiya, kya nateeja aaya, aur aage kya kiya. Aur failures utni hi imaandaari se likhna jitni wins ko.

Kyun? Do wajah. Ek — aap wahi failed idea do saal baad dobara test karoge, agar likha nahi hai. Do — jo aadmi apne 40 failures gin sakta hai, woh 41ve idea pe zyada imaandaar hota hai.

Aur ek chhupa hua faayda: agar aapke log mein 40 test hain aur unme se ek chala, toh aapko pata hai ki woh ek shayad luck tha. Yeh sawaal koi report nahi poochta.

One last thing, and it is Level 4's most valuable habit: the research log.

One entry per hypothesis: what the idea was, how you tested it, what came out, and what you did next. And failures recorded as carefully as wins.

Why? Two reasons. One — you will retest the same failed idea in two years if it isn't written down. Two — someone who can count 40 failures is more honest about the 41st idea.

And a hidden benefit: if the log holds 40 tests and one worked, you know that one may have been luck. No report ever asks you that.

  • When a model looks too good. Your first suspicion will be leakage, not talent.
  • After every piece of research. An entry in the log — even when the idea failed. Especially then.

Algo Ka DhaanchaAnatomy of an Algo

Chhe-parat ka pipeline, broker-agnostic. Aur SEBI ka retail algo framework — jo ab live hai.

The six-layer pipeline, broker-agnostic. And SEBI's retail algo framework — now live.

M48–49M48–49~45 min~45 min
1

Algo ek program nahi haiAn algo is not a program

Rahul Sir

Log sochte hain algo ek script hai jo order lagata hai. Woh nahi hai. Algo ek pipeline hai jiski chhe parat hain — aur order lagana unme se sirf ek hai.

Aur is course mein hum ise broker-agnostic padhate hain. Kyunki broker badal jaate hain, API badal jaati hain, par yeh chhe parat wahi rehti hain.

People think an algo is a script that places orders. It isn't. An algo is a pipeline with six layers — and placing orders is only one of them.

And we teach it broker-agnostically. Because brokers change and APIs change, but these six layers don't.

2

Ab kaanoon — aur yeh live haiNow the law — and it is live

Vridhi

Ab woh hissa jo 2025 tak ‘aane wala hai’ kaha jaata tha. Woh aa chuka hai.

SEBI ne 4 February 2025 ko circular nikaala tha — “Safer participation of retail investors in algorithmic trading”. Deadline 30 September 2025 ko badhaayi gayi. Aur 1 April 2026 se compliance mandatory hai. NSE ne ise exchange level pe apne circular se lagu kiya.

Aaj ki tareekh mein yeh “aane wala rule” nahi hai. Yeh chal raha kaanoon hai. Agar aapne kahin purana course material padha hai jisme yeh ‘upcoming’ likha hai, toh woh material purana hai.

Now the part that until 2025 was described as ‘coming’. It has arrived.

SEBI issued the circular on 4 February 2025 — “Safer participation of retail investors in algorithmic trading”. The deadline was extended on 30 September 2025. And compliance has been mandatory since 1 April 2026. NSE operationalised it at the exchange level through its own circular.

As of today this is not an upcoming rule. It is operating law. If you've read older course material calling it ‘upcoming’, that material is out of date.

RuleKya maangta haiAapke liye practical matlab

Do cheezein jo is course mein verify nahi ki ja sakiTwo things this course could not verify

Ek — server India mein hona chahiye? Kuch current summaries kehte hain ki retail algo Indian servers pe host hone chahiye. Yeh baat generic “koi bhi cloud VPS chalega” wali salaah se seedha takraati hai. Hum ise is course mein fact ki tarah nahi keh rahe — apne broker ki current implementation circular se khud verify karo, aur usi ke hisaab se hosting chuno.

Do — kya API se market order band hai? Ek dawa chalti hai ki API se sirf limit order bhej sakte ho. Structured aur traceable orders ke emphasis ko dekhte hue yeh sambhav lagta hai, par hum ise confirm nahi kar paaye. Ise sach maan ke code mat likho — broker se poocho.

Yeh do cheezein yahan is liye likhi hain kyunki jo verify nahi hua use verify hua nahi batana chahiye. Yeh course ka rule hai, aur aapke algo ka bhi hona chahiye.

One — must the server be in India? Some current summaries say retail algos must be hosted on Indian servers. That conflicts directly with generic “any cloud VPS is fine” advice. This course does not state it as fact — verify it against your broker's current implementation circular and choose hosting accordingly.

Two — are market orders barred via API? There is a claim that only limit orders may be sent through an API. Given the emphasis on structured, traceable orders it is plausible, but we could not confirm it. Don't write code assuming it — ask your broker.

These two are written here because what hasn't been verified must not be presented as verified. That is this course's rule, and it should be your algo's rule too.

3

Level 2 ka matlab badal gaya haiWhat Level 2 now means

Rahul Sir

Chapter 5 mein humne kaha tha ki Level 2 ek regulatory danda hai, sirf technical nahi. Ab aapko dikh gaya ki kyun.

Level 2 pe jaane ka matlab hai: static IP register karwana, Algo-ID lena, 2FA aur daily logout handle karna, aur broker ki implementation note ke hisaab se apna code likhna.

Aur ek line jo poore course mein sabse zaroori hai: apna algo chalana ek cheez hai; kisi aur ko algo dena ya bechna bilkul doosri cheez hai. Woh doosri cheez ek alag regulatory duniya hai, aur usme black-box clause bhi lagta hai.

In Chapter 5 we said Level 2 is a regulatory rung, not just a technical one. Now you can see why.

Moving to Level 2 means registering a static IP, obtaining an Algo-ID, handling 2FA and daily logout, and writing your code to your broker's implementation note.

And a line that matters most in this whole course: running your own algo is one thing; giving or selling one to someone else is entirely another. That second thing is a different regulatory world, and the black-box clause applies there.

Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 4 Expert · Chapter 26Market 1 · Stock Market · Level 4 Expert · Chapter 26

Live JaanaGoing Live

Paper se ek lot, phir scale. Heartbeat, reconciliation, kill-switch. Aur apna research stack.

Paper to one lot, then scale. Heartbeats, reconciliation, the kill-switch. And your own research stack.

M50–51M50–51~40 min~40 min
1

Live jaane ka kramThe order of going live

Vridhi

Live jaana ek switch nahi hai. Woh chaar kadam hain, aur har kadam ka apna imtihan hai.

Ek — paper, jab tak system bina crash ke chalta na rahe. Do — ek lot, sabse chhota size, kam se kam ek mahina. Teen — dheere scale, aur sirf tab jab reconciliation saaf ho. Chaar — poora size.

Kadam 2 mein aap paisa kamane nahi ja rahe. Aap yeh dekhne ja rahe ho ki aapka system asli duniya se takra ke tootta kahan hai.

Aur woh zaroor tootega. Order reject hoga. Internet jaayega. Broker ki API maintenance pe jaayegi. Data feed ek candle chhod degi. Yeh sab hota hai — sirf paper trading mein nahi hota.

Going live isn't a switch. It is four steps, and each has its own test.

One — paper, until the system runs without crashing. Two — one lot, smallest size, for at least a month. Three — scale slowly, and only when reconciliation is clean. Four — full size.

Step 2 isn't about making money. It's about finding where your system breaks when it meets the real world.

And it will break. An order gets rejected. The internet drops. The broker's API goes into maintenance. The data feed skips a candle. All of this happens — just never in paper trading.

“Retry” har error ka jawab nahi hai“Retry” is not the answer to every error

Network timeout? Retry theek hai. Par order rejected: insufficient margin pe retry karna sirf bar-bar wahi reject laayega. Aur order status unknown pe retry karna sabse khatarnaak hai — kyunki pehla order shayad lag chuka ho, aur aap doosra bhej doge.

Isiliye har error ka jawab pehle se likha hona chahiye, teen shreniyon mein: retry karo, rok do aur batao, ya sab band karo. Jo error is list mein nahi hai, uska default jawab hamesha sab band karo hona chahiye — retry nahi.

A network timeout? Retry is fine. But retrying on order rejected: insufficient margin just repeats the rejection. And retrying on order status unknown is the most dangerous of all — the first order may have gone through, and you're about to send a second.

So every error needs a pre-written response in one of three categories: retry, halt and alert, or shut everything. Any error not on the list defaults to shut everything — never to retry.

2

Research stack — bina paid data keA research stack — without paid data

Rahul Sir

Aakhri practical cheez. Log sochte hain research ke liye mehenga data chahiye. Indian market ke liye yeh bilkul sach nahi hai.

Exchange khud bahut kuch free deta hai: daily bhavcopy, delivery data, FII-DII figures, ASM/GSM lists, index constituents aur weights, corporate actions, shareholding patterns.

Aur aapke broker ki API historical data deti hai. Zyadatar retail research ke liye yeh kaafi hai. Jo cheez kam milti hai woh data nahi — woh discipline hai us data ko roz save karne ki.

One last practical thing. People assume research needs expensive data. For the Indian market that simply isn't true.

The exchanges publish a great deal free: the daily bhavcopy, delivery data, FII-DII figures, ASM/GSM lists, index constituents and weights, corporate actions, shareholding patterns.

And your broker's API gives historical data. For most retail research that is enough. The scarce thing isn't data — it's the discipline to save it every day.

Arth

Roz save karna kyun zaroori hai?

Why does saving it daily matter?

Rahul Sir

Kyunki aaj ka data aaj free hai. Do saal purana data aksar nahi milta, ya paise lagte hain. Jo aadmi aaj se roz bhavcopy save karta hai, uske paas do saal baad woh cheez hogi jo doosron ko kharidni padti hai.

Aur ek aur cheez: versioning aur reproducibility. Agar aap apna backtest chhe mahine baad dobara nahi chala sakte aur wahi result nahi nikaal sakte, toh woh backtest ek yaad hai, ek nateeja nahi.

Because today's data is free today. Two-year-old data often isn't available, or costs money. Whoever saves the bhavcopy daily from today will, in two years, own something others have to buy.

And one more: versioning and reproducibility. If you can't rerun your backtest in six months and get the same result, that backtest is a memory, not a finding.

Chapter 26 · band karne se pehleChapter 26 · before you close this

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Live jaana chaar kadam hai: paper → ek lot → dheere scale → poora size. Har kadam ka apna imtihan.

Going live is four steps: paper → one lot → slow scale → full size. Each with its own test.

2

Ek-lot wale kadam ka maqsad paisa nahi hai. Woh yeh dhoondhna hai ki system asli duniya se takra ke tootta kahan hai.

The one-lot step isn't about money. It's about finding where the system breaks against the real world.

3

Position reconciliation sabse zaroori hai. Galat position maan lene se har risk calculation galat ho jaata hai.

Position reconciliation matters most. An assumed position that's wrong makes every risk calculation wrong.

4

“Retry” har error ka jawab nahi. Anjaan error ka default jawab hamesha “sab band karo” hona chahiye.

“Retry” isn't the answer to every error. An unknown error defaults to “shut everything”.

5

Indian market ka research free data pe ho sakta hai. Kami data ki nahi — roz save karne ki discipline ki hai.

Indian market research runs on free data. The scarcity isn't data — it's the discipline to save it daily.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Pehla live din. Sabse chhota size, aur poora dhyaan system pe — P&L pe nahi.
  • Har shaam. Order aur position dono reconcile karoge. Farak mila toh agle din trading band.
  • Jab naya error dikhe. Aap use apni error list mein daaloge — aur tab tak default “band karo” hi rahega.
  • Aaj se roz. Bhavcopy save karoge. Do saal baad woh aapki sabse keemti cheez hogi.
  • The first live day. Smallest size, and all your attention on the system — not the P&L.
  • Every evening. You'll reconcile orders and positions. A mismatch means no trading tomorrow.
  • When a new error appears. You'll add it to your error list — and until then the default stays “shut down”.
  • From today, daily. You'll save the bhavcopy. In two years it will be your most valuable asset.

Aakhri kaamThe last piece of work

Rahul Sir

Arth, Market 1 yahan khatam hota hai. 52 modules, 27 chapters. Aur aakhri kaam koi naya concept nahi hai.

Aakhri kaam yeh hai: ek strategy, poori tarah likhi hui. Sab kuch jo aapne seekha, ek document mein. Aur woh document kisi aur ke liye padhne laayak hona chahiye.

Yeh sirf ek exercise nahi hai. Yeh aapka portfolio piece hai. Agar kal koi poochhe ki aap trading kaise karte ho, toh aap ek document dikha doge — ek kahani nahi sunaoge.

Arth, Market 1 ends here. Fifty-two modules, twenty-seven chapters. And the last piece of work is not a new concept.

The last piece of work is this: one strategy, written out completely. Everything you've learned, in one document. And it must be readable by someone else.

This isn't just an exercise. It is your portfolio piece. If someone asks tomorrow how you trade, you hand over a document — you don't tell a story.

Aage kya — do aur marketsWhat comes next — two more markets

Market 2 — Rupaya. Exchange-traded currency derivatives: USDINR aur uske bhai-band, NSE/BSE pe, RBI aur SEBI ke under. Amaan ke saath, jo rupee pe bet nahi karta — woh apni invoice bachata hai. Aur us market ka doosra module hi yeh saaf karta hai ki legal kya hai aur kya nahi.

Market 3 — Digital Duniya. Virtual Digital Assets jaise woh India mein asal mein hain. Yeh market optional hai, SEBI RA scope ke bahar alag education ke roop mein aati hai, aur kisi bhi asset ki koi recommendation nahi karti. Mudra ke saath, jo hisaab pehle karti hai aur hype baad mein sunti hai.

Market 2 — The Rupee. Exchange-traded currency derivatives: USDINR and its cousins on NSE/BSE, under RBI and SEBI. Told with Amaan, who doesn't bet on the rupee — he protects his invoice. Its second module is the one that makes clear what is legal and what isn't.

Market 3 — Digital Assets. Virtual Digital Assets as they actually exist in India. This market is optional, sits outside SEBI RA scope as separate education, and recommends no asset. Told with Mudra, who does the arithmetic first and listens to the hype afterwards.

Aaj kya seekhaWhat you learned

Agar yeh lines yaad reh gayi, toh chapter kaam kar gaya.

If these lines stick, the chapter did its job.

1

Capstone aath hisson ka document hai — thesis, rules, cost model, backtest, out-of-sample, risk limits, compliance, runbook.

The capstone is an eight-section document — thesis, rules, cost model, backtest, out-of-sample, risk limits, compliance, runbook.

2

Hissa 5 (out-of-sample) hi imaandaar dil hai. Bura result bhi likhna hai — khaas kar tab.

Section 5 (out-of-sample) is the honest heart. A poor result gets written too — especially then.

3

Yeh document kisi aur ke padhne laayak hona chahiye. Jo sirf aap samajh sako, woh document nahi — woh yaaddasht hai.

The document must be readable by someone else. One only you understand isn't a document — it's a memory.

4

Aapke paas ab sawaal hain. Yeh cheez bahut logon ke paas dus saal baad bhi nahi hoti.

You now have the questions. Many people don't have those after ten years.

5

Market 1 poora hua. Market 2 rupaye pe hai; Market 3 optional hai aur SEBI RA scope ke bahar.

Market 1 is complete. Market 2 is the rupee; Market 3 is optional and outside SEBI RA scope.

Yeh kaam kahan aayega — practicallyWhere you'll actually use this
  • Jab koi poochhe ki aap kaise trade karte ho. Aap document doge, kahani nahi sunaoge.
  • Jab koi nayi strategy mile. Aap usko in aath hisson ke saanche mein daaloge. Jo hissa khaali reh jaaye, wahi uski kamzori hai.
  • Chheh mahine baad. Aap apna capstone dobara padhoge aur usme galtiyan dikhengi. Wahi seekhne ka saboot hai.
  • Poori zindagi. Har nayi strategy ka apna capstone hoga — yeh ek format hai, ek exercise nahi.
  • When someone asks how you trade. You'll hand over a document, not tell a story.
  • When you meet a new strategy. You'll pour it into these eight sections. Whichever stays empty is its weakness.
  • Six months from now. You'll reread your capstone and see errors in it. That is the proof of learning.
  • For the rest of it. Every new strategy gets its own capstone — this is a format, not an exercise.
